News.title: China’s chip breakthrough triggers global tech rout
News.content:
China has achieved a breakthrough in developing technology crucial to the AI boom, overcoming US efforts to limit Beijing’s access to the systems.

China’s chip giant Shanghai Yuliangsheng has started production of deep ultraviolet lithography machines, according to The Information, a tech publication.

These machines, which can reach the size of a double-decker bus, use high-powered lasers to imprint designs on to silicon wafers, which are used to make chips.

Until recently, only Western companies and allies of the US had the capability to produce these machines.

The most advanced versions of the technology have largely been the preserve of companies such as Dutch giant ASML and Japan’s Nikon.

These machines have been cut off from China by US export controls, preventing their production of advanced chips as Washington seeks to slow the development of AI in the country.

Semiconductor stocks plunged on the report. Trading was briefly halted on South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index after it suffered a collapse of nearly 11pc overnight, following a bleak day on Wall Street.

Advanced semiconductors, such as those used in AI chips, rely on minuscule circuits, invisible to the naked eye. They can only be manufactured by directing tiny lasers onto microchip wafers, a process known as ultraviolet lithography.

News.title: Ramsay-Peaty ‘human first, athlete second’ as he settles for second bronze
News.content:
So a pair of bronze medals for the man who once only dealt in gold. Not that Adam Ramsay-Peaty thinks that is necessarily such a bad trade when he also computes the wider price of sporting domination.

“I’ve been that person who wins all the time, and it costs you pretty much everything, and I won’t say it’s worth it,” Ramsay-Peaty said after his return to international competition continued in his now favoured 50m breaststroke with a second podium place at these Commonwealth Games. “That period of time, where I was undefeated for eight years, it was athlete first, then human,” he added. “Now it’s human first, then athlete, which is a very fair price to pay.”

Aged 31, and with a baby girl on the way with wife Holly Ramsay, Ramsay-Peaty’s order of priorities might be understandable, but it was still another performance to raise questions over whether he can again climb to the top of a major podium.

Swimming is not kind to the over-30s – Michael Phelps was the first man in 2016 to win an Olympic gold in the pool even at the age Ramsay-Peaty is now – and we still have another two years until the Los Angeles Olympics. It would be the greatest achievement even of the Englishman’s extraordinary career to win his third individual Olympic title.

He trailed from the start here and was almost exactly a second outside his world record – set almost a decade ago – as Australia’s Sam Williamson completed a breaststroke double ahead of South Africa’s Michael Houlie in second. “As you get older, it gets harder,” said Ramsay-Peaty, before adding a crucial caveat, “but I’m enjoying it more…in my head, I’m getting fresher.”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino breaks silence on plan to sell World Cup – but shameless Fifa REFUSE to take questions from media
Sports.content:
GIANNI INFANTINO has broken his silence after his controversial plans to sell the World Cup threatened to plunge global football into civil war.

The Fifa president’s sensational plan to sell off parts of the World Cup to the highest bidder was revealed on Tuesday and was met with fierce backlash from the sports stakeholders.



And despite the threats of a boycott from Uefa and major footballing nations, Infantino has doubled-down on his stance – which it is claimed would create a £20billion subsidiary to run the World Cup and other Fifa competitions by offering stakes of up to 20 per cent to external investors.

Infantino, 56, provided an update in a video shared by Fifa on Wednesday, rather than taking questions from the media.



He said: “It’s part of a democratic process, a consultation process and, above all, it is an opportunity but not an obligation, and, as I said, it kicks off the consultation process.”

The Swiss insisted that Fifa’s 211 members would have the final say on the plan.

Critics blasted Fifa for trying to “enrich themselves and their friends”, as football‘s regional bodies including The FA said they had been blindsided by the move.

Even some of Fifa’s eight vice-presidents were left in the dark over the plan, which could raise as much as £7.5bn according to Infantino.

He continued: “FIFA obviously continues to govern football without any external interference.

“And the flagship tournament it organises, like the FIFA World Cup or the FIFA Women’s World Cup, will always remain.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

In a five-page letter to members outlining the merits of the proposal, Infantino said positive responses before the 19 September deadline would see £15m made available as soon as January.

He has insisted the proposal to set up what will be known as Fifa Forward Enterprise will unlock new commercial opportunities and give rise to the next Cape Verdes, one of four nations to make their debuts at the 2026 World Cup following its expansion to 48 teams.

One of the proposed investors has already been identified as Thrive Eternal, conveniently a fund run by Joshua Kushner, the brother of Donald Trump‘s son-in-law, Jared Kushner, following Infantino’s smothering of the US President before and during the World Cup.

Uefa said the deadline being just 53 days away “says everything you need to know about this plan”.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino’s £7.5billion cash grab leaves football on brink of civil war 60 years on from England’s greatest day
Sports.content:
THE World Cup used to be so simple — and today serves as the perfect reminder of that.

It was exactly 60 years ago that Bobby Moore was lifting the Jules Rimet trophy and being hoisted on the shoulders of his England team-mates.



Those iconic scenes at Wembley came after a tournament that had just 16 teams and lasted only 20 days.

There were no hydration breaks or half-time shows and certainly no private investors looking for a slice of the pie.



The biggest worry was the trophy being stolen — and even that had an innocent ending, thanks to Pickles the dog finding it.

Sadly there is no Pickles this time to save the messy situation, which is rapidly becoming a dog’s dinner.

Football is on the brink of civil war after Gianni Infantino revealed on Tuesday his radical plans to flog off parts of the World Cup.

It essentially involves the creation of a new company, Fifa Forward Enterprise, that would allow them to sell stakes in their commercial and event operations.

Fifa stress those shareholdings would be “minority” and “non-controlling” investments — yet could still raise US$10billion (£7.52bn).

Uefa have warned it “crosses a line” and are expected to hold an emergency meeting on the matter.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Others — such as Asia’s governing body, the AFC — revealed they were “not consulted on the proposal” and were blindsided by Infantino.

The same applies to Concacaf, who represent Central and North America and are “deeply concerned by the lack of due process” that has taken place.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has waded into the debate and the outcry on social media is so great that some are pining for the days of Sepp Blatter.

Imagine saying that when Infantino’s predecessor announced in 2015 that he was finally ending his 17-year reign of corruption as Fifa president?

The nuclear option of some countries boycotting the World Cup has been floated, namely by those at Uefa.



That was their solution back in 2021, when Fifa proposed hosting the World Cup every two years.

It is the obvious move to play as Fifa know the tournament simply does not work without the European heavyweights, especially if you are inviting 64 teams to the party, as is Fifa’s proposal.

At this summer’s 48-team World Cup, six of the eight quarter-finalists were from Europe.

The winners, Spain, were too — and that was also the case in 2018 when France got their hands on the trophy.

Infantino’s big plan to sell stakes in the World Cup is around the commercial money that can be made.



But that is simply a non-starter if the Uefa teams refuse to be a part of this wild new landscape.

The fear is, though, that it is harder to predict a united front coming from those that oppose this outlandish scheme.

Cash is king — and there is a lot of it on the table for those that give Infantino’s proposals the green light.

The Fifa president has written to all 211 of the governing body’s member associations, who will vote on the matter.

In the letter, Infantino outlined the extra £30million they could receive by giving the thumbs-up to his plans.



Part of that comes in the shape of a £15m lump sum, which member associations would have access to.

The idea would be that it is spent on things like stadiums and training centres, with the money’s use audited.

Countries would then get access to a further £15m over the following three years through their member association funding.

The upcoming cycle from 2027-30 was budgeted at £6m per member association — but Fifa say that would rise to £15m if Infantino’s proposals are voted through.

Clearly, some countries would welcome a cash boost like that and there has been praise for the plans as well as opposition.



The Czech Republic FA’s president, David Trunda, has given them his backing and will not be alone.

And then there is the elephant in the room — Russia.

Infantino revealed earlier this year that Fifa would look into reintegrating them into international football after they were banned in 2022 following their invasion of Ukraine.

That could lead to further splits between European countries, with Russia having political influence over at least half a dozen Fifa member associations.

Ultimately, it is the vote of those members that will decide if Infantino gets his wish.



The controversial Swiss requires majority support from them and also backing from the Fifa Council, which consists of 37 members.

And whether people like it or not, history has shown us that Infantino usually gets his way.

The fiasco around USA star Folarin Balogun’s suspension reprieve at the World Cup this summer showed that and made a mockery of the game.

There were concerns afterwards about Donald Trump’s influence, as the US President got his way by simply picking up the phone.

The question now is, does anyone have a trump card to stop Infantino?

Sports.title: Chelsea’s Instagram raided by thousands of Kazakhstan fans after ‘trialist’ scores seven minutes into pre-season clash
Sports.content:
CHELSEA’S Instagram has been raided by fans in Kazakhstan praising Dastan Satpayev – with one post of his goal gathering more than one million likes.

The 17-year-old “trialist” scored just seven minutes into Chelsea‘s pre-season clash against Western Sydney Wanderers on Tuesday.



Kazakh football fans have shown their support for Satpayev as the Blues shared footage of his goal against the Wanderers on social media.

Satpayev was found in open space as he cruised past Western Sydney’s defence to score in the top-right corner.



Chelsea’s Instagram post has gained more than 1 million likes and 359,300 comments – although they may not all be from Kazakhstan.

One fan said: “All my friends here😂 OOO Dastan Satpayev👏👏👏 🇰🇿🇰🇿🇰🇿💙💙💙.”

A £3.3 million deal was agreed between Chelsea and Kazakhstan Premier League side Kairat Almaty last year.

Sports.title: Newcastle star close to tears as he’s forced off just 21 minutes into second game back from SIX-MONTH injury lay-off
Sports.content:
INJURY-JINXED Newcastle star Fabian Schar’s return to action after a six-month lay-off ended in agony.

The Swiss centre-half hobbled off early as his comeback turned into a nightmare, with the Toon slumping to an alarming 4-1 pre-season defeat at Bristol City.



A dejected Schar headed straight to the dressing room on 21 minutes for treatment after collapsing in a heap with what looked like a muscle injury on the half-way line.

It was cruel on Schar, 34, who has been battling his way back to fitness after being sidelined with an ankle injury and then a foot infection.



He had been relishing his ninth campaign with the Geordies after signing a new one-year contract extension last month.

And the sight of him trudging off was a blow for Toon boss Eddie Howe whose preparations for the new campaign have gone from bad to worse.

He has already lost the services of Kieran Trippier, Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali with Bruno Guimaraes’ future also looking uncertain amid Arsenal interest.

Howe desperately needs reinforcements before the Prem season starts judging by their abject Ashton Gate show.

For shambolic Newcastle looked utterly leaderless after Schar, who was crocked in a 4-3 win over Leeds at St James Park way back in January, limped off.

Ex-Sunderland forward Sam Greenwood rubbed salt into the wounds six minutes after Schar’s unfortunate exit with a stunning free-kick for the Robins.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

And then City’s new striker Lorent Tolaj brushed Sven Botman aside before beating the Tynesiders’ new French keeper Ewen Jaouen.

Max Bird piled on the agony after half-time when he broke clear before driving past Jaouen as Newcastle’s leaden defence was prised apart.

Toon skipper Harvey Barnes gave the travelling fans something to shout about on 78 minutes with a cool finish.



But things ended on a low for Howe’s men as the below-par Botman sliced Sam Bell’s low cross beyond Jaouen on 81 minutes.

Sports.title: England fans lead calls for 3 Lions to boycott World Cup as fury grows at Fifa plan & emergency UEFA meeting planned
Sports.content:
FANS are calling on England to boycott the World Cup amid fury at Fifa’s plot to sell off the tournament.

If stakes in the event are flogged as planned it would allow Fifa president Gianni Infantino and his US pals to funnel millions from the sport.



Furious fans say the move is all about greed and that Infantino “must be stopped”.

Europe’s governing body Uefa is set to hold emergency talks as its 55-strong bloc considers a tough response, which could lead to a mass boycott.



England’s FA is leading the opposition, saying its leaders are “deeply concerned about the lack of process” in the plot by world football chiefs Fifa to create a private company to run its competitions.

Three Lions fans were fleeced by Infantino’s obscene ticket prices as the team reached the semi-final at this summer’s tournament.



They have urged the FA to call his bluff after he issued an ultimatum to all Fifa member associations.

He has offered a one-off £30million payment to each of the 211 Fifa nations — provided they sign up to his new deal within 53 days.

He intends to create a tournament organisation called Fifa Forward Enterprise and is believed to be planning for the World Cup to be every two years instead of four.

England fan Simon Harris, 67, a retired finance worker from Bridgnorth, Shrops, who followed Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and co in the US, said: “This would be the end of the World Cup.



“Fifa is destroying football by selling the soul of the game for money. Uefa should take its countries out of Fifa and boycott the next World Cup. That’s the only way to make Fifa see sense.

“This is all about Fifa and Infantino making more money.”

American business associates of Infantino’s US President pal Donald Trump are understood to have been secretly consulted about the change.

They include an investment firm called Thrive run by Joshua Kushner, the brother of Mr Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner.



Fan Simon added: “Trump’s family links to the organisation which would run the World Cup just tops it off. Infantino must be stopped.”

Steve Hartshorne, 68, a retired pharmacist from Walsall, West Mids, who has not missed an England game for 14 years, said: “Infantino needs to be removed.

“He thinks he’s untouchable — Uefa need to stand up to him. The FA should set up their own organisation to run football properly.

“Having the World Cup every two years with 64 teams would be absolutely ridiculous. It’s special because it’s every four years.”



Manchester City supporter Mike Andrews, 60, a nursery manager from Newquay, Cornwall, who also followed England in the US, said: “Fifa are taking the World Cup away from fans by allowing a corporate entity to run it to make even more money. It’s all about Fifa’s greed.”

New PM Andy Burnham has also blasted the proposals. Ex-FA and Man City chairman David Bernstein said England must withdraw from the World Cup if Infantino’s proposals go through.

He added: “The whole thing is dreadful. It feels like cronyism, nepotism. It stinks, frankly.”

An FA spokesman said: “We were completely unaware of this proposal and have no substantive details.



Fifa's World Cup sell-off plan Fifa would set up a firm for the “operational delivery of Fifa tournaments” called Fifa Forward Enterprise, which will effectively control the men’s and women’s World Cups and Club World Cup

Fifa would then own the majority share in the company — but investors could purchase 20 to 30 per cent which could amount to billions of dollars

Each of Fifa’s 211 member associations would also be given a stake worth approximately £15m which they could keep or sell

Infantino would then be in line to run the company after he steps down as head of Fifa

One proposed investor is Joshua Kushner — a younger brother of Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner

“Based on the limited information, we are deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance to get to this point.

“When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by Fifa, we will comment further.”

Uefa accused Fifa of using football “to enrich themselves and their friends”.

A Uefa insider told The Sun: “There is a great deal of anger about this plan. The future of the game is at stake.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But the hoped-for show of European unity faltered as Czech Republic FA chief David Trunda said he can see the “positive impact” of the plans proposed by Infantino, 56, from Switzerland.



Fifa’s American bloc Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation have both expressed disappointment that they were not consulted on the plans.

Sports.title: Non-league football club swap pitch for boxing ring as Noel Gallagher’s ex-security guard puts them through their paces
Sports.content:
SOLIHULL MOORS have made a stunning change to their pre-season football routine by swapping the pitch for a boxing ring.

Players for the non-league club ditched their football boots for boxing gloves just over a week before their season in the National League is due to kick off as they visited McCracken’s Boxing Gym.



Owned by Oscar McCracken, the renowned gym located in Tyseley, Birmingham, hosted Chris Millington’s team for a special intensive boxing and conditioning session.

The link up was made possible by MAN Commercial Protection CEO Iain McCallister, who was named Solihull Moors Foundation Chairman in June.



McCallister is a former boxer and entrepreneur whose company has offered protection to stars including Noel Gallagher, Mike Tyson, Tyson Fury, Ricky Hatton and even the King and Queen.

But the latest venture undertaken by MAN saw the fifth-tier stars breaking a sweat in the gym instead of the pitch at Damson Park.



McCallister said of the partnership: “Boxing has always been a passion of mine, so being able to connect Solihull Moors FC with McCracken’s to create this experience was something I was delighted to make happen.

“The lads embraced every challenge from the first bell to the final round.

“It was brilliant to see them step outside their comfort zone and experience the discipline, resilience and focus that boxing demands.

“Seeing an idea become a reality through collaboration is a great example of how organisations in Solihull and Birmingham can work together.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Crucially Millington, 50, was pleased with the session and said: “I remember mentioning to Iain that I wanted the lads to experience a proper boxing gym and a proper conditioning session during pre-season.

“That was six months ago, and it was fantastic to see it all come together.

“It simply wouldn’t have happened without Iain bringing everyone together.

“Special thanks to Oscar McCracken and everyone at the gym for their commitment to the session.

“It was fantastic, and I can’t speak highly enough of the work Oscar and his team are doing.”



The Moors start their season with an away trip to Harrogate Town on August 8, before a first home game against Boston United the following week.

Sports.title: Love rat footballer Jermain Defoe locks lips with new flame and cheekily fans her chest on cosy lunch date
Sports.content:
FORMER England ace Jermain Defoe was snapped getting intimate with a new woman during a cosy Mayfair lunch date.

The footballer, 43, who had his managerial contract with Woking FC terminated last week after just four months in the role, enjoyed a series of snogs with new partner Nadine Rider – and was caught getting handsy with her at the table.



Jermain dressed for the hot weather in beige chinos and a white t-shirt with a short-sleeved green and white striped shirt over the top, while his female companion matched in a light beige ensemble.

Seated at exclusive restaurant 74 Drake, the shaded pair seemed somewhat distracted at dinner though, as they locked lips several times.



And in one risque moment, the Premier League legend was seen smirking and pulling Nadine’s top open to fan her chest amid their steamy exchange.

Jermain’s new romance comes after his relationship with recruiter Farran Tomlin, 11 years his junior, quietly ended.





The former age gap couple appeared smitten during a break to Turkey last summer at five-star resort Lujo Hotel Bodrum.

The pair posed alongside Turkish singer Dilek Sert Erdogan, who later shared the photo to Instagram captioning it: “The amazing Jermain Defoe and his lovely wife Farran came to see our show.

“Even after I got off stage, they were still there…”

Jermain has a chequered romantic history, with the star caught kissing wedding planner Paige Mallabourn-Edmondson at a hotel in Lancashire back in 2023 – days after appearing on a red carpet with his influencer girlfriend Alisha LeMay.

Jermain previously left his wife Donna Tierney for Alisha after less than a year of marriage.



Sources claim his new flame Nadine is understood to be of a similar age to Jermain and mum to an adult son.

Last week, Jermain and football club Woking ‘mutually agreed’ to part ways, four months after he was given his first managerial role.

In a statement released on social media, Defoe said: “Following recent discussions, I can confirm that I have mutually agreed to leave my position as manager of Woking.

“Unfortunately, circumstances have ultimately made it impossible for me to continue in the position.

“I am extremely proud of the work undertaken during my time at the club and genuinely felt that we were building something special.



“I would like to thank Todd Johnson for giving me the opportunity to manage the club.

“I am incredibly grateful to the supporters and, most importantly, the players, who I am genuinely gutted for.

“The group is a fantastic one and I wish the squad every success for the season ahead.

“Really disappointed the journey has ended so soon, but I leave with great pride in what Paul Bracewell, Karl Halabi and I were building at the club.

“My time at Woking has been an eye-opening managerial experience and one that will undoubtedly make me stronger for the next challenge in my career.”

Sports.title: ‘Point of no return’ – LaLiga club barred indefinitely from own stadium over fears supporters risk catching disease
Sports.content:
LA LIGA side Rayo Vallecano have been banned from their own stadium amid fears supporters could catch Legionnaires’ disease.

The Estadio de Vallecas in Madrid has been closed over links to the severe form of pneumonia, that is caused by inhaling water droplets containing Legionella bacteria.



The Spanish club’s licence to rent the 14,708 stadium from the Madrid government has been suspended following an audit.

This highlighted significant health and safety concerns including a risk of fires because of rubbish around the stadium and electrical faults.



Seating around the stadium also appeared run down with insects present around the ground.

The club is also said to have not complied with the local authorities’ requests to test water quality.



Madrid’s regional head of sport, culture and tourism Mariano ⁠de Paco noted that Rayo failed to comply with maintenance requests.

De Paco told reporters: “We’ve tried to get this back on track but we’ve reached a point of no return – the lack of maintenance has been certified.

“The club wasn’t complying so authorities had ​to take action. What has happened is intolerable.”

Rayo reached last season’s Conference League final, losing 1-0 to Crystal Palace.

There are now less than three weeks remaining until the start of the 2026-27 LaLiga campaign.

They are then set to host Alaves at Vallecas Stadium on Thursday August 20.

No alternative venue has been confirmed if Vallecas Stadium remains out of action.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino responds to furious backlash over World Cup sale as nations consider boycott
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino responds to furious backlash over World Cup sale as nations consider boycott

FIFA boss Gianni Infantino has come out to defend his plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup as he underlines the global benefit despite major organisations in football looking to stop his proposal

View 2 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino has attempted to sell his controversial World Cup plan

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has insisted that 'fans would gain immeasurably' from his proposal to sell stakes in the World Cup - which has been condemned by leading individuals and organisations within the game.

‌



Infantino has seen his popularity plummet following a World Cup that faced accusations of corruption and disregard for the laws of the game. Now, in what is seen as a major money grab, the FIFA president is looking to sell stakes in FIFA's major competitions.

‌



He has claimed that the planned deal would ultimately raise billions, which would be put back into the game, but auctioning off aspects of World Cup has not been well received.

‌



Infantino insisted the proposal was done so that FIFA could unlock "previously uncaptured commercial value" but maintained it would be the subject a democratic vote of FIFA's 211 member associations and approval by the FIFA council - even if he has threatened a lack of funding for those who don't back the idea.

UEFA and Andy Burnham among those to hit back at FIFA's World Cup sale proposal READ MORE :

Ruthless Gianni Infantino's threat to FIFA members as he sets World Cup sale date READ MORE :

In a video released on Wednesday the FIFA president has said: "FIFA Forward Enterprise, or FFE, is actually a proposal, an offer. It's part of a democratic process – a consultation process – and, above all, it is an opportunity but not an obligation. It is a golden opportunity to turbocharge the development of the game globally. But again, it is just an offer, not an obligation."

He went on to add: "Capturing that value requires additional expertise, additional insight, distinct from governing and developing the sport. It would simply commercialise and organise all FIFA-owned competitions along with sponsorship, broadcast, licensing and new ventures for the benefit of FIFA's 211 member associations."

‌



Infantino has appealed to the fans, claiming they would all benefit from the investment. "Fans from everywhere in the world would gain immeasurably from this game-changing potential because it will transform football in their countries," he said.

View 2 Images UEFA are looking to put a stop to Gianni Infantino's proposal (Image: Pau BARRENA/AFP via Getty Images)

UEFA have been outspoken against the idea and will hold a crisis meeting of its members to decide on action to hit back at Infantino’s World Cup plans. He has told countries that they have 53 days to sign up or face financial repercussions.

Article continues below

The 55 European associations are ­expected to discuss a range of actions, which includes a possible boycott of FIFA tournaments. Many of the leading figure in European football see Infantino's proposal as a bribe to the national associations.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher highlights major Bradley Barcola concern as Liverpool make move for star
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher highlights major Bradley Barcola concern as Liverpool make move for star

Liverpool are keen on a deal for PSG star Bradley Barcola before the end of the transfer window but Reds legend Jamie Carragher is concerned over a deal for the Frenchman

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher has shared his thoughts on Liverpool signing Bradley Barcola (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool icon Jamie Carragher believes the Reds are targeting the wrong man in Bradley Barcola. Anfield chiefs are determined to add to their attacking options this summer following the exit of Mohamed Salah.

‌



A number of names have been linked including Yan Diomande - who looks set to join Real Madrid - and Athletic Bilbao’s Nico Williams. But it appears that the Reds are now putting all of their effort into signing Barcola.

‌



It has been reported that Liverpool are ready to submit their first bid for the 23-year-old, who is keen on a move, having turned down the chance to sign a new deal at the Parc des Princes. It has also been suggested that Liverpool may have to pay over £110m for his services.

‌



Liverpool icon Carragher has given his take on a move, but believes Liverpool would be better served spending their money elsewhere.

Liverpool takeover plan clear as billionaires approached over buying stake from FSG READ MORE :

"No, he plays on the opposite flank!" Carragher wrote on social media. "LFC currently have three players who could play from the left in Rio/Gakpo/Wirtz & no one who plays from the right."

Asked if one solution could potentially be to switch academy graduate Rio Ngumoha over to the right-hand side, the former defender did not believe that would work either.

‌



"Well Rio has always played from the left so that’s obviously his best position," Carragher replied. "Gakpo should move really but who knows.

"I’m interested to see where Wirtz plays, if he’s 10 Dom plays CM. I’m not sure about that. Need a right winger desperately!"

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola has been linked with a move to Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Liverpool have of course already added to their attacking options this summer, with a move for Osasuna’s Victor Munoz. The World Cup winner is set to arrive at Liverpool after a season in which he scored seven goals for the Spanish side in all competitions.

Asked if he had a number in his mind of how many players he would want to sign last week, boss Andoni Iraola replied: “No, I think it’s difficult to say a number when the market is open, and you have to be always open to new options to improve the squad.

“There are obvious situations that we know where we need to sign players. A winger, for example – we definitely need to sign a winger.

Article continues below

“But there are other situations that we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what’s the cost, how we also see the players we have. We have some tricky positions where we have injured players that we trust but is still not the ideal situation. So, it will depend on a lot of things.”

Sports.title: Jack Grealish could take unlikely Man City exit route as record transfer snubbed
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish could take unlikely Man City exit route as record transfer snubbed

Jack Grealish has been overlooked for Manchester City's pre-season tour and the playmaker is attracting interest in Saudi Arabia, who could offer him a way out of the Etihad

View 2 Images Jack Grealish is now facing a tough summer (Image: Neal Simpson/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

Jack Grealish could be offered a shock route out of Manchester City with a move to Saudi Arabia potentially materialising for the out of favour playmaker.

‌



The former Aston Villa captain has been overlooked for City's pre-season tour to Hong Kong and Seoul. His foot injury was given as a key reason behind his omission, but it does little to suggested he will be part of Enzo Maresca's plans.

‌



Despite spending his entire career in England Al Hilal are considering a move, reports talkSport. They have already raided West Ham for Crysencio Summerville and Grealish is now on their radar as they eye quality on the flanks.

‌



The 30-year-old returned to his parent club this summer with his future unclear after spending last season on loan at Everton, where he impressed as he benefited from regular minutes for the first time in years.

Arsenal target Bruno Guimaraes facing same transfer dilemma that Man Utd stars got wrong READ MORE :

Chelsea hoping to repeat Man Utd and Liverpool's inspired transfer deals with latest moves READ MORE :

Despite that the Toffees chose not to take up the £50million purchase option in his loan agreement, leaving Grealish back at square one with his City days seemingly numbered as he remains on the periphery with his contract winding down.

Maresca, who has replaced Pep Guardiola, has worked with Grealish when he was an assistant at the Etihad and has already addressed the player's future, but was non-committal over their next move.

‌



"At the moment, he's here. He's a Man City player," he said during his first press conference. "I always said the same. In any club I join, I like to know if there are players that belong to the club. It's my duty to try to coach them. Jack is here. I have a good relationship with Jack since I left.

View 2 Images Manchester United are in talks with a move for Crysencio Summerville (Image: Getty Images)

"Also, we keep in touch, and the reason why is because he has a big heart and he's a very good guy. So this is the reason why. And then we see what happens."

‌



Given he has 12 months left on his deal City are looking to secure a permanent exit, which will now come at a fraction of the £100m they spent to sign him in 2021 when he became their record signing - a tag Elliot Anderson has only just taken from him.

City have benefited from selling players to Saudi Arabian clubs with Riyad Mahrez, Aymeric Laporte and Riyad Mahrez all heading to the Middle East.

Sports.title: Arsenal and Tottenham suffer huge transfer blow as top target out for MONTHS after surgery
Sports.content:
Arsenal and Tottenham suffer huge transfer blow as top target out for MONTHS after surgery

Premier League sides Arsenal and Tottenham have both been linked with a move for Bournemouth star Eli Junior Kroupi but he is now highly unlikely to be on the move this summer

View 2 Images The sought-after Eli Junior Kroupi has undergone foot surgery (Image: Getty Images)

The in-demand Bournemouth striker Eli Junior Kroupi has been hit with a brutal injury blow, having been ruled out for four months after undergoing foot surgery.

‌



The Frenchman sustained the injury while in action for Bournemouth during pre-season. And the issue was so severe that Kroupi was forced to undergo surgery, with the Cherries confirming that the procedure went to plan.

‌



However, it appears the south coast outfit could be without one of their breakout stars from last season until around Christmas. According to reports, the 20-year-old is now facing a period of around three to four months on the sidelines - which is also unwelcome news for the striker's many suitors, including Arsenal, Tottenham and Barcelona.

‌



A statement from Bournemouth on Wednesday read: “AFC Bournemouth can confirm that Junior Kroupi has undergone successful surgery after sustaining a foot injury during a pre-season training session in Austria.

Arsenal target Bruno Guimaraes facing same transfer dilemma that Man Utd stars got wrong READ MORE :

“The 20-year-old returned to the UK earlier this week to undergo the procedure and will consequently face a spell on the sidelines.

“Junior will now be supported by the club's medical and performance staff as he begins a period of rehabilitation. Everyone at AFC Bournemouth extends their best wishes to Junior and looks forward to seeing him back on the pitch.”

‌



Kroupi joined Bournemouth from French side Lorient in 2025 but returned to Ligue 1 on loan. He then enjoyed a very impressive debut campaign on the South Coast, having hit 13 Premier League goals.

That form was good enough to see the likes of Arsenal and Spurs express an interest in his services, while Spanish giants Barcelona were also credited as admirers. But a move now appears highly unlikely.

View 2 Images Kroupi is now set to be out for a considerable amount of time (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Kroupi is not the only Bournemouth star to court interest this summer. Playmaker Alex Scott also has plenty of admirers, with Chelsea among those interested.

Bournemouth will understandably be very keen to keep hold of both as they attempt to get off on the best foot under new boss Marco Rose. The German replaced Andoni Iraola after his move to Liverpool.

Bournemouth also have European football to contend with for the first time this season. The Cherries finished sixth in the table last season and secured a spot in the Europa League.

Article continues below

Arsenal in the meantime have been forced to look elsewhere as they attempt to add to their attacking options. The Gunners have been linked with a move for Real Madrid star Vinicius Jr, albeit a deal would likely have to be the most expensive in British football history.

Sports.title: Arsenal target Bruno Guimaraes facing same transfer dilemma that Man Utd stars got wrong
Sports.content:
Arsenal target Bruno Guimaraes facing same transfer dilemma that Man Utd stars got wrong

The likes of Marcus Rashford and Jadon Sancho face uncertain futures this summer whilst major transfer targets face huge decisions on where they land

View 4 Images Marcus Rashford still faces an uncertain future this summer (Image: Getty Images)

For too many players, this summer presents a dangerous route down a path that could see their careers pass them by - if they haven't already.

‌



There's some big names either without a club - or at clubs who aren't sold on having them as fixtures in the first-team next season. The solution, if they want to realise their potential or have a shot at getting back to their best, is to seek pastures new.

‌



The somewhat uncomfortable reality of today is that if a player in demand, such as Arsenal target Bruno Guimaraes, wants a move, then, in all honesty, he can get it. See Alexander Isak as a case in point 12 months ago. Yes, you'll burn all your bridges with that club and their fanbase, but the likelihood is you'll get your way. Bruno Guimaraes faces that decision this summer - if he does believe that now is the right time to move to Arsenal, which is a question worth asking from a personal stand point.

‌



Going down that forced exit avenue is far harder for a player who is homegrown or has an affiliation with that club, but they wouldn't be the first to do so. It's an option that remains open to those wanting to take greater control of their future - which some would certainly benefit from doing.

Two players unwanted by Manchester United last season - Jadon Sancho and Marcus Rashford - will be wondering what next season holds for them.

Brentford confirm Jordan Henderson exit as shock Chelsea transfer edges closer READ MORE :

Rashford is back at Old Trafford after his loan spell at Barcelona, but a permanent move to Spain appears unlikely. Sancho was also farmed out on loan to Aston Villa, where he was only used sporadically, where his contract wound down. Now he's a free agent.

‌



A player worth paying £72million for only five years ago has been effectively allowed to walk out of Manchester. Rashford was the top target for PSG a number of years ago, when he continued to be their nemesis in the Champions League, but he chose to extend his stay when crunch time came.

One remains at United - for now - and the other has been moved on. It serves to highlight how pivotal timing is in a player's career, as is their choice of destination. Such decisions can leave a player sinking or swimming.

View 4 Images Jadon Sancho was last with Aston Villa, but is still looking for a club (Image: Getty Images)

‌



United ploughed on impressively last season without Rashford and there's certainly been no 'he's back' statement from those making the decisions. It must leave a man who scored 30 goals only three years ago and is now two years shy of his 30th birthday wondering what went wrong.

His year at Barcelona showed that he still has the ability to perform in big games. Sancho's year at Villa Park didn't necessarily prove that, perhaps why he remains on the market. Its a crying shame for a player who once had Europe's elite eyeing him up. Just what might've happened had he taken the Phil Foden route and stuck out getting limited minutes at Manchester City before being let loose under Pep Guardiola.

Rashford's PSG interest came at a time when Thomas Tuchel was in charge. He's clearly still a fan having taken him to the World Cup with England, but there's no obvious door opening for him at club level.

‌



View 4 Images Kalvin Phillips' career has nosedived since leaving Leeds

Another Englishman in Kalvin Phillips is a man who chose the wrong club at the wrong time - and boy has he paid the price. A stalwart in England's midfielder, adored by Leeds fans. Yes he needed to step up one day, but whoever told him that moving to City, who play one holding midfielder by the name of Rodri, was a good idea must have questions to answer.

Loans to West Ham Ipswich and Sheffield United have done little to recapture the magic that had Phillips nicknamed the 'Yorkshire Pirlo', such was his ability to dictate games. He's another fishing around for a club this summer.

‌



Conversely, eyeing up a gap in someone's squad or seeing a club on the up is ultimately a skill in of itself - and one that has worked out for some of the Premier League's top performers.

Declan Rice had his pick of England's elite when he was looking to make a move in 2023 and choosing Arsenal has made him a Premier League champion. The Gunners are favourites this year as they bid to defend their title.

View 4 Images Moving to Arsenal has proved an inspired move for Declan Rice (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

‌



Cole Palmer moved to Chelsea at a time when his route into the City team was firmly blocked off - and landing weekly football at Stamford Bridge helped him to become one of the best young players in England.

Yes those moves needed an element of luck to fall their way, but those breaks often fall to the players who are prepared to take the plunge, especially in the right environment.

The Premier League isn't short of players attracting attention this summer: Guimaraes, Alex Scott, Jack Grealish and Liam Delap - to name a few.

‌



For Guimaraes, does he play every game in an Arsenal midfield that already includes Rice, Mikel Merino, Martin Zubimendi and Martin Odegaard. And are they really set up to win for multiple years. He may think yes to both.

Delap and Grealish have both made the step up to major outfits, but neither move has worked out, so what next?

Opting whether to stick or twist, and where to twist, can define careers. And in recent years, too many have been left questioning where the wrong turn came.

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola transfer: Liverpool ready £110m bid as PSG star approves Anfield move
Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola transfer: Liverpool ready £110m bid as PSG star approves Anfield move

Liverpool are still searching for Mohamed Salah’s replacement but they appear to have been handed encouragement in their interest in PSG and France forward Bradley Barcola

View 2 Images PSG have set a high price for Bradley Barcola (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool are readying their opening offer for Bradley Barcola with the winger open to a move to Anfield - but PSG are remaining firm over their asking price. The Reds have identified the French forward as an ideal option to bolster their forward line following Mohamed Salah’s exit.

‌



Barcola had been mentioned alongside a host of other names including Yan Diomande, who now appears set for a switch to Real Madrid, and Athletic Bilbao’s Nico Williams. But Barcola is now the firm favourite for a switch to Merseyside, with Liverpool having received encouragement ahead of an opening bid.

‌



According to The Telegraph, Barcola is unwilling to sign a new contract at the Parc des Princes, with his current deal set to expire in 2028. As a result, he is now prepared for the next stage of his career in the Premier League.

‌



Anfield officials have reportedly already held talks with the wideman’s representatives and it is said that the response has been favourable. That news has given Liverpool a considerable boost ahead of Andoni Iraola’s first season at the helm, particularly given the task that the Spaniard has in picking the club up after a disappointing campaign.

The task that Liverpool now have is convincing PSG to sell. The French club were previously keen to bank around £145m should they approve a move - having used Morgan Rogers’ £117m switch to Chelsea as a guide.

Liverpool takeover plan clear as billionaires approached over buying stake from FSG READ MORE :

Liverpool forced to change pre-season plans as Reds hit with travel chaos READ MORE :

As it stands Liverpool are ready to lodge an opening offer in the region of around £110m but with PSG wanting considerably more than that, it remains to be seen if Anfield chiefs would be willing to break the British transfer record to sign him.

‌



Should talks progress positively, Barcola will then be offered at least a five-year deal to move to Anfield.

Barcola has been with PSG since a 2023 switch from French rivals Lyon. Since then, he has scored 39 goals in 152 games, 13 of which came last season. He is also a 28-time French international, having also netted on six occasions for his country.

Should he complete a move to Anfield, he would become the third addition of the summer window for Liverpool. Jeremy Jacquet agreed a move back in January from French side Rennes, while Victor Munoz was recruited from Osasuna earlier this summer.

‌



View 2 Images Liverpool have already been in touch with Barcola's representatives (Image: Getty Images)

Asked if he had a number in his mind of how many players he would want to sign last week, boss Iraola replied: “No, I think it’s difficult to say a number when the market is open, and you have to be always open to new options to improve the squad.

“There are obvious situations that we know where we need to sign players. A winger, for example – we definitely need to sign a winger.

Article continues below

“But there are other situations that we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what’s the cost, how we also see the players we have. We have some tricky positions where we have injured players that we trust but is still not the ideal situation. So, it will depend on a lot of things.”

Sports.title: Draper given wild card for National Bank Open in Montreal
Sports.content:
Jack Draper has been given a wild card for the National Bank Open in Montreal, which is live on Sky Sports from Monday August 3.

Draper got one of the final wild cards alongside Canadians Alexis Galarneau and Liam Draxl as he continues his attempt to try and return from a left arm injury.

The former world No 4 has endured an injury-strewn 2026 which saw him miss all three Grand Slam tournaments, but he enters the National Bank Open after a late withdrawal from this week's DC Open in Washington.

The Brit, who is coached by Sir Andy Murray, has slipped to world No 147 in the ATP rankings, leaving him likely to face qualifying if he is to compete at September's US Open after missing out on direct entry into the main draw.

Draper has only played five tour events this year, last playing in Eastbourne last month.

Ahead of his withdrawal from Washington, Draper said: "I've had an incredibly challenging 12 months, a lot of adversity, a lot of problem solving, a lot of pain, and trying to understand that and come through it.

"I've never had a long-term injury before so I feel much better than I ever have in the last year. I feel physically really good."

Draper first stepped away from the tour a year ago with the arm problem and has managed only a handful of tournaments since, with knee and shoulder issues also interrupting his comeback.

Having missed the Australian Open, the French Open, and Wimbledon, Draper's chances at participating in the last major tournament of 2026 - the US Open - are now also in doubt.

Sports.title: Is Littler most dominant sportsperson in the world?
Sports.content:
Teenage dart sensation Luke Littler has left the darts world questioning if anyone will ever get near him again after winning the World Matchplay Darts on Sunday.

'The Nuke' stormed to victory in Blackpool, winning the competition for the second year in a row and seeing off final opponent Gerwyn Price 18-9.

Littler being in total control at a darts competition is nothing new. He's won every PDC major title in 2026 so far, and his World Matchplay performance has made it very difficult to argue he's not head and shoulders above his competitors.

His mind-blowing performances have sparked debate over where he ranks in the sporting world, leading Sky Sports' Love The Darts podcast pundits, former darts player Laura Turner and darts commentator Chris Murphy, to debate whether he is indeed the most dominant sportsperson in the world right now.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chris Murphy and Laura Turner debate whether Luke Littler has already surpassed Phil Taylor as the greatest ever darts player.

"It's a very difficult question, how do you measure dominance?" Murphy said. "Darts seems to have more majors than any other sport, if you're doing it on major titles, but then again if you just took the top four and made it fair, he wins what you might call the Grand Slam titles.

"He holds them all and he's on course to have a clean sweep of every title so of course he does. I think yes [he is the most dominant]."

Murphy then named two other sporting stars that come close to giving Littler a run for his money - tennis world No 1 Jannik Sinner and his golf equivalent, Scottie Scheffler - but concluded neither can touch him.

"Looking at other sports, we've mentioned tennis, Sinner maybe he's in the conversation," he said. "Scheffler in golf has been No 1 for a long time, but I don't think any of them get near Littler."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the World Matchplay final between Luke Littler and Gerwyn Price.

Turner agreed, pointing out how rare it is to have two English people dominating a sport in both the men's and women's editions at the same time.

"It's very hard to say no [he isn't the most dominant] isn't it," Turner said. "From a women's darts point of view actually I think [Women's World Matchplay winner] Beau Greaves is unbelievably dominant, she's just picked up the Matchplay in Blackpool. She won 17 out of the 24 titles available in that qualification process as well.

"She's been on a run of 114 consecutive wins, it took Fallon [Sherrock] at a 102 average just to stop that run. Beau is very dominant.

"In darts at the moment I personally think we're very lucky, I know Beau is on the Pro Tour as well. I can't think of another sport where at this moment in time, anyone that is dominating in the way they are."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Women's World Matchplay final between Beau Greaves and Fallon Sherrock in Blackpool.

Does Littler edge Taylor as darts' greatest?

While Turner and Murphy have been wowed by Littler this month, they believe the teenager still has a while to go until he can call himself darts' greatest ever.

Asked if he is the best darts player to ever do it, Murphy replied: "No, and this is where I think we need to zoom out a little bit. Potential to best the greatest? Possibly, but I don't think it's especially close yet to be honest.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following his World Matchplay final victory against Gerwyn Price, Luke Littler says he'd love to be the greatest darts player of all time and admits he is chasing the feat of winning every major darts title in a calendar year.

"It's not criticism of his abilities and talents, it's just simple arithmetic I suppose. Phil Taylor's title tally, 16 world titles, spanning across four different generations of darts players, and he's had to reinvent himself for different games in different eras."

Taylor, who retired in 2018, holds the record for the most darts world titles. Littler, meanwhile, has two, winning the PDC World Darts Championship in 2025 and 2026 after bursting on the scene in 2024.

Laura agreed that Littler has a way to go yet to edge Taylor, adding: "All of us suffer from recency bias. There's a lot of people don't forget that never engaged in darts to the level they are before Luke Littler came onto the scene.

Image: Darts icon Phil Taylor was Luke Littler's idol growing up

"Ultimately, Phil has played through different generations, I don't want to say mind games but you know you can get under people's skin a bit more.

"Ability wise, and all the accolades he has won over all those years, you have to say Phil is the greatest ever darts player we've had.

"Luke Littler perhaps one of the most dominant sports people at this time."

Sebastian Bialecki secured his second PDC ranking title with a hard-fought 8-6 victory against Mario Vandenbogaerde in Wednesday's Players Championship 26 final.

Exactly a year to the day since he claimed his maiden ranking title in Hildesheim, Bialecki repeated the feat on German soil, overturning a 5-3 deficit to cap off another memorable triumph.

The 22-year-old has celebrated an astonishing six Development Tour titles in 2026, and he reaffirmed his credentials by returning to the winner's circle at Halle 39.

Bialecki began his title challenge with successive ton-plus averages in deciding-leg wins over Dennie Olde Kalter and Cor Dekker, recovering from 5-3 down in his opener against Olde Kalter.

Sports.title: England dominate Tonga in must-win clash at Commonwealth Games
Sports.content:
England dominated Tonga 94-32 in their must-win Pool A game at the Commonwealth Games at the Hydro in Glasgow.

It means England's hunt for a semi-final place continues and they did it in some style, scoring a record 94 goals for the team at the Games.

It surpasses their previous record of 89 goals at the Commonwealth Games, which came 24 years ago against Sri Lanka in 2002.

The match was, throughout, in England's hands after they cantered into a 27-8 lead at the end of the first quarter.

Eleanor Cardwell then took real control, scoring 54 goals from 60 shots. Sasha Glasgow added 18, Ella Clark added 12, then Olivia Tchine added 10 for a statement win.

England are attempting to cement a top-two spot as they try to go for glory for the first time in eight years after their 2018 triumph.

They currently sit in third but are level on points with Australia and South Africa.

England's goal average is 1.74 and goal difference is 127. South Africa's goal average is 2.06 and their goal difference is 123. Australia's goal average is 1.99 and their goal difference is 116.

In their final match of the pool stages, England will take on South Africa at 9pm on Thursday.

Sports.title: Rockets hand Fire first defat in The Hundred as Pretorius stars for Spirit
Sports.content:
Trent Rockets handed Welsh Fire a first defeat of the season in The Hundred in a one-sided affair at Sophia Gardens.

The visitors chased down a below-par target of 123 with 28 balls to spare, Ben Duckett seeing the Rockets to victory with an unbeaten 52.

The start of the Rockets' chase was not fluent by any means but the Fire bowlers were sloppy, giving away four free-hits in the powerplay and seven in total.

Duckett faced the first four, only finding the boundary once, but he and Finn Allen (33) still managed to move the visitors onto 42-0 after 25 balls with little cause for concern.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Welsh Fire's Joe Root was bowled by Matt Henry after a failed attempt at a scoop shot in the match against Trent Rockets

The explosive Allen began to accelerate, taking 17 runs off Sam Cook's first five. He and Duckett cruised along against an uninspired Fire attack, taking the score to 75 before Allen fell lbw to fellow Kiwi Rachin Ravindra for 33.

Duckett, joined by Tom Banton (31), continued on his merry way, bringing up a second half-century in as many games, this time from 42 balls, as the Rockets made it two wins from three.

Hosts Fire had earlier ended their batting powerplay on 26-2, having been asked to bat first. They lost Phil Salt and Joe Root for five runs apiece to the seam of Matt Henry (2-16), the latter failing to connect with a ramp.

After reaching 59-2 at halfway, the Fire looked to push on, but proceeded to lose three wickets in the next 14 balls, including the set Matt Short for 36 from 26.

Jordan Cox (33) countered by launching Mitchell Santner's left-arm spin for three consecutive sixes, but perished going for a fourth, spectacularly caught on the cover boundary by a diving Allen.

Fire then limped to 122-7 with Asa Tribe (13no) and Chris Woakes (4no) failing to find the boundary off Mohammad Amir and Lewis Gregory in the closing stages of the innings.

Their target would prove easily surpassable by Trent Rockets, who moved up to second in the table with their second win from three games.

'The bowlers take credit for the win'

Image: Ben Duckett credited the bowling attack for the win (ECB Images)

Meerkat Match Hero - Ben Duckett - on Sky Sports Cricket:

"The bowlers were superb. Coming here, we spoke about adapting to the pitch as early as you can. They take massive credit for this win.

"My aim was to try and get through the powerplay and then it might actually become easier. It's made a lot easier when you've got Finn Allen at the other end whacking it.

"Four free-hits really help as well, but, to be honest, I really struggled to find rhythm throughout that whole innings. I'm pretty sure everyone saw that. Finn played beautifully and Bants came in and took all the pressure off me.

Spirit beat MI London by seven wickets thanks to Pretorius heroics

Twenty-year-old Lhuan-dre Pretorius smashed 64 from 28 balls to help London Spirit to a seven-wicket win over MI London in a hotly contested London derby.

Chasing 165 to win, Jonny Bairstow and Pretorius flew out of the blocks with the left-handed Pretorius smashing Trent Boult out of the ground, a towering blow 106 metres over midwicket.

They were to be rewarded for their patience, moving up through the gears against Adam Zampa and Andrew Tye, England man Jacks moving to his half-century from 30 balls.

Things then swung back in the favour of the visitors when Vince fell to James Coles for 26 and Jamie Overton (3-30) saw the back of Jacks and new man Nicholas Pooran in the space of three balls. Sports.title: Player at centre of viral 'Clicky Ponting' scandal suspended
Sports.content:
The cricketer at the centre of the 'Clicky Ponting' cheating allegations has been suspended and will not play again "for the foreseeable future", the club have announced.

Saltburn Cricket Club is under investigation by the North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League amid cheating accusations against one of their players.

Saltburn, who have made national headlines, were due to face Marton Cricket Club on Wednesday but have conceded the contest.

It comes after footage of an alleged finger-clicking incident, which took place in a Division Two match between Saltburn and Norton Cricket Club on Saturday, went viral on social media.

The clip has over 7.5m views and the scandal has been dubbed 'Clicky Ponting', after the former Australia captain, Ricky Ponting.

Some users have suggested the fielder, seen standing at slip, clicks his fingers as the ball passes an opponent's bat to imitate the noise of an edge.

The clip shows Saltburn's wicketkeeper then catching the ball behind the stumps. The team appeals to the umpire, who gives the batter out.

The North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League says it has launched an investigation into the matter.

A statement released on Saltburn's social media channels read: "This is issued in response to the widely publicised complaint made against a Saltburn Cricket Club member and, as a consequence, against the club more generally.

"We are treating this allegation with the utmost seriousness and, as a family-centric club, we are fully cooperating with the NYS League's investigation.

"We believe that the club acted decisively as soon as the complaint and investigation were made known to us. The player at the centre of the complaint has been suspended and will not play again for the club this season or in the foreseeable future, pending the outcome of this investigation."

The player in question, when contacted by the Daily Mail, said: "Naturally, I cannot comment on that. I also cannot answer any questions because I am currently at work."

Saltburn currently sit top of the Division Two league table having won 10 of their 15 matches this season.

The team's wicketkeeper also leads the league for the most fielding dismissals - 34, of which 31 came from catches behind the stumps.

Earlier in July, Saltburn secured a 22-run victory against Shildon Railway Cricket Club, a match in which their wicketkeeper took eight catches. No Test wicketkeeper has taken more than seven catches in an innings.

After the video surfaced on social media, Middlesbrough second XI captain Rory Cotterill alleged that two further incidents had taken place during a game between his side and Saltburn in June.

Banton: 'Clicky Ponting' kind of clever but not acceptable

The story has engulfed the cricketing world, with discussions raging about what the next steps will be.

For England and Somerset's Tom Banton, while it is a "clever" way of cricket it is not one that can be justified.

"It's interesting, kind of clever in a way. But I cannot vouch for things like that, it's not acceptable," he told Sky Sports.

"It's been caught out and something is going to be done about it because I'm not sure it's in the rules of cricket."

Sports.title: WRU confirm Scarlets or Ospreys will be cut by 2028
Sports.content:
The Welsh Rugby Union has confirmed it will cut one of its four men's professional teams from the 2028/29 season.

The WRU says one of its teams will be based in the capital Cardiff, one in the west and one in the east.

It means one of the two regions in the west, Llanelli-based Scarlets or Swansea-based Ospreys, will be defunct, while Cardiff and the Dragons offered the respective capital and east licences.

The WRU Board says the licensing framework and the licence award process will begin in December 2026 and conclude by the end of the 2026/27 season at the latest.

Professional Rugby Board chair Marianne Okland said: "There is now a duty on all of us involved in the professional game in Wales to work together to determine a shared future operating model. How we progress over the forthcoming months will be critical."

Sports.title: Uefa calls emergency meeting as opposition to Fifa plan hardens
Sports.content:
Uefa has called an emergency ­meeting of its 55 members for Thursday afternoon to discuss a coordinated response to Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors. A European boycott of Fifa tournaments is among the options under consideration.

As the next major event in the Fifa calendar, a boycott of next year’s Women’s World Cup has been ­mentioned in preliminary ­discussions, although there would be a reluctance in some quarters to make the women’s game suffer as a consequence of a protest against Fifa proposals that primarily revolve around ­monetising the men’s World Cup and Club World Cup.

Uefa’s initial condemnation of Fifa’s plan to “sell the soul” of ­football has received strong backing from Concacaf – the North, Central ­American and Caribbean ­confederation – and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC). If their members follow their leads there should be sufficient votes to block the proposal.

Those three confederations make up 143 of the 211 Fifa members, but unanimity is not guaranteed, as was made clear when Czechia’s ­football association became the first in Europe to back the plan.

Having received more than 200 ­letters of endorsement backing his re-election next year, Infantino is confident he has enough votes – although it is unclear whether the proposal requires a simple ­majority to be passed. Several sources have said that creating a new commercial entity – Fifa Forward Enterprise [FFE] – and selling a 20% stake to investors would necessitate a change of Fifa statutes, which requires a 75% majority that would be much harder to obtain.

View image in fullscreen Fifa’s branding was impossible to miss during the World Cup. Photograph: Mike Segar/Reuters

On Wednesday evening, Infantino released a video to address the ­backlash. “FFE is actually a ­proposal, an offer,” he said. “It’s part of a democratic process – a ­consultation process – and, above all, it is an opportunity but not an ­obligation. It is a golden opportunity to turbocharge the development of the game globally.”

Earlier, Uefa redoubled its attack on Fifa by accusing the world ­governing body of “using our sport to enrich themselves and their friends” after it emerged that ­Infantino had ­presented members with a deadline of 19 September to decide whether to apply for an ­initial payment of $20m (£15m) from the proposed sell-off.

A further $20m for each ­association would also be made available at a later date, although it is unclear whether accepting the money would equate to a formal ­endorsement and therefore remove the need for a vote.

“Today we have learned of Fifa’s deadline to associations to support their proposals or have the one-off payout offer withdrawn,” Uefa said. “This says everything you need to know about this plan. But having held discussions with many stakeholders across the game, Uefa knows there is significant and growing opposition to Fifa’s scheme. Fifa cannot continue to use our sport to enrich themselves and their friends. We can grow the game correctly. It’s time to prioritise associations, clubs, leagues, players and fans.”

Uefa’s second statement of condemnation followed a similarly strong intervention from ­Concacaf, which is particularly ­significant given the confederation has just hosted the most ­lucrative World Cup and covers the region that has brought the proposed new investment from the New York-based Thrive Eternal.

The Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, was instrumental in the success of the US, Mexican and Canadian bid for the tournament, but along with the seven other Fifa vice‑presidents and Fifa council members he was kept in the dark over the plans.

“Concacaf was only made aware of this matter through media reports and, subsequently, via a media release,” Concacaf said. “We are deeply concerned by the lack of due process.

“We share the ­disappointment of many within our region and the game that this level of detail has been designed and shared publicly before any discussion with the ­relevant governance bodies and stakeholders has taken place.

“As leaders within football, we are the custodians of the game. Collectively, Fifa, the confederations and every member association have a responsibility to always act in the best interests of the sport. Every decision we make must be guided by good governance, robust processes and long-term stewardship.

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino announces Saudi Arabia as the 2034 World Cup hosts. The AFC’s statement is understood to have the backing of the Saudi Arabian federation. Photograph: Fifa

“This is the framework within which Concacaf operates. We trust that all within the Fifa family will act in the same manner.”

The AFC issued a similar statement of disapproval, which significantly is understood to have the backing of the Saudi Arabian football federation, a close ally of Infantino and the host of the 2034 World Cup.

“The AFC was not consulted on the proposal and is disappointed that a matter of such significance entered the public domain before the AFC family had been afforded the opportunity to examine and discuss it through the appropriate and established governance channels,” it said.

“While the AFC recognises the importance of exploring innovative approaches that can strengthen the future of global football, initiatives of this scale and consequence must be founded upon the principles of good governance, transparency and meaningful consultation.

“Decisions that may reshape the commercial and financial future of the game require comprehensive prior engagement with confederations, member associations and other relevant stakeholders before any proposal is made to the appropriate decision-making bodies.”

Elite clubs also expressed their unhappiness, with the European Football Clubs organisation pointing out that Fifa had not consulted it despite the two bodies having signed a memorandum of understanding.

“As an institution that represents over 850 football clubs – whose member clubs, their players and communities are fundamental participants in football worldwide, not least in Fifa’s competitions including all the international club competitions – it would be wholly appropriate for EFC to be fully consulted on a proposal of such magnitude,” it said.

“EFC learned about this proposal in the same way as most global football stakeholders – without warning and through the media.”

Sports.title: Fifa opens disciplinary proceedings against Argentina over Falklands banner and final chaos
Sports.content:
Fifa has opened disciplinary ­proceedings against Argentina over the Falkland Islands banner ­displayed after their World Cup semi‑final win against England in Atlanta.

As Argentina celebrated ­reaching the final with their dramatic 2-1 ­victory, several players held a sign ­proclaiming “Las Malvinas son ­Argentinas” – the ­Malvinas are Argentinian – in ­reference to the ­British overseas territory in the south Atlantic.

The dispute over the islands, which have been ruled by Britain since 1833, is long running and led to a 74-day conflict in 1982, during which more than 900 people – 649 Argentinians and 255 Britons – lost their lives.

Fifa’s disciplinary code ­prohibits “using a sports event for ­demonstrations of a non-sporting nature” and the banner prompted political debate on both sides of the ­Atlantic. A spokesperson for the then UK prime minister, Keir Starmer, said: “The World Cup might not be ours, but the Falkland Islands ­definitely are.” Andrew Giuliani, the head of the White House Fifa taskforce, defended Argentina’s players, saying the US believed in free speech.

The incident was not the first time an Argentina team had expressed such sentiments. In 2014, Fifa fined Argentina £20,000 for a far larger banner held ‌up by players before a friendly with Slovenia in La Plata.

Fifa’s full World Cup charge sheet against the Argentinian Football Association also includes ­“discriminatory chants and gestures, late kick-offs, failure to comply with match and security protocols, the display of inappropriate messages by the team and spectators and the throwing of objects by spectators in relation to several matches”.

0:18 Ugly scenes as Argentina lose World Cup final – video

Several players are also under investigation in relation to the ­chaotic scenes that followed ­Argentina’s 1-0 extra-time defeat by Spain in the final. As Spain attempted to celebrate, ­altercations broke out across the pitch at New York New Jersey Stadium.

The Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes, who was seen wrestling Spain’s Eric García to the ground, faces three counts of assault under the Fifa disciplinary code, while the defender Nahuel Molina faces two counts of assault (one completed and one attempted) and one count of unsporting behaviour.

The assistant coach, Roberto Ayala, faces one count of assault, and Thiago Almada, an unused substitute in the final, one count of unsporting behaviour. Spain’s Gavi also faces an unsporting behaviour charge.

“In accordance with the Fifa ­disciplinary code, the respondents have now been provided with the opportunity to present their position, following which a decision will be issued by the Fifa disciplinary committee in due course,” said Fifa.

Sports.title: ‘I’m very sorry’: Mancini apologises after being reappointed as Italy head coach
Sports.content:
Roberto Mancini issued an apology in his first public comments after being reappointed as the Italy head coach, three years after he abandoned the same job for a lucrative contract with Saudi Arabia.

“I’m very sorry,” Mancini said. “It was like losing the woman of your life. And it means you did something that shouldn’t have been done. So I’m sorry, very sorry also for everything that happened over these last three years … I’m going to try to bring the national team back where it belongs.”

Italy failed for a third straight time to qualify for the World Cup, prompting the resignations of Gabriele Gravina as federation president and Gennaro Gattuso as head coach in April, shortly after the playoff defeat to Bosnia and Herzegovina.

The 61-year-old Mancini led the Azzurri to the European Championship title in 2021 but resigned as Italy coach in August 2023, taking over Saudi Arabia’s national team two weeks later. “It was completely my fault,” Mancini said, referring to a lack of communication with Gravina.

Mancini’s first match back in charge will be against Belgium in the Nations League on 25 September at the Stadio Olimpico in Rome. He was asked about what type of reception fans might give him. “I realise some people will be against me,” Mancini said. “I’m hoping the squad plays well enough that maybe people will forgive me.”
