World.title: Mancini wants Italy back to trophy-winning ways
World.content:
ROME - Newly-appointed Italy coach Roberto Mancini said Wednesday he was dreaming of bagging a major trophy, the Azzurri having missed out on the last three World Cups.

Mancini was speaking at his first press conference since being unveiled as the successor to Gennaro Gattuso, who resigned as Italy coach after their World Cup qualification play-off final defeat by Bosnia and Herzegovina in March.

The 61-year-old Mancini was previously Italy boss from 2018 until 2023, leading them to the Euro 2020 title.

He has been preferred to another ex-national team coach in Antonio Conte.

"I hope to win another trophy, maybe two," Mancini said.

"My goal is to make sure the team immediately gets back to winning ways."

Mancini's first period at the helm of the Italy side ended suddenly when he took up the Saudi Arabia job.

Leaving the Italy setup at the time, he said, was "a bit like losing the woman of your life".

But the former Manchester City and Inter Milan coach, who has signed a four-year deal, vowed "to make sure the team is so good that the fans fall in love with it all over again".

Mancini added: "I believe there are young, talented players in Italy. I simply believe we need to trust them and let them play."

Mancini's first game in charge is a Nations League match against Belgium in Rome on September 25, before facing Turkey three days later.

Then comes a trip to Paris when Italy take on France, with Zinedine Zidane at the helm.

"These will be important matches," he said. "We'll immediately see our strengths and the areas in which we'll need to improve."

Mancini was appointed on Tuesday, along with Claudio Ranieri as technical director in place of Paolo Maldini, who reportedly threatened to resign if Mancini was appointed.

Mancini's appointment, however, remains divisive despite leading Italy to the Euro 2020 title and a 37-match unbeaten streak.

His abrupt resignation as Italy coach in the summer of 2023 to take charge of Saudi Arabia reportedly damaged his standing with many senior officials at the Italian federation, particularly as the Azzurri were struggling in their qualifying campaign for Euro 2024.

Mancini left his job with the Saudi national side just 14 months later.

He was most recently coach of Qatari club Al-Sadd, with whom he signed a two-year deal last November.

Now he will turn his attentions to the job of taking Italy back to the top of the international game.

The four-time world champions have not reached a World Cup since 2014, and have not even played a knock-out stage match at the tournament since winning the 2006 final against France on penalties.

The one success in that time was the European Championship victory, also secured in a shoot-out against England five years ago.

Their title defence, with Luciano Spalletti at the helm, ended with a last-16 loss to Switzerland in 2024.

Mancini also won three consecutive Serie A titles as Inter Milan boss between 2005 and 2008.

He then led Manchester City to their first English league title since 1968 with a famous last-day victory over QPR in the 2011-12 Premier League season.

World.title: 'Hi Gorgeous' messages put Johnson-Khan relationship under spotlight
World.content:
PRETORIA - The personal relationship between former Investigating Directorate Against Corruption (IDAC) head Advocate Andrea Johnson and Major-General Feroz Khan came under question at the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry on Wednesday.

During Johnson's sixth day on the hot seat, evidence leader Advocate Mahlape Sello presented the commission with text messages between the pair

One of the first text extracts showed Khan had invited Johnson and her family for supper.

Johnson acknowledged this invite but insisted it never happened.

READ | LIVE: Andrea Johnson nears end of marathon testimony

Following those text messages, Sello also focused on the manner in which the two addressed each other.

According to Sello, there were several text messages where the two addressed each other with phrases such as ‘hi, gorgeous’, ‘dearest’ and even expressed how they missed each other.

According to Sello, these messages showed the pair's relationship extended beyond a professional one.

Johnson also faced questions over the arranged meeting between the two at the IDAC office.

During this visit, once again, detailed text messages revealed how Khan entered the IDAC offices through a VIP entrance without signing in, which was against standard protocol.

The visit related to Khan’s concern that someone from the Hawks was plotting against him and needed assistance from Johnson.

READ | LIVE: Andrea Johnson nears end of marathon testimony

Sello, who pressed Johnson, said Khan was not coming to visit in his capacity as a VIP but instead in his personal capacity and needed a favour from her.

She argued that Johnson's intentions were to avoid a record of this visit and that their personal relationship was to an extent where they would go to great lengths to accommodate each other.

Andrea, who did not dismiss the visit, admitted that Khan is not an exception to the rule that when high-ranking officials are invited to the office, they are expected to use the side entrance.

“I am not disputing that he used the entrance. He did come to visit me, and unfortunately, when he did, it turned out to have nothing to do with the Hawks, but he had an issue about someone plotting against him," she said.

World.title: Western Cape has a new police commissioner
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - There is a new sheriff in town and he goes by the name of Lieutenant General Sizakhele Dyantyi.



Dyantyi succeeds Thembisile Patekile as Western Cape Police Commissioner.



He has over 30 years of experience in the police force.



His appointment comes at a time when the province is faced with almost weekly mass shootings as part of deadly gang violence.



The top cop said his main priorities include regaining the trust of communities and expanding the fight against extortion and gangsterism.



The appointments of new Provincial Commissioners in the Western Cape, North West, Limpopo, and Mpumalanga form part of the ongoing efforts to strengthen leadership within the South African Police Service.



eNCA's Ayesha Ismail reports in the video above.

World.title: 'Cat' Matala Trial | Kekana claims police forced their way into his property
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Alleged hitman Musa Kekana, accused number one in the attempted murder case against Vusimuzi 'Cat' Matlala and four others, claims officers illegally breached his property and ignored his basic constitutional rights.



The allegations emerged during the cross-examination of Police Captain Phimi Sekgobela, who's in the witness box to defend police actions.



Matlala and his co-accused's trial within a trial is underway in the High Court in Johannesburg.



The defence is challenging the admissibility of evidence obtained during Kekana's arrest.



Kekana isn't backing down on his fight to have evidence obtained from his arrest deemed inadmissible.



These include firearms, ammunition, cellphone records and some admissions.



Kekana claims the police forced entry into his home and arrested him without reading him his rights, a severe procedural violation if proven true.



A crucial turning point in the trial within a trial may hinge on Captain Sekgobela’s official pocketbook and his diary entry from the day of the arrest.



The defence is expected to scrutinise these logs to expose potential discrepancies between the captain's written records and his testimony.



eNCA's Silindelo Sebata has more details in the video above.

World.title: Can IDAC restore public trust?
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africa’s premier anti-corruption unit is facing one of its biggest challenges yet.

Not prosecuting corruption but restoring public trust.

Founded to spearhead South Africa’s fight against corruption, the Investigating Directorate Against Corruption (IDAC) is now battling to gain the country's confidence back.

Testimony before the Madlanga Commission and Parliament’s ad hoc committee has cast a shadow over IDAC, raising tough questions about its leadership and future.

Former IDAC head Andrea Johnson faced tough questions over allegations relating to IDAC’s conduct and decision-making.

She has since resigned.

Some say Johnson’s resignation isn’t enough.

Since its establishment, IDAC has enrolled major corruption cases, built specialist capacity and helped recover stolen assets, but those gains are now overshadowed by a leadership crisis, slow prosecutions and growing questions over public trust.

The challenge facing IDAC is now bigger than a leadership controversy.

It is about preserving the integrity of one of the country’s most important anti-corruption institutions because in the fight against corruption, public trust is just as important as successful prosecutions.

In the video above, eNCA’s Nabeelah Shaikh unpacks the controversy inside IDAC.

World.title: US man accused of destroying evidence by wiping phone at airport
World.content:
ATLANTA - A US citizen is facing charges for allegedly supplying US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) agents with a passcode that erased the contents of his phone during an airport interrogation.

Samuel Tunick, an activist in a campaign to stop construction of a police training center in Georgia, is accused of destroying evidence during the January 24, 2025 incident at Atlanta's airport.

Tunick, who has pleaded not guilty, faces up to five years in prison if convicted of violating a law that makes it a crime to destroy property to prevent its seizure.

A hearing in the unusual case was held in a US District Court in Atlanta last week.

Tunick was returning from a visit to the Dominican Republic when he was taken aside for questioning by CBP and FBI agents and had his belongings searched, according to court documents.

Tunick's requests to have a lawyer present were repeatedly denied and when asked to unlock his Google Pixel phone, he allegedly supplied a passcode that triggered software that wiped the device.

"The screen went blank, flashed several times and the phone appeared to restart," according to CBP officers.

Tunick's attorneys are arguing that his constitutional rights were violated, including his Fourth Amendment protection from warrantless search and seizure.

Even though the interrogation took place at an international airport, "officers were not permitted to disregard all constitutional protections afforded to Mr Tunick simply because he was at the border," they said in a court filing.

Tunick was being investigated because of his activities with an environmental group known as Defend the Atlanta Forest, which opposes plans to build a police training center, his lawyers said.

There is no evidence that Tunick was involved in criminal activity in connection with the Defend the Atlanta Forest movement, they said, and the demand to unlock his phone was an illegal "fishing expedition."

US courts have held previously, though not unanimously, that a warrantless search at the border is legal, including a forensic search of electronic devices.

In Tunick's case, "law enforcement seemingly took advantage of the relaxed constitutional protections at the border to try to dig up evidence" against him, his lawyers said.

A trial date has not yet been set.

World.title: Spanish wildfire evacuees go home as France hit by new heat alert
World.content:
"I'm happy, I couldn't wait to come home and have my coffee and breakfast," said Maria Jesus Perez Blanca, in her seventies. She was one of about a dozen returnees at the cafes of Aldea del Fresno, west of Madrid on Wednesday morning.

But 12 kilometres (eight miles) away in Pelayos de la Presa, David Rodriguez was knocking down the scorched remains of his home.

"It's a disaster. Just look at it," he said. "All my memories, everything I had was here. My dad built it 40 years ago and everything has been lost."

Officials said on Wednesday that better overnight conditions had helped crews stabilise the fire area, and Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said the coming hours would be "decisive" in the battle to extinguish all the remaining flames.

In France, the Gironde region reported a second calm night and said the massive fire west of France's wine-making capital of Bordeaux was stable.

- 'Extreme temperatures' -

Nevertheless, conditions were set to worsen as the fourth heatwave of an already intense summer arrived.

Water-bombing planes and firefighters supported by volunteers battled a blaze near the seaside town of Lanton west of Bordeaux.

Among the helpers was Jean-Claude Bonnet, 67, who said he had never seen anything like it. "The worst part is seeing the animals that have been burnt to death by the side of the road," he added.

Shortly after the water-bombing planes left, emergency teams were called back into action as a whirlwind of stinging hot ash swept off the burning pine trees and the fire roared back into life.

World.title: Qacha's Nek Port of Entry temporarily closed due to heavy snowfall
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Border Management Authority (BMA) has temporarily suspended operations at the Qacha's Nek Port of Entry between South Africa and Lesotho due to heavy snowfall.

Authorities closed the crossing near Matatiele after weather conditions made travel unsafe for border staff and travellers.

The BMA made the decision in consultation with Lesotho authorities.

Travellers and freight operators are urged to delay their trips or use the Telle Bridge Port of Entry, about 190km away.

President William Ruto and Deputy President Kithure Kindiki during his swearing-in ceremony at KICC in Nairobi on November 1, 2024. [AFP]

Deputy President Kithure Kindiki is a man between a rock and a hard place. Few weeks ago he was moving across the country with display of power and influence.

World.title: Power outage hits Nairobi, Coast and other regions
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya Power technicians replace a transformer in Kanyange, Nyeri. [Mose Sammy, Standard]

Large parts of the country have plunged into darkness on Wednesday evening following a widespread power outage affecting customers in Nairobi, the Coast region, Mt. Kenya and parts of the Central Rift, Kenya Power has announced.

In a statement, the company said electricity supply remains stable in parts of the North Rift and Western regions, which were not affected by the outage.

"Our technical teams have been deployed and are working to restore electricity to the affected areas as quickly as possible," the statement read in part.

However, Kenya Power did not immediately disclose the cause of the blackout or provide a timeline for full restoration.

The company apologised to customers for the inconvenience caused and appealed for patience as restoration efforts continue.

The outage disrupted businesses and households across the affected regions, with many customers taking to social media to seek updates on when power supply would be restored.

World.title: Lawyer seeks orders to suspend court boycott
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Advocate Adrian Kamotho argues that LSK's actions create the impression that court orders can be overturned through a boycott. [File, Standard]

A city lawyer has moved to the High Court seeking conservatory orders to suspend the Law Society of Kenya's (LSK) ongoing targeted boycott of judges and judicial officers.

In a petition filed under a certificate of urgency, Advocate Adrian Kamotho has sued LSK led by President Charles Kanjama, over its nationwide and targeted court boycott of Chief Justice Martha Koome, Deputy Chief Justice Philomena Mwilu and other judges, arguing that the action is unconstitutional, undermines judicial independence and denies litigants access to justice.

"The LSK's actions create the impression that lawful court orders can be overturned through a boycott, setting a dangerous precedent to the rule of law and thereby undermining the proper administration of justice," Kamotho states in the petition.

The lawyer has named the Judicial Service Commission (JSC), Chief Justice Martha Koome, Deputy Chief Justice Mwilu, several Supreme Court, High Court and Environment and Land Court judges, Court of Appeal Judge Sankale Ole Kantai, Kibera Chief Magistrate Stella Atambo and the Kenya Magistrates and Judges Association as interested parties in the case.

He is seeking orders to immediately suspend the implementation of the LSK's targeted boycott announced through statements and operational guidelines issued on July 17, July 20 and July 22, 2026, pending the hearing and determination of the petition.

"Pending the hearing and determination of this Petition, the court be pleased to issue a conservatory order restraining the LSK, whether by itself, its Council, officers, agents or any person acting under its authority, from implementing, enforcing or giving effect to the targeted boycott," Kamotho seeks.

According to the petition, the targeted boycott, which commenced on July 23, directs advocates not to participate in fresh hearings, part-heard matters or new applications before judges listed by the LSK.

East Africa Law Society president Ramadhan Abubakar Mukira addresses the media on the court boycott outside the Supreme Court of Kenya in Nairobi on July 22, 2026. [Benard Orwongo, Standard]

Lawyers are also required to seek adjournments, transfers or recusals of matters regardless of their clients' instructions.

"The Respondent has directed advocates not to participate in fresh hearings, part-heard matters or new applications before the listed judges and judicial officers," Kamotho states.

He adds: "Advocates appearing before the targeted judges and judicial officers have been directed to seek the transfer, recusal or adjournment of pending proceedings, irrespective of their clients' instructions, the circumstances of the individual case or the applicable legal principles."

Kamotho further claims the society has threatened disciplinary action against judges, judicial officers and advocates who decline to implement the boycott.

"The LSK has further directed that any judge, judicial officer or advocate who declines to facilitate the boycott be reported to it for 'appropriate action,' including possible complaints before the Judicial Service Commission and such further action as its Council may deem necessary," he says.

According to the petition, every day the boycott remains in force exposes court users to delayed justice and unnecessary hardship.

"Every day that the targeted boycott remains operative exposes litigants and court users to adjournments, disruption of part-heard proceedings, expiry of interim protection measures, prolonged detention, additional expense and denial or delay of access to justice," Kamotho argues.

He also faults the LSK for allegedly including the late Supreme Court Judge Mohammed Ibrahim in its list of judges affected by the boycott.

"The targeted list of judges includes Hon. Justice Mohammed Ibrahim (deceased), demonstrating unconscionable casualness on the part of the LSK and apparent failure to verify elementary material facts before imposing measures of such gravity," the petition states.

Kamotho contends that the boycott creates an unlawful mechanism for exerting pressure on judges outside the constitutional framework.

He argues that the dispute raises fundamental constitutional questions, including whether the LSK has the legal authority to organise an indefinite boycott, compel advocates to withhold legal services from clients and determine which judicial functions judges may perform.

He maintains that the boycott threatens litigants' constitutional rights to equality before the law, access to justice, legal representation and a fair hearing, particularly in urgent and criminal matters.

In his supporting affidavit, Kamotho says advocates have been placed in an impossible position by the LSK's directives.

"The directions therefore place advocates in an immediate and irreconcilable conflict between their lawful professional duties and the Respondent's threatened enforcement measures," he says.

He further says litigants are innocent parties caught in an institutional dispute.

"The practical burden of the boycott consequently falls upon litigants and court users who are strangers to the institutional dispute forming the alleged basis of the boycott," he states.

Kamotho insists the conservatory orders sought are intended only to preserve uninterrupted court operations and judicial independence pending determination of the constitutional petition, arguing that the public interest favours continued access to courts and legal representation rather than disruption of judicial proceedings.

The petition is pending directions and hearing.

World.title: Ruto: Government will deal firmly with criminals
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto arrive for the consecration of Rev. Vitalis Job Ekuru as the fourth Bishop of the ACK Diocese of Katakwa in Busia County on July 26, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has declared war on individuals who involve in violence, destruction of property and political intimidation.

He said people initially participated in anti-government demonstrations have "graduated from protesters to goons."

Speaking on Sunday during the consecration of Rev. Vitalis Job Ekuru as the fourth Bishop of the ACK Diocese of Katakwa in Busia County, the President said the government would no longer tolerate criminality disguised as peaceful protests.

"They have now graduated from protesters to goons. They are bringing chaos everywhere," Ruto said.

President Ruto maintained that safeguarding peace remains the government's top priority while ensuring all leaders have the freedom to campaign without fear of violence or intimidation.

He argued that Kenya had previously experienced a rise in criminal activities, but efforts to deal with those responsible had been complicated by differing opinions over how security agencies should respond.

"We had a small problem earlier when crime issues increased and we did not agree on how to tackle the crime as a nation because sometimes we used to defend those who were hurting people and destroying property. We could say that they should not be touched because they are our children," he said.

"But now we have seen the repercussions because they have now graduated from protesters to goons. They are bringing chaos everywhere."

Ruto said the government had resolved to restore law and order, insisting that criminal gangs would not be allowed to disrupt peace under the cover of political demonstrations.

"We have agreed to discipline all the goons, and no one will be allowed to propagate crime and disrupt peace in our country," he said.

The President also sought to reassure Kenyans that the country would remain peaceful as preparations begin for the 2027 General Election, saying his administration would do everything possible to safeguard stability before, during and after the polls.

"I agree that peace is not negotiable. All of us, irrespective of who we are, our persuasion, our political leaning and whatever it is that we believe in, we must have a peaceful nation," Ruto said.

"I want to assure you as the people of Kenya that we will have peaceful elections next year because elections come and go, but this nation must remain firm, united and stable. We shall do everything possible to ensure that this nation is stable."

At the same time, the Head of State emphasized that every political leader should be free to campaign and present their agenda without intimidation, provided they conduct their activities peacefully.

"Every leader should be given a chance to give their opinion. Those who have an agenda or plan should be given an opportunity to explain it to Kenyans. Even those who have nothing should be given a chance to speak, but all of us must ensure that we are peaceful," he said.

The President's remarks come against the backdrop of heightened political tensions and growing concerns over violent disruptions at political gatherings.

Recent incidents, including the Ol Kalou by-election in Nyandarua County, saw armed gangs disrupt voting and terrorize residents, prompting renewed debate over the role of criminal groups in Kenya's political landscape.

The government has faced criticism from sections of the opposition, who have accused state agencies of sponsoring the gangs.

However, Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has rejected the claims, instead alleging that the groups were mobilized by allies of former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua. Murkomen has pledged decisive action against those behind the violence, regardless of their political affiliation.

World.title: Ruiru 'Vampire' arrested after lodging incident with woman
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The suspect was arrested after an angry mob cornered and assaulted him near the Powerstar area in Ruiru town following weeks of attacks that had spread fear among residents. [Courtesy, X]

Police in Ruiru have arrested a 35-year-old man believed to be behind a series of bizarre and violent attacks in which residents were robbed and bitten, leaving several victims nursing serious injuries.

The suspect, identified as Githaiga from Mugutha, was arrested on Saturday afternoon after an angry mob cornered and assaulted him near the Powerstar area in Ruiru town following weeks of attacks that had spread fear among residents.

Ruiru Sub-County Police Commander Charles Kibathi confirmed the arrest, saying the suspect was heavily intoxicated at the time and had allegedly bitten a woman who was with him, tearing part of her lower lip.

"The suspect and the female victim were taken to hospital for treatment as investigations continue," Kibathi said.

He added that detectives are investigating whether the suspect is linked to the earlier attacks reported in Ruiru and neighbouring Gitothua Ward.

However, some residents defended the suspect, claiming the altercation that led to the woman being bitten stemmed from a disagreement after the two emerged from a room where they had spent the night.

Kibathi assured residents that police are pursuing all leads to establish whether other people may have been involved in the attacks and pledged to intensify security operations in the area.

The arrest follows weeks of panic after several residents reported being attacked by a man who allegedly robbed victims before violently biting them.

Among the latest victims was Daniel Ndegwa, who was attacked on July 11 at about 9 p.m. while walking to a nearby shopping centre. Ndegwa told police he was confronted by a man demanding his mobile phone before a struggle ensued. During the confrontation, the attacker bit his finger and injured his left hand. A friend who was accompanying him was also reportedly bitten.

Residents said the attacks had become increasingly frequent throughout July, forcing many people to avoid walking outside after dark.

In one of the most shocking incidents, another victim reportedly suffered severe facial injuries after the attacker allegedly bit off part of his cheek.

The incidents have disrupted normal life in Ruiru town and Gitothua Ward, with many residents opting to remain indoors in the evenings for fear of being attacked.

Residents, led by Severino Githinji, criticized the security situation, saying families have been living in constant fear and called for increased police patrols and swift action against those responsible.

Police said the first official report of the attacks was made on July 11, and investigations are ongoing to establish whether the arrested suspect is responsible for all the reported incidents.

Kibathi urged members of the public to continue cooperating with investigators as detectives work to unravel the full circumstances surrounding the attacks.

World.title: Murkomen: Police no longer rely on Gachagua's 'gossip'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen during the official launch of the Multi-biometric Identification System (MBIS) and handover ceremony of ANSI National Accreditation Board Certificate at DCI Headquarters on July 23, 2026. [NPS]

Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has accused former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua of spreading falsehoods, saying technology-driven policing has replaced "gossip-based" investigations.

Speaking during the handover of the ANSI National Accreditation Board certification to the Forensic Evidence Management Unit and the launch of the Multi-Biometric Identification System at the Directorate of Criminal Investigations headquarters on Thursday, Murkomen said the country has shifted from outdated investigative methods to science-based policing.

"We are moving away from gossip-based collection of evidence to science. I saw an impeached former leader claiming he is well connected to police officers and receives gossip every day because he is not busy unlike the President," said Murkomen.

He said the biometric system will strengthen investigations through science and technology, making unofficial information unnecessary.

"That is an old style of collecting evidence. We now have a modern police service driven by science and technology. We do not need his gossip to run the National Police Service," he observed.

Murkomen claimed the technology would make it harder for unsuitable individuals to rise through public office.

"If these systems had been in place many years ago, people like Gachagua would not have survived the system as habitual offenders until he slipped through to become Deputy President. Such things will never happen again with this technological advancement," said Murkomen.

The Interior CS defended Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja, saying he has the government's confidence and has discharged his duties professionally.

"I have full support and faith in the leadership of the Inspector General. He has carried out his duties with dignity, honour and respect for the citizens of Kenya and his office," noted Murkomen.

Murkomen also rejected Gachagua's criticism of police leadership, arguing that Kenya is recording fewer cases of terrorism, banditry, robbery and other crimes.

"There has never been a period when Kenya has recorded fewer incidents of terrorism, banditry, robberies and other crimes. Our security agencies are working together and have improved security," he said.

He also criticised remarks attributed to Gachagua warning tourists against visiting Kenya, saying they damage the country's reputation.

"For anyone to stand out there and say Kenya is not safe and tourists should not come to our country is very embarrassing," explained Murkomen.

Murkomen dismissed claims that 68 women were raped by police officers during the Ol Kalou parliamentary by-election, urging anyone with evidence to report the matter to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations, the Independent Policing Oversight Authority or the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights.

"If those incidents occurred, they should be reported so those responsible can be held accountable. If not, those making such reckless statements must also be held accountable," said Murkomen.

He accused Gachagua of making the allegations out of political desperation.

"I know why Gachagua speaks the way he does. It is because of desperation. Knowing that he cannot hold any office again in Kenya and can never be President of this republic, he wants to take the entire nation, including the economy, down the drain with himself. We will not allow that," he said.

Murkomen also urged media organisations to challenge politicians they host instead of allowing false claims to go unchecked.

"We should not feed Kenyans with lies. I want to tell media houses that when you invite such reckless human beings, please carry with you a lie detector. Otherwise you are going to mislead the people of Kenya and drive bad behaviour in our country," said Murkomen.

He maintained that intelligence gathering within the National Police Service follows lawful procedures and dismissed claims that private individuals receive confidential police briefings outside official channels

World.title: Gachagua: Why Ruto will not steal the 2027 General Election
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Righathi Gachagua during a live interview with KTN at his Karen home, Nairobi. [Kanyiri Wahito, Standard]

Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has claimed that President William Ruto will not be able to manipulate the outcome of the 2027 General Election, arguing that Kenyans have become more vigilant in protecting their votes.

Speaking during a live interview with KTN from his Karen residence, the former Deputy President said the recent Ol Kalou by-election had provided opposition supporters with a blueprint on safeguarding the electoral process.

"Voting is not enough; you vote and protect the vote. We now have a template from the Ol Kalou by-election," Gachagua said.

He urged Kenyans to remain vigilant during the next General Election, saying the alleged intimidation witnessed in Ol Kalou had failed to influence voters.

"They tried intimidating the people of Ol Kalou, but they did not succeed. We are celebrating what happened, and people from across the country are calling to benchmark on how it worked," he said.

Gachagua also questioned the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC)'s ability to conduct a free and fair election, accusing the electoral body of failing to condemn alleged voter suppression and bribery during the Ol Kalou by-election.

"IEBC has not even condemned the wrongs that happened during the by-election in Ol Kalou. We lost two people who were actually protecting our votes," he alleged.

The DCP leader further renewed his criticism of President Ruto, accusing him of betraying voters from the Mt Kenya region despite earlier warnings.

According to Gachagua, the outcome of the Ol Kalou by-election should serve as a warning to the Kenya Kwanza administration ahead of the 2027 General Election.

He maintained that the by-election demonstrated that Kenyans could no longer be intimidated by the State and described the result as a preview of what to expect in the next national polls.

Gachagua also revisited the Mbeere North by-election, alleging that DCP lost because of widespread voter bribery, intimidation of elderly voters and failure by the party to adequately protect its votes.

"We lost the Mbeere North by-election because we didn't protect our votes properly. There was also massive voter bribery, and those who participated were allegedly given the balance of their bribe after showing a photo of whom they had voted for," he claimed.

The former Deputy President further argued that DCP would have secured an even larger victory in Ol Kalou were it not for what he described as voter suppression and police intimidation.



More to follow...

World.title: Charles Owino appointed as Government Spokesperson
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

President William Ruto has promoted Government Spokesperson Isaac Mwaura in a fresh round of changes within the Executive, while also making nominations to key constitutional commissions and statutory bodies.

In an Executive Order issued on Tuesday, Chief of Staff and Head of Public Service Felix Koskei said the Public Service Commission had approved promotions and redeployments affecting senior government officials.

Under the changes, Mwaura was promoted and redesignated as the Head of the Office of Diversity, Inclusion and Disability Rights in the Executive Office of the President.

Charles Owino Wahong’o was redeployed from the Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy to the Executive Office of the President, where he will serve as Acting Head of Government Communications.

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

At the same time, Ruto also nominated new office holders to key constitutional commissions and approved changes within the senior ranks of the Executive in a fresh round of appointments aimed at filling vacancies and strengthening government institutions.

Among the nominees is Dr. Duncan Ojwang Oburu, who has been picked to serve as the Chairperson of the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA).

Ruto also nominated Ms. Antonina Lentoijoni and former Kenya National Union of Teachers (KNUT) Secretary-General Wilson Sossion as members of the Teachers Service Commission (TSC).

Ms. Flora Mutua was nominated as a member of the Public Service Commission (PSC).

In the nominations, Ruto also named seven individuals to serve on the Intergovernmental Relations Technical Committee (IGRTC), subject to ratification by the National and County Government Co-ordinating Summit in accordance with the Intergovernmental Relations Act.

The nominees are Wilson Kuria Thuita (Murang'a), Silvya C. Apaa (Busia), Ahmed Kanyara Bishar (Wajir), Pascalyne Ntang'enoi Kimiriri (Laikipia), Ken Riaga (Migori), Evalyn Chepkirui Aruasa (Nakuru) and Mary Nanjala Kilobi (Nairobi).

World.title: Iran has not sought talks with US over past two weeks, official says
World.content:
Iran has not sought negotiations with the United States over the past two weeks and will not relinquish control of the Hormuz Strait, a senior Iranian official said yesterday, hours before the country launched a fresh round of missile attacks against US bases in Jordan.

US President Donald Trump had claimed that Iran was “dying for a negotiation,” Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said. But he painted a very different picture in an interview on Iranian television late Tuesday.

“We have sent no request for negotiation with the US during the past 16–17 days,” he said.

Control of the Strait of Hormuz has become a key issue in the conflict between Iran and the United States, which has insisted that freedom of navigation must be restored through the critical waterway, through which more than one-fifth of the world’s oil is normally carried.

“If the Strait of Hormuz returns to its previous state, our success in this war is not complete,” Gharibabadi said.

US warships were not allowed to come near the Strait, he said, because demining the sea-lanes was Iran’s responsibility according to the Memorandum of Understanding signed last month.

“The Omanis wanted to bring in a country to conduct mine-clearing operations in the southern part of the Strait of Hormuz, but we did not allow it.” Gharibabadi asserted.

He also suggested that Iran retained the right to charge fees for passage.

The MoU obliged Iran “to provide safe passage for commercial ships, free of charge, for only 60 days,” he said.

Negotiations with Oman over a new regime for the Strait have continued through the month, but are yet to resolve the issue.

World.title: FIFA plan for Kushner-backed $20 billion operation to run World Cup meets fury from Europe’s UEFA
World.content:
Geneva AP — FIFA President FIFA President Gianni Infantino ’s plan to create a $20 billion company running the World Cup with private investors, including the Kushner family, was announced Tuesday — and immediately attacked by European soccer body UEFA

“It is not FIFA’s to sell,” UEFA said in a statement. “None of us are the owners of football.”

Infantino’s plans to form a commercial subsidiary, which would be called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), running competitions like the World Cup and Club World Cup was first reported by The Times of London.

FIFA said in a statement FFE would raise up to $4.2 billion later this year to help fund development programs “based on an initial equity valuation of $20 billion by carefully selecting long-term investors who will purchase minority, non-controlling interests.”

FIFA is working with J.P. Morgan while intended investors include Thrive Eternal launched by Joshua Kushner, whose brother Jared Kushner is a son-in-law of U.S. President Donald Trump.

The men’s World Cup that finished this month only deepened the political and personal ties between Trump and Infantino, and fueled concerns about those ties, including from UEFA.

“The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade — especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially,” UEFA said Tuesday, responding to the reports of selling stakes in FIFA competitions.

FIFA is currently a Swiss-based not-for-profit association of its 211 national member federations worldwide.

Those members must approve any plan and would get the chance “to access up to $20 million in one-off capital,” FIFA said.

“This is about the democratization of football worldwide,” Infantino said in a FIFA statement, which added that “a consultation process has begun.”

UEFA, however, said it took reports of the project “extremely seriously. So should every national Football Association.”

“This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross,” said UEFA, which comprises 55 of the FIFA members.

FIFA’s $20M offer to member federations

The outline of Tuesday’s surprise announcement was, FIFA said, detailed by Infantino to members who met in Manhattan on July 18 ahead of the World Cup final. There, Infantino promised to “unleash the commercial potential and opportunity that FIFA has.”

FIFA’s statement Tuesday about its proposed project led on how much money each of its 211 members could get through 2038 in the “FIFA Fast-Forward Program.”

Instead of the currently promised $8 million each in development funds through the 2027-30 World Cup commercial cycle, it would be $20 million, then $22 million and $24 million in the following cycles.

The World Cup trophy was awarded to Spain on July 19. Vincent Carchietta/Imagn Images/Reuters

FIFA banked record World Cup income of about $12 billion from the 2026 tournament which had unprecedented high prices for tickets and hospitality across the US, Canada and Mexico. It already was unclear how that money could be matched from Spain, Portugal and Morocco co-hosting the 2030 men’s edition.

Member federations could choose if they wanted to take part in the new financial opportunities, FIFA said.

“FIFA would retain sole control of FFE and exclusive authority over football governance, competitions, match calendar, and all regulatory and sporting decisions,” the soccer body said.

FIFA’s integrity standards were called into question during the World Cup, including by team coaches, Norway’s soccer federation and a top European public body, the Council of Europe.

FIFA’s previous attempt to privatize assets

The project announced Tuesday is the second time in Infantino’s increasingly controversial 11-year presidency he has tried to push through a multi-billion dollar deal with private backers.

In 2018, Infantino proposed a secretive $25 billion offer over 12 years with SoftBank of Japan to create new global competitions, including an expanded men’s Club World Cup, seemingly backed by Saudi Arabian money.

That ultimately failed after meeting fierce resistance from UEFA, which saw threats to its prize assets: the Champions League and the European Championship.

Infantino still built closer ties to Saudi soccer and the kingdom’s Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman. Saudi Arabia will host the 2034 World Cup and largely funded the revamped men’s Club World Cup hosted in the U.S. last year.

Infantino’s future?

The financial success of the just-ended World Cup has looked likely to ensure Infantino is re-elected next year unopposed for a fourth and final term in office through 2031.

At his re-election by acclaim in 2023 in Rwanda, Infantino suggested any CEO delivering similar financial results would be kept in the job forever.

Speculation has swirled for years Infantino might want a different global role in soccer beyond his FIFA presidency, which is due to end when he is 61.

The Times reported Tuesday that a CEO-like commissioner role of the new FFE operation could be created for Infantino.

“This has never been discussed,” FIFA said in a statement Tuesday. “However, the FIFA president and the FIFA administration will and must have leading roles in this entity — if approved.”

There was no timetable suggested Tuesday for debate and decisions by FIFA, its ruling Council chaired by Infantino, and the 211 members.

FIFA is scheduled to hold an online congress on Nov. 23 to confirm hosts of the Women’s World Cup editions in 2031 and 2035.

World.title: Apple will now let you lease your next iPhone or Mac instead of buying it
World.content:
There are plenty of things you can lease: a car, an apartment or an office space, for example. Now you can add your next iPhone to that list.

Apple is launching a new leasing program to make iPhones, Macs and other products feel more affordable at a time when electronics prices are climbing and consumers are holding onto devices longer.

Apple is partnering with payment platform Klarna on the program, which will be available in the United States starting Tuesday through retail locations, online and in the Apple Store app. iPhones and Apple Watches can be leased on either a 12- or 24-month basis, while Macs and iPads will have a 24- or 36-month lease term.

Eligible products include:

iPhone 17 lineup

iPhone Air

Apple Watch Series 11

Apple Watch Ultra 3

MacBook Air

MacBook Pro

iMac

Mac Studio

iPad Air

iPad Pro

iPad Mini

Apple’s cheaper products — like the iPhone 16, MacBook Neo, base iPad and Apple Watch SE — are not part of the program.

This new leasing plan replaces the iPhone Upgrade Program, which allowed consumers to swap out iPhones after making 12 monthly payments. The new plan aims to apply a similar concept to a broader range of Apple products while offering more flexibility in payment plans and lower monthly costs.

The cheapest iPhone leasing option costs $17.99 per month, while the iPhone upgrade plan starts at about $42 per month, according to Apple’s website.

The program could help consumers think about an iPhone or Mac as another subscription rather than a big-ticket purchase, according to Francisco Jeronimo, an analyst for market research firm International Data Corporation. Most Americans no longer upgrade their phone every year: The average user keeps their phone for 22 months, according to a survey last year from Reviews.org.

Meanwhile, some analysts expect Apple’s next batch of iPhones to cost more. Last month, Apple raised prices on a range of devices, including certain Mac and iPad models, because of an ongoing memory shortage from increasing demand for data centers.

“We should start thinking about a $1,500 iPhone instead of a $1,000 (or) $1,200 iPhone,” Mike Howard, vice president of memory coverage at research firm TechInsights, told CNN earlier this month.

The new leasing program debuts ahead of Apple’s anticipated iPhone launch in September. The company is expected to release what will likely be its most expensive smartphone yet: the first foldable iPhone, according to Bloomberg.

“Apple’s real risk is that rising prices even further can impact the upgrade cycle,” Jeronimo said in a statement last week after Bloomberg reported on the leasing program.

“Apple Upgrade lands at precisely the moment Apple needs it,” he said.

World.title: US-Saudi strikes in Iraq kill at least 20, wound 32, Iran-aligned militia says
World.content:
At least 20 people have been killed and 32 wounded after US and Saudi Arabian forces conducted joint strikes against Iran-linked “logistics and weapons sites” in Iraq, according to a statement posted on Telegram from the Popular Mobilization Forces.

The attacks targeted PMF facilities in the provinces of Baghdad, Wasit, Nineveh, Basra, Kirkuk, Karbala, and Diyala, the PMF said, causing varying degrees of damage to several military headquarters, vehicles, and equipment.

In an earlier statement on social media, the group’s 30th Brigade said seven airstrikes hit key sites in Nineveh, a region in northern Iraq, at around 3:20 a.m, local time – killing 10 and wounding six.

In response to the strikes, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi has convened an emergency meeting of the Ministerial Council for National Security Wednesday, according to a statement from his office.

World.title: Egypt claims 3 gold medals in African Archery Championship
World.content:
Egypt’s archery national team secured three gold medals on Tuesday at the 15th African Archery Championship in Oran, Algeria.

Ismail Ezz al-Din won gold in the U-18 men’s individual event, while Nourai al-Sayed claimed gold in the U-18 women’s individual competition.

The duo teamed up to capture a third gold in the U-18 mixed team event.

The tournament featured record-breaking performances by the Egyptian national team.

Ezz al-Din set a new African record in the U-18 men’s individual event with 650 points.

Ezz al-Din and al-Sayed also set an African record in the U-18 mixed team competition, scoring 1,258 points.

The Egyptian delegation includes Ali Abdel-Barr, Bahaa Ali, Ismail Ezz al-Din, Abdel-Rahman Hani and Nourai al-Sayed, alongside technical director Dr. Maged Mohie.

The delegation is headed by board member of the Egyptian Archery Federation Reham Soweilem.

World.title: Egypt, Cyprus discuss strengthening energy cooperation
World.content:
Minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources Karim Badawi met Cypriot Ambassador to Egypt Polly Ioannou to discuss accelerating joint natural gas projects and expanding cooperation in the mining sector.

Badawi said that Egypt and Cyprus have made steady progress in developing Cypriot gas fields and connecting them to Egypt’s gas infrastructure through partnerships with major international energy companies.

He said that the projects will strengthen Egypt’s role as a regional energy hub, support regional energy security and increase gas exports to European markets.

The minister also reviewed recent reforms aimed at improving Egypt’s mining investment climate, saying they have attracted new international interest.

He added that cooperation with Cypriot companies is expected to grow as investment opportunities expand.

The two sides also discussed the return of Cyprus-based FMC to resume gold and mineral exploration in Egypt’s Eastern Desert, while Ioannou said the company plans to expand its operations.

She added that another Cypriot company is studying investment opportunities in Egypt’s marine bunkering sector.

At the end of the meeting, Badawi thanked Ioannou for her efforts to strengthen Egypt-Cyprus relations ahead of the conclusion of her diplomatic mission.

World.title: PM: Government committed to expanding Egypt’s oil, gas sector
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly reaffirmed the government’s commitment to expanding Egypt’s oil and natural gas sector, describing it as a vital pillar of the national economy and a major driver of energy security, investment and economic growth.

During a meeting in New Alamein City with Minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources Karim Badawi, Madbouly stressed the importance of increasing domestic production, attracting more investment and accelerating exploration activities to maximize the country’s natural resources.

Badawi reviewed progress on several strategic oil and gas projects being carried out with international energy companies. He said these projects are expected to increase the value of Egypt’s natural resources, support local industries, reduce imports and expand exports.

The minister also welcomed the final investment decision (FID) by Eni and TotalEnergies to develop Cyprus’ Cronos gas field and connect it to Egypt’s energy infrastructure. Under the project, gas from the Cypriot field will be transported to Egypt for processing and liquefaction at the Damietta LNG plant before being exported to European markets, further strengthening Egypt’s position as a regional energy hub.

For his part, Badawi said that Egypt’s crude oil production has reached its highest level in two years, driven by higher investment and expanded exploration following the settlement of overdue payments to international energy partners.

He added that the ministry successfully secured natural gas supplies during the recent period of peak electricity demand caused by high summer temperatures and has completed preparations to ensure stable supplies throughout the rest of the summer.

The minister also announced a new natural gas discovery in the Western Desert through the deep exploratory Wanda well, which is expected to produce around 40 million cubic feet of gas per day, supporting Egypt’s plans to increase domestic production and strengthen long-term energy security.

World.title: PM reviews plan to raise incentives for university academic staff
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly reviewed on Tuesday measures to increase incentives for academic staff of universities and research centers.

This came during a meeting chaired by the prime minister on Tuesday to discuss ways and mechanisms to increase incentives for faculty members at universities and research centers. The meeting was attended by Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk, Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research and Acting Minister of Culture Abdelaziz Konsowa, as well as officials from both ministries.

The discussions also covered the financial requirements and implementation steps needed to introduce the proposed increase while ensuring consistency with the state budget.

Madbouly directed that the draft decision be finalized promptly for submission to the Cabinet for consideration.

World.title: Solwezi residents in full support of UPND-Mulusa
World.content:
Solwezi North Constituency United Party for National Development (UPND) aspiring candidate, Stafford Mulusa, says residents of North-western Province are in full support of the party and President Hakainde Hichilema.

Mr Mulusa has refuted claims that the party has lost popularity in the province, noting that people are happy with the works of the UPND administration and have confidence in the President and the party’s progressive reforms.

Speaking to the media in Solwezi District, Mr Mulusa said the development achieved in the last five years, is an indication of the current administration’s commitment towards economic transformation of the province and the country as a whole.

He indicated that unlike social media claims that North-western Province has been denied development, the province is on a path of greater transformation with on-going projects.

Mr Mulusa, who is Solwezi Central Constituency immediate past Member of Parliament, empasised that UPND is an action oriented party which stands on truth and hard work.

He added that President Hichilema’ investment in different sectors of the economy, is a clear indication of well-meaning leadership that puts the needs of citizens first.

He has urged Zambians to vote for the UPND and President Hichilema for continuity of good progressive policies.

Meanwhile, President Hakainde Hichilema has assured the people of Nangoma Constituency of a bright mining prospect for them, especially the youths.

President Hichilema says the mineral resources must benefit the local people noting that minerals should however, be extracted legally and in a safe environment.

Addressing the people of Nangoma Constituency in Senior Chief Shakumbila’s area, Mr Hichilema said government is working round the clock to establish a gold washing plant and market to ensure the local people sell their minerals at a profit.

“No parent would send children where they will die. We are not stopping you from mining, we want you to mine safely. We don’t want you to use mercury to clean your gold because it will pollute the environment and water sources,” Mr Hichilema said.

President Hichilema said government will open a gold washing plant and market as well as bring ZCCM to ensure the local people can mine safely and at a profit without polluting the environment and water bodies.

The President stressed that government is upgrading the Farmers – Nalubanda and Nangoma roads to the bituminous standard.

The Head of State urged the people of Nangoma to vote for all United Party for National Development (UPND) candidates for the sustenance of various social protection programmes.

He declared that once re-elected, he will ensure that the feeder roads in Nangoma Constituency are worked on to accelerate trade.

And Mr Hichilema said he will consider the appeal by Senior Chief Shakumbila of the Sala people of giving Nangoma Constituency a district status.

“His Royal Highness has caught me off guard. I have heard the appeal to upgrade Nangoma to a district hospital and I will look into that,” the President assured.

And Senior Chief Shakumbila of Mumbwa and Shibuyunji Districts in Central Province has endorsed President Hichilema for the August 13 General Elections.

The traditional leader has also urged his subjects to vote for all UPND candidates during the August polls.

The Chief said President Hichilema deserved a second term merited by various developmental projects in his chiefdom and employment of local youths into public service.

World.title: Commonwealth Games: Samukonga qualifies for 400m Semis ‎ ‎
World.content:
Team Zambia’s Muzala Samukonga has secured direct qualification to the Men’s 400m semi-finals at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games, placing him among the event’s eight fastest athletes.

‎

‎Speaking to the Commonwealth Games Association of Zambia – CGA Zambia Media Team, Samukonga expressed confidence in his preparations to defend the title he won in Birmingham four years ago.

‎

‎“I am more than prepared. I have been preparing for the Commonwealth Games for the past two years,” he said.

‎

‎The defending Commonwealth champion said he is in excellent condition and is looking forward to stepping onto the track with confidence.

‎

‎“I am okay, and I am going onto the track to enjoy myself and have fun,” Samukonga added.

‎

‎Reflecting on the challenge ahead, the Zambian sprint star acknowledged that retaining a title is often more demanding than winning it for the first time.

‎

‎“Becoming a champion is easy, but defending your title and remaining consistent is hard. I am praying to God to guide me through this journey, and I know He will,” he said.

‎

‎According to the National Olympic Committee of Zambia, Samukonga will compete in Men’s 400m Semi-Final Heat 2 on Thursday, 30 July, at 14:10 CAT at Scotstoun Stadium, where he will be aiming to secure a place in the final.

‎

‎Meanwhile, Team Zambia sprinter Edna Ng’andula’s quest for a place in the Women’s 200m final came to an unfortunate end after she was disqualified in the semi-final.

‎

‎Ng’andula had crossed the finish line in second place with a personal best time of 23.50 seconds, but was disqualified for stepping on the lane line during the race.

‎

‎She will now turn her attention to the mixed 4x400m Relay, where she will aim to help Team Zambia deliver another strong performance.

‎

‎In lawn bowls, Mildred Mkandawire lost in the Women’s Singles to Bridget Herselman of South Africa in straight sets, 13–1 and 8–4.

‎

‎Despite the setbacks, Team Zambia continues to compete with determination, resilience, and pride as the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games enter the decisive stages.

World.title: Manufacturing leads Zambia’s investment boom-ZDA
World.content:
The Zambia Association of Manufacturers (ZAM) has welcomed the Zambia Development Agency (ZDA) report showing that manufacturing attracted the largest share of actualised investments between 2021 and June 2026, describing the sector’s performance as evidence of Zambia’s growing attractiveness as an investment destination.

In a statement made available to the media today, ZAM President Mohammed Umar said ZDA recorded US$19.07 billion in actualised investments during the period, with the manufacturing sector accounting for US$7.33 billion, representing 38.5 per cent of the total investments and the highest among all sectors.

Mr Umar said the sector also created 46,759 actual jobs, making it the second largest contributor to employment among the sectors monitored.

He noted that the investment performance is consistent with data from the Zambia Statistics Agency, which shows manufacturing recorded positive growth throughout the review period, expanding by 4.7 per cent in 2022, 4.5 per cent in 2023, 2.3 per cent in 2024, 7.1 per cent in 2025 and 5.4 per cent in the first quarter of 2026.

“Sustained growth of this kind shows that rising investment is translating into real production capacity, value addition and employment, not simply commitments on paper,” Mr Umar said.

He added that manufacturing now contributes nearly 10 percent of Zambia’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and accounts for 10.4 per cent of Government tax revenue as of the first quarter of 2026.

Mr Umar attributed the sector’s resilience to sustained investor confidence despite challenges such as energy constraints caused by drought, limited access to affordable long-term finance and global economic uncertainty.

He further acknowledged government reforms, such as macroeconomic stabilisation, regulatory reforms, digitalisation of public services and strengthened public-private dialogue, for improving the country’s investment climate and supporting industrial growth.

He said ZAM will continue advocating for reliable and affordable electricity, lower business costs, access to competitively priced long-term finance, predictable tax policies, stronger implementation of local content policies, expanded market access and increased value addition.

Mr Umar also reaffirmed ZAM’s commitment to working with government and other stakeholders to strengthen the competitiveness of Zambia’s manufacturing sector and accelerate inclusive and sustainable industrial development.

World.title: Team win matters more than personal goals – Kundananji
World.content:
Copper Queens forward Rachael Kundananji says she is unfazed by not scoring as Zambia thumped Egypt 6-0 in their opening Group C match of the 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations on Tuesday night at the Olympic Stadium in Rabat, Morocco.

‎

‎Captain Barbra Banda scored four goals, with debutant Eneless Phiri and experienced player Rachael Nachula adding the others.

‎

‎In a post-match comment, Kundananji said Zambia’s win was more important than personal milestones.

‎

‎“You know there is a win, there are three points. Whether assist or no assist there are three points for Team Zambia. We are one team,” Kundananji said.

‎

‎“Scoring six goals in a game is not easy. It shows that working together as a team made it possible,” she added.

‎

‎She said the Copper Queens will remain focused as WAFCON advances.

‎

‎“We are in a tough group and scoring many goals is important and we are focused. We just want to do our best. We know what we want to achieve at this WAFCON,” Kundananji said.

‎

‎Zambia’s next Group C match will be against Nigeria on 1st August, while Egypt will face Malawi.

‎

‎The top four semifinalists at WAFCON will earn automatic qualification to the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil.

‎

‎The Copper Queens are aiming to better their 2022 WAFCON bronze medal achievement won under the late coach Bruce Mwape.

World.title: Youths urged to participate in electoral process
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) has called on young people in Western Province to take keen interest in the electoral process ahead of the August 2026 General Elections.

Provincial Elections Officer, Nixon Nkwapu, says meaningful youth participation is critical to strengthening democracy and ensuring credible elections.

Mr Nkwapu was speaking during a civic education engagement with youth groups in Mongu.

“The Commission is urging the youths in the province to take keen interest in understanding the electoral process ahead of the August 2026 elections,” he said.

He emphasised that young people have a vital role to play beyond just voting.

“We are emphasising the importance of youth’s contribution to the electoral processes in a meaningful manner. The active participation of youth will promote and enhance democracy in the country,” Mr Nkwapu stated.

The Provincial Elections Officer also took time to explain recent constitutional reforms aimed at increasing representation of marginalised groups.

Mr Nkwapu explained the provision for the 40 seats of proportional representation for women, youths, and persons with disabilities as provided for under Constitution Amendment Act No. 13 of 2025.

“The amendment is meant to ensure that women, youths and persons with disability are adequately represented in political positions and in decision-making,” he said.

Mr Nkwapu further reiterated the Commission’s commitment to public education and transparency.

“The Commission remains committed to providing information to the public about the electoral process so that every eligible voter, especially the youth, can participate effectively,” he added.

The ECZ says it will continue rolling out voter education programmes across all districts in the province in the lead-up to the 2026 elections.

World.title: Copper Queens kick off WAFCON in style
World.content:
The Zambia Women’s Senior National Team has started its Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) campaign in Morocco on a high note.

Zambia defeated Egypt 6–0, with Rachael Nachula opening the scoring from the penalty spot in the 25th minute after Copper Queens captain Barbra Banda was brought down in the 18-yard box by Egyptian defender Ibrahim.

The Nora Häuptle-coached side created numerous scoring opportunities but failed to convert several chances before the referee blew the whistle for halftime in an entertaining match played at the Olympic Stadium in Rabat on Tuesday.

In the 58th minute of the second half, Banda scored her first goal of the match from the penalty spot after the referee awarded Zambia a penalty for a handball by an Egyptian defender following Prisca Chilufya’s cross into the box.

Shortly afterwards, Banda headed home her second goal to give the Copper Queens a 3–0 lead. She completed her hat-trick in the 85th minute with another well-taken finish.

Eneless Phiri added Zambia’s fifth goal in stoppage time with a powerful strike from outside the penalty area after exchanging passes with Banda.

Banda then sealed the emphatic 6–0 victory by scoring her fourth goal of the match three minutes before the final whistle.

Zambia now tops Group C with 3 points, which also includes Nigeria, Egypt and Malawi.

World.title: Verification and validation of FSP beneficiaries commence in Kaoma
World.content:
The Department of Community Development under the Food Security Pack has commenced the verification and validation of beneficiaries to be enrolled for another three-year programme where they will receive farming inputs.

The exercise follows a successful recruitment exercise that was conducted early this year.

Community Development Officers in Kaoma are on the ground to conduct the exercise, following the receipt of inputs that are due for distribution.

Leading the team, Community Development Officer, Mwanida Mukosayi, disclosed in an interview with the media that Kaoma district has a total of 2,044 beneficiaries who are classified as vulnerable but viable.

Mrs Mukosayi revealed that the district has since received inputs under both wetlands and rain-fed packages for the beneficiaries.

She said the department could not start the distribution before beneficiaries are verified in order to avoid duplication with the Ministry of Agriculture.

“It is a crime for any person to benefit both under the Farmer Input Support Programme and the Food Security Pack because they are similar government empowerment programmes aimed at uplifting people’s livelihoods and alleviating poverty,” Mrs Mukosayi explained.

She further stated that each farmer, depending on their location, will be given 5kg of maize seed, one bag of Compound D fertilizer, one bag of Urea fertilizer, groundnut seed, vegetable seed and compensation.

Mrs Mukosayi said distribution will be done immediately after verification is completed.

She has since appealed to beneficiaries not to divert the seeds for purposes other than those intended.

One of the beneficiaries, Bella Munyama from Mwanche area commended the government for the programme, saying it aims to improve livelihoods.

Ms Munyama explained how difficult it was for her to venture into agriculture due to lack of farming inputs and said her household lacked enough food to feed for her family.

“Hunger is now out of my household because with the seeds that I will be given I am able to grow, harvest, sell some and have money to buy other necessities” she said.

Another beneficiary, Monde Nawa, from Kaoma Ndonga area said after harvesting, she will be able to support her children with both food and school requirements.

Ms Nawa assured the government that the inputs will be put to good use.

Food Security Pack (FSP) is a social protection programme run by the government through the Department of Community Development under the Ministry of Community Development and Social Services.

The programme targets the most vulnerable but viable households who cannot afford farming inputs on their own. The goal is to help them become self-reliant in food production and improve their livelihoods.

World.title: Chilubi Pastors Fellowship commends government
World.content:
The Pastors Fellowship in Chilubi District in Northern Province has commended the government for making key strides towards economic transformation.

Pastors Fellowship Chairperson, Charles Katongo, says the country is on the right trajectory under President Hakainde Hichilema’s leadership as the county has seen economic stability.

Pastor Katongo notes that the policies of the government are reflective of efforts to spearhead prosperity.

He said this when Republican Vice President, Mutale Nalumango, met the clergy at Chilubi Mainland Boarding Secondary School today.

“We are able to see that the country is on the right track because President Hakainde Hichilema’s plans are to see Zambia prosper, which is what we are seeing today” he said.

Pastor Katongo also thanked the government for recognising the clergy as partners in governance through its all-inclusive policies.

And Mrs Nalumango said men of God are key partners in development saying both government and the church serve the interest of the people.

She further urged the church to promote Christian values in society.

“The church being the salt of the world should impact society with Christ-like character if our country is to be a better place,” Mrs Nalumango said.

The Vice President also appealed to the church to continue preaching peace, love and unity as the country heads to August 13, General Elections.

Mrs Nalumango said Zambians should not allow politics to divide them but instead remain united.

And speaking during a meeting with civil servants, Mrs Nalumango, said implementation of the Free-Education Policy which has now become law, has brought about inclusivity.

She observed that the policy which is now law has enabled even children from poor households to attain education.

Mrs Nalumango is on a five day working visit to Northern Province and is tomorrow expected to hold meetings in Nsama and Mporokoso Districts.
