World.title: “En el rap, destaca el que tiene más ingenio. Lo que hacemos tiene un verdadero peso cultural”
World.content:
Arkano, el adolescente que descubrió su identidad gracias al rap. Conversaciones sobre la educación que queremos | Pensemos el mañana (Episodio 2)

Arkano, rapero y referente del ‘freestyle’ en España, se sienta a conversar con Bohemia, una joven promesa de la improvisación, sobre cómo el error forma parte del aprendizaje, cómo gestionar las críticas y cómo la educación colabora en crear mejores artistas urbanos

Guillermo Rodríguez 'Arkano' Artista de rap Su trayectoria reúne algunos de los grandes hitos del freestyle desde que, con 15 años, se proclamó campeón de España de la Red Bull Batalla de los Gallos de 2009. Incluso batió un récord Guinness al improvisar durante 24 horas y 34 minutos seguidos. Paralelamente, impulsa y participa en iniciativas sobre salud mental y colabora en campañas contra el acoso escolar Isabel Arrabal 'Bohemia' Estudiante de 3º de ESO Y ‘freestyler’ A sus 15 años, compagina los estudios en el IES Averroes (Córdoba) con sus primeras competiciones de freestyle. Empezó a improvisar con 14 años, tras descubrir el rap en YouTube, y forma parte de una nueva generación de jóvenes que ha encontrado en la cultura urbana un lugar donde desarrollar su confianza

Dice Arkano (Alicante, 32 años) que el rap le transformó, que incluso le salvó la vida. A los 15 años, cuando aún lo conocían más como Guillermo Rodríguez y todavía cursaba la ESO, ganó en España la Red Bull Batalla de los Gallos, la competición de improvisación más importante del país. “Yo era un chaval muy tímido, no tenía habilidades sociales, lo pasé bastante mal en la época del instituto y descubrir el rap fue como encontrar una voz propia”, cuenta. La cultura urbana le alumbró, le infundió más confianza.

“El 'freestyle' se basa en lanzarse al vacío, no podemos aspirar a que todo sea perfecto. Tenemos que estar preparados para el error”

Isabel Arrabal, conocida como Bohemia, tiene la misma edad que tenía Arkano cuando se coronó como una joven promesa. No es su única coincidencia; esta cordobesa también ha ganado seguridad en sí misma después de atreverse a rapear. En Pensemos el mañana, el proyecto de Fundación Unicaja y Grupo Prisa sobre la educación del futuro, reflexionan sobre cómo han podido desarrollarse gracias a sus inquietudes artísticas y a esos entornos sociales fuera de las aulas, no convencionales.

"El rap me ayudó mucho a relacionarme con mis compañeros, a tener más seguridad en lo que hago, porque antes era muy tímida. Me ha ayudado a confiar más en mí”

Bohemia y Arkano charlan, además, sobre lograr que el miedo a equivocarse no les inmovilice, la relación entre educación y rap (y la importancia de tener “un lenguaje más rico”, como precisa Arkano) o la gestión de críticas y redes sociales. Aunque sea una asignatura pendiente para algunos adolescentes, Bohemia ha aprendido a manejar esos mensajes anónimos y ofensivos: “A mucha gente le puede llegar a afectar, y el consejo que les daría es que piensen en quiénes son ellos realmente”.

Pensemos la educación del futuro ‘Pensemos el mañana’, un proyecto de Fundación Unicaja, busca fomentar el conocimiento, los valores de la educación, un aprendizaje sostenible y responsable y dar respuestas a los grandes desafíos de la educación del futuro. El proyecto pivota sobre seis ejes: 1 Aprendizaje y sentido vital 2 Bienestar y salud mental 3 Futuro y empleabilidad 4 Sostenibilidad y sentido colectivo 5 Tecnología y ética 6 Carácter y ciudadanía ¿Qué está ocurriendo en estos tiempos de cambios profundos y transversales? ¿Cuáles son los grandes retos para afrontar la transformación que viene? ¿Qué educación necesitamos? Diferentes personalidades de todos los ámbitos nos ayudarán a responder a estas y otras preguntas destinadas a impulsar cambios, dinamizar ideas y apoyar propuestas con impacto pedagógico y social. ‘Pensemos el mañana’ es un proyecto inspirador para las futuras generaciones llamadas a conquistar nuevas cotas del saber en un mundo complejo y cambiante.

World.title: El destino dorado del turismo español
World.content:
Las 685.856 empresas de la industria de los viajes, la hospitalidad y el ocio conforman uno de los principales motores de la economía española: suponen el 12,6% del Producto Interior Bruto (PIB) y casi el 13% del empleo. Las cifras del sector baten récords cada año, pero abren un debate sobre dónde está el tope

Pangea The Travel Store David Hernández Fundador y director ejecutivo Agencia fundada en 2014 con sucursales por toda España que diseña viajes a medida Nomading Camp Miquel Vila Fundador y director ejecutivo Empresa dedicada al ‘glamping’, una fórmula que ofrece alojamientos de lujo en medio de la naturaleza

España es uno de los mayores escaparates de experiencias del mundo. Es el segundo país más visitado, después de Francia, y cada vez más viajeros lo eligen como destino turístico, de manera que bate registros año tras año. En 2026 se esperan 100 millones de visitas, una cifra nunca alcanzada. “España es una potencia turística a todos los niveles”, señala David Hernández, ingeniero y fundador de Pangea, una agencia que diseña viajes personalizados por todo el mundo. “Y sus empresas, las mejor preparadas por el conocimiento y la experiencia que han acumulado dentro del país. Aquí sabemos de vivir bien y de viajar”, añade Miquel Vila, fundador de Nomading Camp, compañía que ofrece alojamientos de lujo en medio de la naturaleza.

Ambos comparten conversación en un nuevo capítulo del pódcast El poder de las empresas, el pódcast de los que hacen, de Banco Sabadell, dedicado al sector turístico. La charla entre ambos empresarios sirve como visita guiada por las particularidades, los éxitos y los desafíos de la industria turística española.

“Lo que busca el cliente es estar conectado al sitio que visita, ya sea en una escapada a la Sierra de Gredos o en un viaje a Tanzania” Miquel Vila, fundador de Nomading Camp

Las fortalezas Un sector conocido en todo el mundo y en plena digitalización

Una industria que no para de crecer. El sector del turismo lleva más de una década de crecimiento casi ininterrumpido—a excepción de los años de la pandemia—, tanto en número de visitantes como en ingresos. Los cerca de 97 millones de turistas internacionales que visitaron España en 2025 gastaron 134.700 millones de euros, el máximo histórico.

Entornos naturales de gran valor. España destaca como uno de los destinos con mayor biodiversidad, contraste y variedad de paisajes naturales en Europa: cuenta con alta montaña, bosques y playas muy bien valoradas. El país lidera la clasificación mundial de banderas azules que otorga la Fundación FEE, una organización internacional sin ánimo de lucro que promueve el desarrollo sostenible a través de la educación ambiental, valorando la calidad del agua, la seguridad y la accesibilidad. Este año cuenta con 677 playas con bandera azul, 35 más que en 2025, el mejor resultado desde el inicio de esta iniciativa en 1987.

Empresas líderes a nivel internacional. Varias de las mayores compañías turísticas del mundo, especialmente en el ámbito hotelero, son españolas. Operan en decenas de países con marcas como Meliá Hotels International, Barceló Hotel Group, RIU Hotels & Resorts e Iberostar Hotels & Resorts.

Con una marca internacional consolidada. España mantiene una posición de liderazgo como destino turístico y con un visitante fiel que repite, destaca Óscar Perelli, vicepresidente ejecutivo de Exceltur, asociación sin ánimo de lucro que agrupa a las principales empresas turísticas. El país ocupa el segundo lugar en el Travel & Tourism Development Index, clasificación que elabora el Foro Económico Mundial, gracias a la calidad de sus infraestructuras, su riqueza cultural o su conectividad, entre otros factores.

Altamente digitalizado. Las empresas del sector han hecho un esfuerzo por digitalizarse en la última década, apunta Enrique Martínez Marín, presidente de Segittur, un organismo dependiente del Ministerio de Industria y Turismo para impulsar la modernización en el sector. El salto ha sido importante en las cadenas hoteleras y en las agencias de viajes, aunque aún muchas pymes, como restaurantes o alojamientos rurales, tienen margen de mejora. El informe Tendencias y políticas sobre turismo 2026 de la Organización para la Cooperación y el Desarrollo Económicos (OCDE) destaca a España como uno de los países que más está invirtiendo en digitalización.

El país sobresale por la Plataforma Inteligente de Destinos (PID) de Segittur, una infraestructura tecnológica que permite a la Administración y a las empresas de 600 destinos turísticos recabar, compartir y analizar los datos relacionados con este sector: ocupación, transporte, consumo, incidencias meteorológicas... La idea es tomar decisiones a partir de información obtenida en tiempo real, no a base de estadísticas mensuales, y planificar mejor.

Centro de la reflexión sobre la propia industria. Madrid acogerá la sede del Consejo Mundial de Viajes y Turismo (WTTC, por sus siglas en inglés), tras su salida de Londres, Reino Unido. Esta organización internacional representa a las empresas de la industria turística para defender sus intereses, elaborar estudios económicos y promover políticas que favorezcan el desarrollo del turismo.

“De entre las cosas que sabemos hacer en España montar hoteles es una de ellas” Miquel Vila, fundador de Nomading Camp

Los desafios Una industria que puede morir por su propio éxito o por el cambio climático

Riesgo de saturación de los destinos. Los expertos empiezan a cuestionar si el número de visitas internacionales tiene un límite físico y social. Los centros históricos saturados y las playas abarrotadas han alimentado protestas ciudadanas en territorios dependientes del turismo, como ambos archipiélagos, Málaga o Barcelona. Incluso se ha acuñado el concepto “turismofobia” para la corriente más radical del rechazo al auge del turismo. Ayuntamientos y Gobiernos autonómicos apuestan por redistribuir los flujos turísticos hacia destinos menos saturados y alargar las temporadas hacia el otoño y la primavera para aliviar la presión veraniega.

Adaptarse al cambio climático. Pocas industrias dependen tanto del clima como el turismo, por lo que el aumento de las temperaturas, la sequía, los incendios forestales o la erosión costera afectan directamente al principal activo turístico español: el territorio y su riqueza natural. El desafío pasa por diversificar y reforzar la resiliencia de las infraestructuras, así como proteger los ecosistemas que sustentan buena parte de los territorios turísticos del país.

El reto continuo de mejorar en sostenibilidad. La conservación del medio ambiente es una tarea compartida por todos los sectores económicos, pero resulta esencial en el turismo. Entre los principales retos figuran la gestión del agua, particularmente en zonas con estrés hídrico como las islas y el litoral mediterráneo, así como la reducción de los residuos y de las emisiones contaminantes, derivadas del transporte aéreo y marítimo, dos de las actividades con mayor huella de carbono. Todo ello empuja a la industria a caminar hacia un modelo más eficiente y menos intensivo en el uso de recursos.

Tensión sobre el parque de viviendas. Óscar Perelli, vicepresidente de Exceltur muestra su preocupación por la conversión masiva de inmuebles en establecimientos turísticos en los principales destinos. Algo que genera tensiones entre los ciudadanos. El turismo no es el único responsable del problema en el sector inmobiliario, pero sí uno de sus aceleradores en zonas con alta demanda.

World.title: Rosa Vañó (Castillo de Canena): “Madonna es una de las personas más complicadas y con más ego con las que he trabajado”
World.content:
Economista de formación, dejó su exitosa carrera de directiva en Coca-Cola para desarrollar, junto a su hermano Francisco, la explotación olivarera que había creado su padre en Jaén. Además, conoce muy bien el mundo de las discográficas ya que trabajó para Warner Music y Universal

Es la gran dama del aceite español. Rosa Vañó (Madrid, 63 años), economista de formación, abandonó una exitosa carrera como directiva de Coca-Cola, donde se dedicaba al desarrollo de nuevas líneas de negocio, lanzamientos y reposicionamiento de productos, para dedicarse, junto a su hermano Francisco, al sueño que inició su padre, Luis Vañó: impulsar Castillo de Canena, una explotación olivarera con almazara situada en Canena (Jaén), propiedad de su familia y reconocida con numerosos premios nacionales e internacionales. Anteriormente trabajó en las discográficas Warner Music y Universal, “donde aprendí a gestionar egos y a entender que hay que contar con los medios de comunicación como embajadores y transmisores de la creatividad y el valor añadido de los músicos”. Ejerce también como tesorera de la Real Academia de Gastronomía.

Pregunta. Con este bagaje, decide desarrollar su propio negocio.

Respuesta. Sí, porque teníamos la enorme suerte de tener campo, almazara y también el castillo. Se puede empezar de cero, pero de distintas formas. Es un recorrido profesional que te va formando y quitando miedos. La ignorancia es muy valiente y te hace creer que puedes hacer las cosas mejor, de forma diferente y de manera especial. Todo esto cuesta mucho trabajo. Primero, porque no es fácil hacerlo y porque hay mucha gente que lo hace igual o mejor que tú. Al final, la fórmula no es otra que trabajo, pero bien entendido.

P. ¿Qué significa esto?

R. El trabajo no son horas, es calidad y flexibilidad. Los peores resultados los he tenido cuando he trabajado 14 horas al día. He sido menos resolutiva y creativa. Me parece importante la conectividad para mi conciliación como madre, como hija y como profesional. Son las tres prioridades de mi vida. El teléfono me permite tener mi sitio de trabajo en cualquier lugar.

P. Comentaba que sabe manejar los egos. ¿Se ha encontrado con muchos?

R. Madonna es una de las personas más complicadas y con más ego que he conocido y con la que he trabajado en mi vida. Me tocó trabajar con ella en promoción y en gira. Por el contrario, con Phil Collins o los hermanos Young [Malcolm y Angus], de AC/DC, me he divertido mucho. Son personas que han dejado el ego a un lado. Y no tiene nada que ver con que sean hombres o mujeres. Por ejemplo, Prince era un hombre que tenía inseguridades, pero con una gestión muy peculiar de su ego. Porque el ego no es solo el de tipo Madonna, en el que tienes que interpretar su gestión, sino también cómo se siente, cómo es su timidez y cómo tienes que relacionarte con él. Seal tampoco era una persona fácil. Fue mi primer artista y era complicado de manejar.

P. ¿Qué se hace en esos casos?

R. Callar, entender y destensar la situación, aunque no tengas la culpa. Hay que intentar destensar y tratar de ser empático y resolutivo. El ego es más complejo que creerse superior, por eso hay que entender cómo es la personalidad de cada uno. Ha sido una gran escuela de vida.

P. Salir a vender aceite por el mundo habrá sido mucho más fácil, ¿no?

R. La primera vez que salí a vender aceite fue en España. Entré en un restaurante, que no voy a decir cuál, por la puerta principal. Me preguntaron a qué iba y les dije que a vender aceite. Me dijeron que eso era por la puerta de proveedores, que estaba por detrás, donde estaban los cubos de basura y los cascos de botellas. Entré por ahí. Hoy, si no me dicen lo contrario, siempre entro por la puerta de proveedores. Entiendo que, si el cocinero me tiene que recibir en su cocina para probar el aceite, esa es la puerta. Hay que entender cada situación.

P. ¿Ha hecho mucha calle?

R. Al principio hay que hacer mucha calle. Ahora también, pero tenemos más gente que te ayuda. Estoy en un momento de mi vida en el que tengo que mirarlo todo con mucha positividad. Lo mejor es hoy y tengo que estar preparada para el día de mañana. Debe haber un relevo. Hay decisiones que ya no me toca tomar a mí, sino al equipo, a mi sobrino y a mi hijo [ambos se llaman Luis y llevan el apellido Vañó]. Me pueden pedir opinión, pero no puedo empecinarme en que la decisión es mía porque hay gente alrededor que tiene que liderar. Odiaría ser la típica persona que es la primera que llega a la oficina y la última que se va. O la que va todos los días, con 80 años, a ver qué pasa.

P. ¿A qué dedica el resto del tiempo cuando no trabaja?

R. Voy a ir por orden de frivolidad. Me gusta jugar al golf; hago pilates tres días a la semana, que me divierte mucho, y camino. Soy una gran aficionada a viajar, pero con causa. Mi afición siempre ha sido la antropología, la arqueología y el arte antiguo. Me ha interesado saber cuándo el hombre deja de ser animal y adquiere un toque divino o humano. Me gusta viajar con contenido, por ejemplo, para ver el románico del norte de España, el misterio de las catedrales, conocer culturas antiguas... Es algo que no he hecho en los últimos años todo lo que me habría gustado y me gustaría retomarlo. Coger un barco y recorrer las esclusas francesas, pararte en los vignerons y vas viendo el paisaje, me gusta. Me voy a dedicar a viajar más. También he descuidado mucho mi afición a las exposiciones. Antes iba prácticamente todos los meses a ver dos exposiciones en Madrid y, si tenía que irme fuera, también lo hacía. Pero ahora, por mi situación personal, he descuidado un poco esa faceta. Me encantaba ir con toda la familia a ver una exposición y luego irnos a comer. Me parece gratificante. Adoro leer.

P. ¿Cuál es su género preferido?

R. Leo mucha historia, pero como formo parte de varias tertulias literarias me hacen leer todo tipo de libros. Uno de los más recientes ha sido Historia de una escalera. También acabo de leer varias obras de Hermann Hesse para una tertulia. Me esfuerzo por leer cosas diferentes de las que suelo leer durante el insomnio.

P. ¿Qué lee en esas noches en vela?

R. Leo a Agatha Christie y a sir Arthur Conan Doyle. Quiero lecturas ligeras para quedarme dormida. La ópera me ha encantado toda la vida. He estado en distintos teatros, como el Bolshói o La Scala de Milán. Verdi y Puccini me encantan porque mi madre me los ponía de pequeña. Voy a cuatro o cinco óperas al año. También me encanta la música barroca. No me pierdo los ciclos de Händel en el Auditorio Nacional de Música de Madrid.

P. ¿Qué restaurantes frecuenta?

R. Tanto de producto y muy clásicos como sorprendentes y de vanguardia. Me gustan los dos extremos. Estuve hace poco en Desde 1911 y trabaja con un gran producto. También me gustan las verduras de Saddle o el ganso de Navidad, que tomo con mis hijos. Los atunes guisados de El Campero me encantan. No me gustan los crudos. Estuve hace poco en Tetsu y me pareció espectacular y divertido. De Jaén me gustan Juan Carlos García, de Vandelvira, y Pedro Sánchez, de Bagá; también Dani Carnero, del restaurante Kaleja en Málaga. Son maravillosos. Y José Álvarez, en la costa de Almería, con su proyecto de tomates.

P. ¿Su desayuno preferido?

R. Una tostada de pan bien caliente, restregada con ajo, aceite de oliva virgen extra y sal. El ajo es maravilloso de todas las maneras. No soy muy cafetera, tomo uno al día. Me gusta su olor, pero no tanto el sabor.

P. ¿Le gusta darse caprichos?

R. No, salvo gastronómicos. Comprarme ropa siempre tiene que ser algo organizado. Hace años, una compañera de trabajo me dijo que salía con la misma ropa en todas las fotografías. Nunca se lo agradeceré lo suficiente porque no había caído en ello. Soy muy estructurada con lo que me pongo, pero ir de compras me aburre. También me aburren las obras en casa y comprar cosas para decorarla.

P. ¿Tiene algún viaje pendiente?

R. Cuando era pequeña leí los libros de Jack London y sus viajes a los mares del Sur. Por eso me atrae la Polinesia, aunque luego quizá sea un coñazo y tenga que llevarme 200 libros, preguntándome qué hago yo en un palafito. Me gustaría conocerla. También me gustaría ver una aurora boreal. La Antártida me resulta muy atractiva. Y me apetecería hacer un viaje en barco entre Moscú y San Petersburgo.

P. ¿Algún remedio para el insomnio?

R. La edad no perdona. He probado todo lo que no es químico y, a veces, funciona y otras no. Ya convivo con él, incluso cuando estoy de vacaciones en Granada, frente al mar Mediterráneo, al que tanto quiero. Lo que no me gusta es pensar por la noche porque es muy mala compañera. También escucho pódcasts ligeros y de true crime; eso me evade y evita que me invadan los malos pensamientos, porque soy una persona muy positiva y estable.

World.title: Extra supervision for KLM’s maintenance arm over safety concerns
World.content:
Dutch flag carrier KLM’s maintenance division has been put under s etricter supervision because of concerns about its workplace safety culture.

The environment and transport inspectorate (ILT) confirmed to the Volkskrant that the special measures had been put in place at KLM Engineering & Maintenance since May and would last for the rest of the year.

The company handles more than 3,000 aircraft and components a year on behalf of major airlines such as British Airways, Lufthansa and Emirates, as well as KLM and Transavia. It recorded a turnover of €2.4 billion last year, 18% of KLM’s total activity.

The ILT would give details of what issues had prompted the move, citing confidentiality, but stressed there were no implications for aircraft safety.

A spokesman told the Volkskrant that KLM’s security management was at the “minimal level of maturity and the supervision would focus on “compliance and administrative findings that can lead to operational security risks”.

World.title: Deventer closes harbour indefinitely due to low river levels
World.content:
Deventer is closing its harbour to ships from this weekend after the summer drought caused the water level in the river IJssel to drop to exceptionally low levels.

The municipal council said on its website that the sluice gates would close to prevent “damage to water barriers, problems for ships and risks for houseboats”.

The rules state that the sluice gates must be closed if the level of the river outside the harbour falls below 45cm above Normaal Amsterdams Peil (NAP), the baseline measure roughly equivalent to sea level.

That level is expected to be reached on Saturday. Ships will be allowed to enter the harbour until Thursday, but will have to leave by Friday evening.

The last time Deventer’s harbour was closed due to low water levels was in 2018, when it was able to reopen after two weeks.

The Twentekanaal, which runs between Almelo, Hengelo and Enschede, has been closed since last Saturday because the water level is too low. The regional liaison group Twente Board has written to infrastructure minister Vincent Karremans asking for financial support for affected businesses.

Koninklijke Binnenvaart Nederland (KBN), the collective body for inland waterway operators, said the closure would cost the local economy between €125,000 and €500,000 a day. The canal will reopen once the water level rises to 9.10 metres above NAP.

World.title: Government failed to protect family of Marengo crown witness
World.content:
A court in The Hague ruled on Wednesday that the authorities did not do enough to safeguard the family of Nabil Bakkali, the crown witness in the Marengo trial.

Judges found in a civil suit brought by the family that the government acted “unlawfully towards the family by failing to take sufficient security measures prior to the announcement of the crown witness deal.”

Nabil Bakkali was involved in the criminal operations of Ridouan Taghi and, in 2017, turned crown witness in exchange for a reduced sentence. His brother, who was not involved in the case, was killed shortly after. Other members of the family have lived in hiding since.

Taghi was given a life sentence in 2024 in one of the largest trials in Dutch history.

Life and death: the biggest Dutch criminal trial explained

Bakkali’s family brought the suit several years ago. The ruling was made in January but it was only published by the court today.

The family had already been awarded compensation for the negligence and the judges determined that no further money is warranted.

In a statement, the family said they would appeal. “Lives have been disrupted, careers have been lost, and those involved have suffered serious and lasting psychological damage,” they said.

In 2023, the Dutch Safety Board (OVV) already issued a damning report on the system for protecting relatives of crown witnesses.

World.title: Manhunt after car carrying explosives crashes in police chase
World.content:
Police are trying to trace the occupants of a car that crashed at high speed in Amsterdam while carrying high explosives, causing dozens of homes to be evacuated.

The black BMW M1 was being pursued by Dutch police after their German colleagues spotted it at the scene of a cashpoint explosion in Fürth, Hessen, around 250km from the Dutch border.

Witnesses described how it was driven into Nierkerkestraat, Osdorp, at high speed, hit a speed bump and crashed. The occupants, at least one of whom was armed, got out and fled on foot.

A specialist explosives team quickly arrived on the scene and cleared all houses within a 100m radius after discovering bomb-making materials in the vehicle.

Residents had to stay out of their homes for nearly nine hours following the incident, which happened at around 1pm on Tuesday, until the car was taken away on a tow truck.

Police appealed for witnesses to come forward, as well as anyone with information about the storage of explosives in the area. It is not clear how many people were in the car.

Cross-border gangs

German police said no money was stolen in the attack on the cash machine, but the building where it was located was badly damaged by the blast.

The Osdorp area of Amsterdam is known to be a base for gangs that carry out cross-border raids on German cashpoints, which tend to contain more money than those in the Netherlands because cash is still widely used there.

Last month seven people were injured and an entire block of flats had to be evacuated after an explosion in a basement gym next to the Osdorper Ban which was caused by home-made explosives.

Police arrested two men aged 24 and 23, both of whom were among the casualties. Prosecutors said they were suspected of planning explosions and possessing explosive materials.

Police have arrested three teenagers in overnight raids in Eindhoven, Rotterdam and Alkmaar as part of a a counter-terrorism investigation.

The three suspects, aged between 16 and 19, were arrested at their homes in the early hours of Wednesday.

Video footage from Rotterdam showed around half a dozen police wearing riot helmets and body armour going into a house and leading a blindfolded man to a car.

The Eindhovens Dagblad newspaper said the 19-year-old man was arrested in Jan van Eyckgracht, a street in the Burghplan neighbourhood.

Three years ago he was reportedly arrested at the same address on suspicion of planning attacks on nightclubs and police stations in Belgium via social media channels. No attacks actually took place.

He was given a 112-day jail sentence, a 200-hour community service order and banned from travelling out of the Netherlands after the court heard he had talked about joining the terrorist organisation Islamic State in Afghanistan.

No further details were available of the arrest in Alkmaar, Noord-Holland.

World.title: Fire destroys youth care facility in Beekbergen
World.content:

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Firefighters in the Gelderland town of Beekbergen are still trying to contain a blaze on Wednesday that destroyed a youth care facility.

The local safety board says teams are “extinguishing hidden pockets of fire” from the inferno that broke out late Tuesday evening.

Around 20 people were evacuated and one person was rushed to the hospital. The cause of the fire is not yet clear.

The flames quickly spread to a nearby wooded area and more than 150 children hundred children attending a local camp were also evacuated.

The facility is a residential care home for young people with complex psychological problems, behavioural problems or autism. Security staff said all residents were accounted for. 186 children attending a nearby summer camp were also evacuated.

The building is considered to be a total loss. It dates from 1981 and is suspected to contain asbestos. The authorities have cordoned off the area and asked residents to close their windows as a precautionary measure.

World.title: Weather warnings issued as temperatures set to hit 35C
World.content:
The national heat plan has been activated for the second time this summer as temperatures are set to reach between 30C and 35C in most parts of the Netherlands.

The meteorological office KNMI has issued code yellow warnings for the inland provinces of Overijssel, Gelderland, Noord-Brabant and Limburg, for Wednesday, and Thursday and Friday.

Temperatures are due to peak at 35C on Wednesday before falling slightly to around 32C on Thursday. On Saturday there will be a brief respite, with maximum temperatures of 25C, but new highs of 33C are forecast for Monday.

A lack of wind will make the heat feel more intense and temperatures will remain high at night, close to 20C in most parts of the country. Conditions will be cooler on the Wadden Islands, with a maximum temperature of 24C.

The national heat plan is invoked if there is a serious risk of temperatures above 27C for four days or longer.

It includes advice to pay extra attention to vulnerable people, drink more water to stay cool and be aware that medicines may work differently in warm conditions.

Last month the KNMI issued a red alert for heat for the first time. Schools and universities were closed, work was suspended on building sites and some supermarkets cancelled home deliveries.

World.title: Dutch tourist dies after boat overturns at waterfalls in Brazil
World.content:
A Dutch tourist has died and another is recovering in hospital after a boat overturned during a safari in Brazil.

The accident at the Iguaçu Falls, in the Iguaçu national park on the border with Argentina, happened on Tuesday afternoon and is being investigated by the Brazilian navy.

Six Dutch nationals were on board the boat, including a family of four with two daughters, as well as two crew members. The foreign affairs ministry said the man who died was 25 years old and from Rijssen-Holten in Overijssel. He was reportedly the boyfriend of one of the daughters.

Investigations will focus on what caused the boat to capsize during the tour of the falls, which mark the boundary between the upper and lower Iguazu river.

Four of the victims, three women and a man, were given treatment at the scene by park staff but did not need to go to hospital. The victim died at Padre Germano Lauck Municipal Hospital in Foz do Iguaçu, where another member of the party is receiving treatment after being rescued by park workers.

The fire department confirmed the cause of death was drowning.

News website G1 reported that the falls were carrying 4.3 million litres of water per second at the time of the accident, nearly three times the normal level.

Tour operator Macuco Safari said in a statement that it regretted the incident and was providing assistance to the victims.

World.title: Record number of Poles opposed to Ukraine’s EU membership

Support for Ukraine joining the European Union has fallen sharply in Poland, with opposition reaching a record high of 40%, a survey carried out by the Polish state research agency CBOS shows. The figures show that 50% of Poles still support Ukraine’s EU membership, but that is a significant decline from 74% in October 2023, when the question was last asked, and from a record 90% in March 2022, shortly after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The shift comes as public sentiment towards Ukrainians in general in Poland has deteriorated in recent years. The latest CBOS poll shows that, among those who support Ukraine’s EU accession, most favour a gradual process, with 41% of all respondents saying Ukraine should join the EU but “without undue haste”. “Only 9% of respondents currently support Ukraine’s earliest possible EU membership, which is the lowest figure in the history of these surveys,” CBOS reported. Meanwhile, opposition to Ukraine’s EU membership has increased by 23 percentage points since October 2023, reaching its highest level in the history of CBOS surveys. People with right-wing political beliefs are most likely to be opposed to Ukraine’s accession (53%), while the age group with the highest percentage of people opposed is those aged 18-24 (58%). The survey also found that a majority of Poles expect the war in Ukraine to end with territorial concessions from Kyiv – 55% of respondents said they believed Ukraine would lose some territory, a view that has remained dominant since December 2024. Compared with the previous survey, however, pessimism has eased. The proportion of respondents who expect Ukraine to lose part of its territory fell by 8 percentage points, while the number expecting Russia to take control of the entire country declined from 8% to 6%. On Western support for Ukraine, 39% of respondents said the military, financial and humanitarian assistance provided by countries in the West was sufficient. Meanwhile, 27% said aid was excessive, while 22% said it was insufficient. Russia has published purported archival documents relating to massacres of Poles by Ukrainians in WWII. Kyiv had warned that Russia was planning to release the files in order to stir tensions, while Polish media note that the material contains nothing new https://t.co/CI0cfAlDle — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 6, 2026 Ukrainians are Poland’s largest foreign national group, with almost 1.6 million living in the country, but recent polls have shown growing hostility towards them, fuelled in part by anti-Ukrainian rhetoric from far-right parties and a tougher stance towards Kyiv from some opposition politicians. In its annual survey of attitudes towards national and ethnic groups, CBOS found earlier this year that the proportion of Poles who said they disliked Ukrainians increased by five percentage points this year, the largest rise recorded among all groups surveyed, reaching 43%. Tensions between the two countries have also been heightened by disputes over historical issues and a series of recent incidents targeting Ukrainians in Poland. The number of reported hate crimes against Ukrainians in Poland is up 30% so far this year, police data show. The figures come following recent high-profile cases of verbal and physical attacks against Ukrainians, who are Poland's largest immigrant group https://t.co/pcTsJddDz7 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 17, 2026 The number of reported hate crimes against Ukrainians rose by 30% in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period a year earlier, according to newly reported police data. Last weekend, three men were filmed violently attacking a Ukrainian woman and her partner outside a shop in Wrocław, apparently because of her accent. Two of the assailants have since been detained by police, while their victims required treatment in hospital. In response, Prime Minister Donald Tusk called for Poles to “wage war on violence”, saying that the perpetrators of such acts “have become emboldened precisely because they now have political role models, political patrons, and political support”. World.title: Newly sworn-in judge of Poland’s constitutional court stages boycott over blocked colleagues
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A newly sworn-in judge of Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) has said he will refuse to sit on the court until four other judges appointed by parliament earlier this year, but blocked by the president, are allowed to take their seats. It is the latest development in a months-long dispute between the opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki and the government, which considers the TK to be improperly staffed and therefore illegitimate. Although Nawrocki swore in Sławomir Patyra, who was appointed by the ruling majority in parliament in June, as a TK judge on Tuesday, he continues to refuse to swear in four other judges appointed by parliament earlier this year. Po złożeniu przysięgi Patyra ogłosił, że zamierza odmówić orzekania. To gest solidarności z czwórką sędziów, od których prezydent nie chce przyjąć przysięgi https://t.co/jdbKusQ3H9 — OKO.press (@oko_press) July 28, 2026 Shortly after his swearing-in ceremony at the presidential palace on Tuesday, Patyra arrived at the TK headquarters in Warsaw, where he was accompanied by four other judges appointed by parliament this year, including two whom Nawrocki has refused to swear in. There, he announced that his decision not to sit on the court was a matter of loyalty to the constitution and his belief in judicial ethos. “I cannot imagine taking an oath today to uphold the constitution, only to start breaking that constitution tomorrow,” he said. Patyra told journalists that he would “submit a declaration of refusal to adjudicate” due to his solidarity with judges who are “unlawfully deprived of the chance to participate in the work of the tribunal”. He added that, along with the other judges chosen this year, he is “fully mobilised to restore the Constitutional Tribunal to its proper, constitutional, systemic form”. Under Polish law, when a vacancy emerges among the 15 positions on the TK, the lower house of parliament, the Sejm, chooses who should fill it. However, to take office, the judge must swear an oath before the president. In April, after the Sejm had chosen six candidates to fill vacancies on the court, Nawrocki took the unprecedented step of inviting only two of them to be sworn in. He argued there were doubts over the legality of how all six had been chosen, but decided to accept two to ensure the TK had the necessary quorum to function. Those two have been able to take up their seats on the court, but the other four remain in limbo. Although they arranged their own private swearing-in ceremony without the presence of Nawrocki, TK’s chief justice Bogdan Święczkowski has refused to accept them. In May, the European Court of Human Rights ordered that the quartet be allowed to take up their positions. But the TK – where judges appointed under the former Law and Justice (PiS) government retain a majority – issued its own ruling endorsing Nawrocki’s right not to swear in the new judges. The European Court of Human Rights has ordered Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) to accept four judges whom opposition-aligned President Nawrocki refused to swear in. The decision was welcomed by the government but rejected by the TK itself https://t.co/9NxInPdYk9 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 6, 2026 On 11 June, the Sejm then chose another judge, Patyra, to fill a newly opened vacancy on the court. In his case, the legal doubts Nawrocki had expressed regarding the previous appointments, which in some instances were made more than a year after the vacancies had arisen, did not seem to apply. Yet for weeks the president refused to confirm whether he would swear him in. That prompted Patyra to write to Nawrocki in early July and then again later in the month, asking the president to indicate a date on which he could take his oath. After repeated requests, Nawrocki finally decided last week to invite Patyra to the presidential palace. The president’s chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, noted that “there were some doubts” but “the president dispelled them” and added that Patyra was chosen “in accordance with all procedures”. Nowo wybrany przez Sejm Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej uchwałą z dnia 11 czerwca 2026 r. sędzia Trybunału Konstytucyjnego Sławomir Patyra złożył wobec Prezydenta RP ślubowanie. pic.twitter.com/VLMRAIg1Yj — Kancelaria Prezydenta RP (@prezydentpl) July 28, 2026 The TK has been at the heart of the rule-of-law crisis that has developed in Poland over the last decade. In 2015, former PiS-aligned President Andrzej Duda refused to swear in three judges legally chosen by the Sejm. Shortly afterwards, PiS won parliamentary elections and nominated three replacements for those judges, who were sworn in by Duda. Those three judges and their successors have been deemed illegitimate in a succession of rulings by Polish and European courts. Due to their continued presence on the court, the current government, which replaced PiS in 2023, rejects the TK’s legitimacy and refuses to recognise its rulings. Under both Święczkowski, a former member of the PiS government, and his predecessor Julia Przyłębska, a close personal associate of PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński, the TK has been widely seen as issuing rulings aligned with the political interests of PiS. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Former Polish PM Morawiecki forms parliamentary caucus  rival to PiS, deepening opposition split
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Former Polish Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki says that 40 MPs and one senator aligned with him will form their own parliamentary group, deepening a split in the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party after a dispute over party direction and loyalty declarations. The move marks the most serious internal challenge in years to PiS, which ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023, and follows months of tensions between Morawiecki’s more moderate faction and party conservatives who have pushed the group in a hard-right direction. Once formally established, Morawiecki’s caucus would become the third-largest bloc in the Sejm, Poland’s lower house of parliament. Powstanie klub parlamentarny „Rozwój Plus”. Morawiecki zdecydował#PAPInformacjehttps://t.co/IftRdgpIPw — Polska Agencja Prasowa/Polish Press Agency (PAP) (@PAPinformacje) July 29, 2026 One of Morawiecki’s allies, Marcin Horała, told reporters that the creation of the caucus did not mean they were leaving PiS, but “simply setting up a parliamentary group so that we can get on with our work”. He noted, however, that PiS’s parliamentary group “has stopped treating us as its members”. Morawiecki, meanwhile, said that his group remained ready to cooperate with PiS as a “second lung” of the party’s broader political camp, but suggested that the current leadership was moving in a different direction. He said that parts of PiS’s messaging were increasingly influenced by “dissidents and schemers” as well as hardline factions, including Sovereign Poland (Suwerenna Polska), a nationalist group that was previously a junior coalition partner of PiS and often clashed with Morawiecki when he was prime minister. Reacting to Morawiecki’s announcement, party chairman Jarosław Kaczyński said the former prime minister had carried out a planned split of the party despite his efforts to reach a deal. “Until the end I made efforts to reach an agreement, unfortunately Mateusz Morawiecki clearly had his own political plan in mind, carried out on the basis of a split in PiS,” Kaczyński wrote on X. The announcement follows a dispute that began after Morawiecki launched his Development Plus (Rozwój Plus) association in April. The former prime minister insisted the association was intended to complement PiS with a pro-development agenda rather than rival it. However, critics within PiS viewed it as an attempt by Morawiecki to build an alternative power base that could eventually evolve into a separate party ahead of the 2027 parliamentary election. Seeking to end the standoff, the party ordered PiS lawmakers to resign from all outside political associations by last Thursday, or face “consequences” including “the loss of membership in PiS”. On Friday, Kaczyński said that “around 30 MPs” had failed to comply and had therefore effectively resigned from the party, adding that Tuesday’s meeting of the party’s political committee would simply confirm this fact. Poland's right-wing opposition PiS party is set to split after a more moderate faction of over 30 MPs loyal to deputy leader @MorawieckiM refused to sign a loyalty pledge demanded by leader @OficjalnyJK, who says that means they have effectively resigned https://t.co/TuqYpGI5ak — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 24, 2026 On Tuesday, the party announced that instead, the committee had referred the cases of 44 members, who either failed to submit the required declarations or submitted them on the wrong form, to the party’s disciplinary officer for individual review, delaying a final decision. “From a formal and legal perspective, Mr Mateusz Morawiecki has not yet been removed from the list of members,” PiS spokesman Rafał Bochenek said on Tuesday. PiS disciplinary officer Karol Karski told the Polish Press Agency (PAP) he would examine each case individually. “I am open to speaking with each of them so they can present their positions,” Karski said. “At this point, I can initiate proceedings against the individual in question, refer the case to a peer disciplinary tribunal with a motion for punishment – this could include a temporary suspension or expulsion from PiS.” PiS has for the last two decades been the dominant force on the Polish right, including periods leading governments in 2005-2007 and 2015-2023. However, since losing power at elections in 2023, when the party won 35% of the vote, the party has seen its average support in polls fall to around 23-24%, the lowest level in 14 years. Support for PiS has fallen to its lowest in 14 years, as the party grapples with internal division, the rise of far-right challengers, living in President Nawrocki's shadow, and the unpopularity in Poland of PiS ally Donald Trump, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/QRScBpEQQG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 2, 2026 Meanwhile, it has been challenged by the rise of the far right, where two parties, Confederation (Konfederacja) and Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP), now together poll at a similar combined level of support to PiS. In response, Kaczyński in March named a hardline figure, Przemysław Czarnek, as PiS’s candidate for prime minister in next year’s elections. Czarnek was seen as someone who could appeal to far-right voters, while also potentially working with the far right if a coalition was needed after the elections. However, there has been no rise in support for PiS since Czarnek was named, prompting growing concern from more moderate figures within the party, led by Morawiecki. The national-conservative opposition PiS party has named its candidate to be prime minister if it wins next year’s parliamentary elections. Przemysław Czarnek is a hardline conservative who played a prominent role in PiS's campaign against "LGBT ideology" https://t.co/sSJLON00hW — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 7, 2026 They argue that PiS has wrongly disowned many of the successes of its time in office before 2023, and they fear that its rightward shift damages its chances of winning over more centrist voters. Adam Szłapka, the spokesman of the current more liberal government, said Braun was “the ultimate playmaker in this whole game”, who had helped push far-right rhetoric into the political mainstream. “The worst thing about this whole situation is that Poland’s largest opposition party has, in effect, started to adopt Grzegorz Braun’s agenda from A to Z,” Szłapka told broadcaster TVN24. Ostatecznym rozgrywającym w całej tej rozgrywce nie jest ani prezes Jarosław Kaczyński, ani Mateusz Morawiecki, tylko Grzegorz Braun – ocenił w #JedenNaJeden w TVN24 rzecznik rządu Adam Szłapka. W rozmowie z @AgataAdamek komentował sytuację w PiS. World.title: Polish court finds regulation allowing foreign same-sex marriage registration unconstitutional
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) has ruled that a new regulation allowing the registration of foreign same-sex marriage certificates in Poland was partly unconstitutional, saying it went beyond technical administrative changes and conflicted with the constitution’s definition of marriage. The regulation, introduced by the digital affairs ministry after rulings by the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) and Poland’s Supreme Administrative Court (NSA), was due to take effect on 23 August. The government, which considers the court to be improperly constituted, says it will not implement the ruling. The government has issued a regulation allowing foreign same-sex marriages to be entered in the civil registry The decision comes in response to an EU court order and marks a major change in a country that does not allow same-sex unions under domestic law https://t.co/2an5mGtnHl — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 22, 2026 Polish law does not allow same-sex couples to marry or enter into civil unions, and a bill that would have granted such limited rights to unmarried couples was recently vetoed by the opposition-backed president. Until this year, same-sex couples who married abroad were also unable to register their marriage certificates in Poland. After the CJEU ruled that Poland must recognise such marriages, the digital affairs ministry changed civil status forms. Instead of separate fields for “man” and “woman”, the new templates use “man/woman”, allowing registry offices to record both opposite-sex and same-sex marriages. Lawmakers from the national-conservative opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party, however, challenged the regulation, arguing that the digital affairs minister had exceeded his powers because the changes were not merely technical but affected the legal definition of marriage. The tribunal, which is widely seen as being under PiS’s influence, agreed. The tribunal said the new forms allowed relationships that do not match the constitution’s definition of marriage as a union between a man and a woman to be recorded as marriages. It said regulations can only implement existing laws and cannot change matters reserved for the constitution or parliament. The tribunal also said that registering a foreign marriage certificate cannot produce legal effects that conflict with the basic principles of Polish law. It added that changing the constitutional definition of marriage would require amendments to the constitution and related laws. Some legal experts argue that, while the constitution states that a “marriage, being a union of a man and a woman… shall be placed under the protection and care of the Republic of Poland,” that phrasing does not rule out other legally recognised unions receiving state protection. Poland has begun recognising foreign same-sex marriages. But the legal consequences for such couples remain unclear, especially as Polish law does not allow any form of same-sex union We asked five experts for their view on what this will mean in practice https://t.co/h2KHmW8sMI — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 19, 2026 Shortly after the ruling, government members said they would not comply with the tribunal’s decision and that the regulation would enter into force as planned. “The illegal Constitutional Tribunal is once again attempting to obstruct a state that is enforcing the law in force and the rulings of European courts,” digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said. “The transcription of foreign same-sex marriage certificates is and will remain legal,” he said, adding that 184 same-sex couples had so far had their foreign marriage certificates transcribed. Katarzyna Kotula, the government official responsible for equality issues, said the TK ruling on the issue of transcriptions “has no legal force whatsoever”. Transkrypcja zagranicznych aktów małżeństw jednopłciowych jest i będzie legalna. Rozporządzenie, które przyjęliśmy porządkuje dokumenty i… — Krzysztof Gawkowski (@KGawkowski) July 28, 2026 The TK has been at the heart of the rule-of-law crisis that has developed in Poland over the last decade. In 2015, former PiS-aligned President Andrzej Duda refused to swear in three judges legally chosen by the Sejm. Shortly afterwards, PiS won parliamentary elections and nominated three replacements for those judges, who were sworn in by Duda. Those three judges and their successors have been deemed illegitimate in a succession of rulings by Polish and European courts. Due to their continued presence on the court, the current government, which replaced PiS in 2023, rejects the TK’s legitimacy and refuses to recognise its rulings. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 Under both Święczkowski, a former member of the PiS government, and his predecessor Julia Przyłębska, a close personal associate of PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński, the TK has been widely seen as issuing rulings aligned with the political interests of PiS. For a long time, the government refused to appoint new judges to the Constitutional Tribunal as the terms of the previous judges expired, with some vacancies remaining unfilled for over a year. In recent months, the government has resumed appointing new judges, but President Karol Nawrocki, an ally of PiS, is refusing to administer the oath of office to some of them. World.title: Residents oppose move to add Polish village to list of protected monuments
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A decision to designate a village as a protected monument has sparked fierce opposition from residents, who have vowed to “fight until the end” against measures they say will limit their ability to renovate and build on their properties. The village in question, Ostaszów in southwestern Poland’s Lower Silesia province, was established in 1936 by Nazi Germany as an agricultural settlement of around 42 farms. At the time, the region still belonged to Germany. The Lower Silesian Provincial Conservator of Monuments argues Ostaszów has “unique, homogeneous historical architecture” requiring state protection, but local officials say that the way the decision was made, despite opposition from residents, shows “the voice of local communities has no significance”. After World War Two, most of Lower Silesia, including the village, became part of Poland. The village’s architecture has remained largely unchanged, with its residential buildings connected to barns, forming unique cohesive farmstead units. Around 250 people live there. Earlier this year, the residents were told proceedings had begun to add the village to the register of protected monuments, reports the Gazeta Wyborcza daily. The provincial conservator said on Friday it had reached a decision. “The unique, above-standard historical, scientific and artistic value of Ostaszów as a monument cannot be questioned,” it wrote in a statement. It noted that a study by a team working under the culture ministry had found that the village was the only preserved settlement of its kind in Lower Silesia. Residents and local officials said they planned to appeal against the decision, arguing it would create additional bureaucracy and interfere with property owners’ ability to decide on building and renovation work. “We have a years-long legal battle ahead of us, but we won’t give up. We will fight until the end. We believe that decisions about the 42 homes in Ostaszów should be made by their residents, not by harmful officials,” residents wrote in a statement quoted by the Polish Press Agency (PAP). “In a cardboard state, the voice of local communities has no significance – only orders and bans count. Our future is to be decided by a heartless official from [the Lower Silesian capital of] Wrocław who does not even have time to meet with the victims of his decisions,” said the village head, Sylwia Mazur. Wieś Ostaszów wpisana do rejestru zabytków. Mieszkańcy będą się odwoływaćhttps://t.co/ZxmH2lbHnb pic.twitter.com/cPdL73PXIH — Dzieje.pl (@dziejepl) July 26, 2026 The conservator noted, however, that until the appeals process is concluded, construction works cannot proceed. It added that it planned to cooperate with locals to “develop principles of renovation and investment procedures in accordance with the regulations on the protection of monuments”. It also urged residents not to spread “scandalous narratives” about the decision leading to an “open-air museum, the impossibility of renovation, and the blocking of investments”. It said other villages in Lower Silesia were subject to similar protections without hindering their development. Gazeta Wyborcza cited some residents saying that the launch of proceedings in January had already forced them to pause work on their properties. Others complained that the decision will increase renovation costs due to strict conservation requirements. The Opole Provincial Conservator of Monuments said that, as of 2021, some 86 villages across Poland had been added to the register of monuments because of their historic layouts. World.title: Poland enters race to host EU-backed AI gigafactory

Poland has joined the European Union’s plan to build artificial intelligence (AI) gigafactories with a view to hosting one of the bloc’s new computing centres. Deputy digital affairs minister Dariusz Standerski said Poland had completed a key legal step by joining the joint procurement process. The move enables Poland to bid for one of seven AI gigafactory projects planned under the EU programme, potentially attracting investment of more than 10 billion zloty (€2.3 billion) while giving businesses, researchers and public institutions access to advanced AI computing capacity. “On behalf of the Republic of Poland, I have signed the Joint Procurement Agreement, which means that Poland joins the AI gigafactory initiative,” Standerski told daily Rzeczpospolita. Under the proposed model, AI gigafactories will be designed, financed, built and operated by private consortia selected through a European tender organised by the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU). In the first procurement round, EuroHPC JU plans to select seven projects comprising four medium-scale facilities and three large-scale sites. Poland is bidding for a medium-scale project, which would initially provide computing capacity equivalent to at least 25,000 AI accelerators before expanding to at least 75,000. The EU and its member states will support the projects by committing to purchase computing services during the initial years of operation, providing demand certainty for investors. “Poland and the EU will each buy 17% of the power, and the remaining two thirds will be made commercially available by a private consortium; Poland will commit to purchasing its own pool for five years,” Standerski said. Standerski also told the newspaper that companies’ interest in the project is “enormous”. “This means that, from the very first day the gigafactory is operational, part of its computing capacity will already have been sold,” he added. Poland’s government will spend 1.9 billion zloty (€437 million) equipping the majority of schools with so-called AI labs before the start of the next school year. The money will fund laptops, AI software and interactive displays, among other equipment https://t.co/outNQIGCv0 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 19, 2026 Standerski said the government would not designate a site for the facility, with the final location to be determined by the winning consortium through the European procurement process. He said the government had previously identified 10 locations across Poland capable of hosting. Last week, the deputy minister also said Poland was preparing to sign an agreement with the Czech government, under which cooperation would involve mutual purchases of computing capacity between the two countries. He also said Lithuania had committed to a one-sided arrangement to buy computing power from a Polish AI gigafactory. Częstochowa will become the first city in Poland to use the Polish Large Language Model to support the use of AI in providing municipal services. It will help write letters, analyse inquiries from residents, and summarise long documents https://t.co/SLrmVg9VBz — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 11, 2025 Earlier this month, Poland’s government approved a resolution enabling the country to participate in the European AI Gigafactory programme, committing more than 400 million zloty towards what the government says would be the largest computing centre in the country’s history. The government also pledged to purchase AI services worth €100 million between 2028 and 2033, with a matching contribution from the European Union. According to the government’s timetable, the European procurement process is expected to begin later this year. Bidding consortia will have 15 weeks to submit proposals, contracts are due to be awarded in early 2027 and the facilities are scheduled to become operational in 2028. 🚀 Droga do Gigafabryki AI otwarta. World.title: Poland asks US to extradite former minister Ziobro over criminal charges
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has formally asked the United States to detain and extradite former justice minister Zbigniew Ziobro, who is wanted on multiple criminal charges. Ziobro, a senior figure in the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, is accused of offences including leading an organised criminal group and abuse of office. Having previously fled Poland to Hungary, where Viktor Orbán’s government, an ally of PiS, granted him asylum, Ziobro arrived in the United States in May following a change of government in Budapest. Wniosek o ekstradycję podejrzanego Zbigniewa Ziobro: ⬇️https://t.co/YC7T3RrIEc — Prokuratura (@PK_GOV_PL) July 27, 2026 Ziobro served as justice minister in the PiS government from 2015 to 2023. Last year, prosecutors announced that they wanted to charge him with 26 crimes, including leading a criminal group and approving the unlawful purchase of Pegasus spyware. In October, parliament approved the lifting of Ziobro’s immunity from prosecution. By then, however, he had already travelled to Hungary, and in December he was granted political asylum by the Hungarian government. In February this year, Warsaw’s district court approved a request from prosecutors to place Ziobro in pretrial detention. That decision was needed in order for the authorities to issue domestic and European arrest warrants against the suspect. However, Ziobro’s lawyers appealed against the decision. While that appeal was waiting to be heard, Orbán lost power in Hungary and, as his successor Péter Magyar was being sworn in, Ziobro left the country and flew to the United States. In July, a Warsaw court rejected Ziobro’s appeal, opening the way for Poland to seek the politician’s extradition from the US. Ziobro has no valid travel documents after Poland cancelled his passports and Budapest revoked his refugee status. The extradition request covers 19 of the 26 offences listed in the indictment, the prosecutors said. The documents submitted include the final order for Ziobro’s detention, the indictment, a wanted notice and evidence supporting the case. The request will now be sent through diplomatic channels to the US Department of Justice, where it will be assessed to determine whether it meets the formal requirements of the Polish-US extradition treaty, prosecutor Anna Adamiak said. If the request satisfies those requirements, it will be referred to a US federal court, where a judge will decide on the legal admissibility of Ziobro’s extradition to Poland. A court has upheld a request by prosecutors to bring former justice minister Zbigniew Ziobro, who is wanted on 26 criminal charges, into detention. The decision paves the way for Poland to request Ziobro's extradition from the US, where he fled in May https://t.co/vIPRjvgQnA — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 2, 2026 Asked how long the extradition process could take, Adamiak said previous cases suggested proceedings could last anywhere from a few months to several years, depending on their nature and complexity. Adamiak noted, however, that the extradition proceedings would not determine Ziobro’s guilt. “Its role is merely to assess whether the surrender of that person in extradition proceedings is legally permissible in light of treaty regulations and domestic law,” she told reporters, quoted by online news service Wirtualna Polska. “However, the decision on surrender is, of course, a decision made by the state, so other circumstances may also play a role,” she added. PiS, Poland’s largest opposition party, enjoys close ties with US President Donald Trump’s administration. Poland's conservative opposition enthusiastically welcomed Trump's return to the White House, but it is becoming increasingly difficult for them to maintain a tough anti-Russian line while also showing allegiance to the US president, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/4PW6H9nMEF — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 7, 2025 Asked at a news conference about the likelihood of Ziobro’s extradition and when it might take place, Poland’s Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the question should be directed at “the other Donald”, reported the Polish Press Agency (PAP). “We will, in accordance with the law, seek all available means to ensure that these politicians, against whom such serious charges have been brought, appear before a Polish court sooner or later,” he added. “We are waiting for positive signals from Washington. Will they come? I don’t know.” Ziobro has long denied all accusations, saying the case against him is an act of “political revenge” by Tusk’s government. Commenting on the extradition request on the conservative television channel Republika, Ziobro said he was pleased that the case would be heard “in the United States, on American soil, and before an American court”. He claimed that the proceedings would show that the Polish government “regularly breaks the law, ignores procedures, rejects democratic principles, has taken control of the prosecutor’s office unlawfully, and is trying to destroy the opposition”. UNESCO has added the modernist city centre of the Polish port city of Gdynia to its World Heritage List, recognising its interwar urban planning and architecture. The designation, approved during the World Heritage Committee’s 48th session in Busan, South Korea, is Poland’s 18th World Heritage site and comes as Gdynia marks the centenary of gaining city rights. In its justification, UNESCO referred to “an urban organism that harnesses a building-block-based planning approach to develop a characteristic, compact complex of modernist architecture, with robust individual architectural expressions”. Gdynia’s city centre “illustrates a critical break with historicism in the progression of turning the village of Gdynia into a new major sea gateway of the first Polish Republic between the First and Second World Wars”, it added. Granted city status in 1926, Gdynia was rapidly developed by the newly independent Polish state from a small fishing village into a major Baltic seaport, growing to more than 100,000 residents in under 20 years and providing Poland with a modern maritime gateway. It is now Poland’s 13th largest city by population, with just under 210,000 residents, and the third largest by area when including its maritime territory. Nowy tydzień zaczynamy od dobrych wieści! Komitet Światowego Dziedzictwa UNESCO oficjalnie uznał modernistyczne centrum Gdyni za dobro o wyjątkowym znaczeniu dla całego świata. Nie ma lepszego momentu niż 100-lecie Gdyni na to wyjątkowe wyróżnienie!https://t.co/L3WZZCJCAz — Gdynia (@MiastoGdynia) July 27, 2026 Oktawia Gorzeńska, Gdynia’s deputy mayor, who represented the city in Busan, celebrated the decision of the committee as “a wonderful gift for our anniversary and a tribute to the vision and determination of the people who created one of Europe’s great modernist cities”. The city’s mayor, Aleksandra Kosiorek, added that the decision “confirms that the vision which launched the history of modern Gdynia over a century ago has retained its power and universal significance.” Gdynia’s central district of Śródmieście was built largely between 1926 and 1939. Its rapid development at the time drew international attention, with a National Geographic reporter writing that “Poland dreams of building her New York”. Unlike Warsaw and nearby Gdańsk, it escaped extensive destruction during World War Two, preserving much of its original street layout and interwar architecture. According to the city authorities, UNESCO experts have recognised the Gdynia’s centre as one of the world’s most outstanding examples of early modernism in urban planning. The nomination also highlighted Gdynia’s distinctive model of modernist urban planning, setting it apart from contemporaneous developments such as Germany’s Bauhaus, Berlin’s housing estates, Kaunas in Lithuania and Tel Aviv. Gdynia’s modernist architecture is characterised by white façades and maritime-inspired details, including round windows and building forms resembling ship hulls. Gdańsk in Poland has been named a global City of Literature by @UNESCO. It is now one of only 63 such cities in the world, and the third in Poland to obtain the distinction https://t.co/QdMxlT65V4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 3, 2025 Notable examples include the so-called “bank building”, a modernist tenement block, and the Museum of Emigration, housed in the former Maritime Station, which from the 1930s until 1979 was a transit building from which thousands of Polish emigrants left for their new homelands. According to the city, the road to recognition took over 20 years, beginning in 2007, when the historic urban layout was entered into the regional register of monuments. It was designated a Monument of History in 2015, and Poland submitted the site to UNESCO’s Tentative List in 2019. Two sites in Poland were included in the inaugural World Heritage List in 1978: the Historic Centre of Kraków and the nearby Wieliczka and Bochnia Royal Salt Mines. Gdynia’s inscription is the 18th for Poland overall and the first for a Polish modernist urban complex. The most recent Polish additions before Gdynia were the Krzemionki Prehistoric Striped Flint Mining Region in 2019 and, in 2021, the beech forests in the Bieszczady Mountains.
