World.title: 'Not going to let him get away': Rahul Gandhi targets Amit Shah over police action on NEET protesters; BJP says 'prove it or apologise'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha on Wednesday plunged into bedlam after leader of opposition

blamed home minister

for police's alleged excesses against protesters, including firing, riling up treasury benches as Union minister

demanded that he either furnish proof or apologise.

He also blamed Hindutva organisation RSS for all the ills afflicting the education sector.

Government challenged him to prove his allegation or apologise and declared that they would not let Rahul continue with his speech if he did not authenticate or regret making the charge. "You cannot level a charge to grab a headline and get away with it without providing proof," said Rijiju.

Union minister Jitendra Singh also stressed that police firings are ordered by a magistrate. He also defended

Delhi Police

in his reply, saying it exercised "utmost restraint" in handling protesters' march on July 20, a first such assertion from a senior govt functionary.

"It was made sure that any casualty does not happen," Singh said, refuting the allegations of Congress MP Gaurav Gogoi and other opposition MPs that brutal force was used against protesters.

Rahul ties Shah to police action on protesters

Rahul Gandhi demanded Amit Shah be sacked as home minister and a Supreme Court-monitored probe be ordered into use of "lethal force" against young protesters - raising the stakes in the battle of wits with govt over the police crackdown on students.





He said Shah either directly ordered use of pellet guns, shock batons, lathicharge and tear gas on students, which makes him "culpable of brutalisation" of youngsters, or he did not know what police was doing, which makes him "incompetent". "In either case, he has to go," he said, advising PM Narendra Modi to sack the senior minister.

Rahul alleged students are still being threatened, with face recognition and Bajrang Dal being used to scare them.

"These are our children and govt has no business threatening them or beating them. They have not committed any crime. They should not be punished," he said.

He said demand for Shah's sacking was not proforma, raising possibility of the confrontation of last week resuming after the opposition joined parliamentary proceedings to discuss the public exam bill for two days. "Shah is responsible and we are not going to let him get away with it," he said.

The renewed aggression from Rahul came at a news conference that he addressed after he could not complete his heavily interrupted speech in Lok Sabha following a clash with

BJP

benches over his remarks about Shah.

After brief adjournments over an "unparliamentary" word, BJP blocked him when he directly linked Shah to the police crackdown. While his remarks were expunged, BJP led by Union minister Kiren Rijiju insisted he tell the source of his claim or apologise.

As per Rahul, he was told he would have to apologise if he wanted to complete his speech, but he replied he would never apologise to BJP or RSS.

With Shah's photograph on the big screen at Congress's headquarters, Rahul said, "Every child beaten by police should know that this is the man who is responsible for what happened. He takes orders from PM, but he is the man who thrashed you and humiliated you." He slammed Shah for not coming to LS, saying it shows he is "guilty".

At the same time, Rahul said he is proud of students who protested and "they had the courage that their parents did not have" to stand up to BJP.

Rahul riled BJP by claiming a student told him about three categories of people - "students" who accept they don't know everything; those who think they know everything and pretend to be God, and "andh bhakts" who believe the second category is God.

He alleged Dharmendra Pradhan, who had to resign as education minister due to students' stir, was a symbol while the real mess in the education system was created by the RSS.

World.title: Ahead of dengue vaccine rollout, all 4 strains found in circulation
World.content:
NEW DELHI: As India moves towards introducing a dengue vaccine by next year, the country's first nationwide mapping of dengue virus strains has found all four serotypes circulating simultaneously in eight states and UTs, a development researchers say could influence vaccine strategy as infections with multiple strains are associated with more severe disease.

The pan-India molecular surveillance study, led by ICMR-National Institute of Virology, Pune, analysed 6,889 lab-confirmed dengue samples collected through 45 virus research and diagnostic laboratories (VRDLs) across 25 states and UTs between 2023 and 2025. It found that dengue serotypes - at least two - were co-circulating in each state and UT included in the surveillance, indicating increasing hyperendemicity of the disease in India.

According to the study, all four dengue serotypes (DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3 and DENV-4) were detected simultaneously in Andhra, Gujarat, Haryana, MP, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal. Fifteen other states and UTs had three serotypes in circulation, while two reported circulation of two serotypes.

Researchers found DENV-2 to be the dominant circulating strain, accounting for 51% of infections, followed by DENV-3 (13%), DENV-1 (7%) and DENV-4 (1%).





About 7% of patients were infected with two or more dengue serotypes simultaneously.

The study found patients with concurrent infections were more likely to develop thrombocytopenia, haemorrhagic manifestations and arthralgia than those infected with a single serotype, suggesting that circulation of multiple strains could increase the burden of severe dengue.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The researchers said continuous molecular surveillance is essential to monitor changing dengue virus circulation, improve outbreak prediction and guide vaccine introduction strategies.

They noted that several dengue vaccine candidates are in advanced stages of development and that vaccine efficacy varies against different serotypes, making surveillance critical for immunisation policy.

The study also highlighted regional differences in virus circulation. While DENV-2 predominated across India, DENV-1 accounted for a relatively larger share of infections in Tamil Nadu (29%), Haryana (38%) and Rajasthan (25%). DENV-3 was more frequently detected in Gujarat (30%), TN(29%), UP (29%) and WB (20%).

World.title: Guard's accidental gunshot kills man visiting bank in city
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A 27-year-old customer visiting a Union Bank branch in southwest Delhi's Jaffarpur Kalan to update his Aadhaar card was killed Tuesday after the security guard's gun went off accidentally.

The deceased, Manish Kumar, a farmer, was a resident of Issapur village. He is survived by his elderly parents and five older sisters. Police have arrested the security guard, Vinod Kumar, 53, an ex-serviceman.

Police said the incident took place around 10.30am when Vinod was loading cartridges into his 12-bore double-barrel gun.

The firearm allegedly discharged accidentally, and the bullet struck Manish in the back

Vinod later told police that he reported late for duty Tuesday and by the time he started loading the cartridges, customers and bank employees had already started pouring in.

Vinod private firm staffer, served in Army till 2018

The sound of the gunshot sent customers and the staff into panic. People rushed towards the entrance after hearing the loud bang and found Manish lying in a pool of blood.

Police received a PCR call around 11.06 am alerting them about the incident. The caller informed cops that the guardâs firearm had gone off and a man had been shot and was critical. By the time police reached the spot, Manish had already been rushed to RTR Hospital, where doctors declared him dead.

Cops are also scanning CCTV footage to ascertain the sequence of events

According to police, Vinod, a resident of Majri village in Haryanaâs Jhajjar district, served in the Army before retiring in 2018 and had been working with a private security agency for the past two years. Investigators said he was posted at the bank as part of his security duties. He has two sons â one is pursuing an MD course while the other is studying MBBS.

Police have seized the weapon involved in the incident and sent it for forensic examination. A post-mortem examination of the deceased has been conducted to ascertain the exact cause of death. The report is awaited. Cops are also scanning CCTV footage to ascertain the sequence of events.

A case has been registered under BNS Section 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder).

World.title: No ban on Jagannath movie, artists must enjoy creative liberty, says Supreme Court
World.content:
An SC bench said that if depiction of gods and goddesses is prevented, then movies on the Ramayana and Mahabharata would not be made at all

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Rejecting a plea seeking a ban on release of an animated film on Mahaprabhu Jagannath, Supreme Court on Wednesday said artists must enjoy the liberty of creative expression, with courts not getting in the way of art and creativity.As Jagannath temple committee strongly opposed the release of the animation film, a bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and R Mahadevan said that if depiction of gods and goddesses is prevented, then movies on the Ramayana and Mahabharata would not be made and screened at all. It stressed that people ought to be tolerant of depiction of gods and goddesses."If this is the kind of sensibility, sensitivity...we will pass an order that in respect of Hindu God, Goddess or Mythology, let there be no art form in India! We have Kabir's Ramayana, Valmiki Ramayana, Skanda Ramayana, etc. We have Ramayana in every State. Every person has his own creativity. If we pass such an order, all Ramayana, Mahabharata on television will stop! No art in any form, television, creativity, painting, sculpture of Hindu God or Goddess. .." Supreme Court said.Bench said that when the film was passed by Censor Board then there was no reason for the court to interfere and people should not object to the screening of a film which had been approved by the statutory body."Just because there are two-three sensitive people, can we pass an extreme order that with respect to deity, there shall be no creativity, no literature, no sculpture?...Animated films are for the purpose of children...Earlier, there used to be Yashodhama every night. People used to collect money for it. Artists can't be taken to ransom like this," court said while rejecting the plea of the temple committee."We cannot sit in judgement in the matter of art and creativity," it said.Advocate general of Odisha Pritambar Acharya submitted that Lord Jagannath cannot be depicted as Doraemon and Spiderman. But senior advocate Devadatt Kamat, appearing for the producer, refuted the allegation that the deity had been shown in a derogatory manner and pointed out that committee members had walked out of the special screening of the film.The court thereafter refused to modify its earlier order allowing release of the film.

World.title: Delhi HC declines to stay HPV vaccination drive, seeks Centre’s reply
World.content:
The Delhi High Court on Wednesday (July 29, 2026) refused to stay the Centre’s ongoing Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination drive, saying the material placed before it did not show any immediate harm from the vaccine. At the same time, the court stressed that “half-baked vaccines” should not be administered and that all required protocols must be followed.

A Bench of Chief Justice D.K. Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia said the data submitted by the Centre on the administration of 5.5 million HPV vaccine doses to 14-year-old girls did not indicate any “instant harm” that would justify stopping the vaccination drive.

“Half-baked vaccines should not be administered. We are only to ensure that the necessary protocol is followed,” the court observed.

The court was hearing a public interest litigation (PIL) seeking a review of the decision to introduce the HPV vaccine, raising concerns over its long-term safety, lack of informed consent, and monitoring of adverse events.

Appearing for the Centre, Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma said HPV vaccination is not part of the Universal Immunisation Programme. He told the court that, as of July 25, around 5.5 million doses had been administered, with 120 reports of adverse events. Of these, only 42 involved “slightly aggravated” symptoms, and no deaths had been reported.

Mr. Sharma assured that all protocols were duly followed before introducing HPV vaccines.

The Bench said it would examine the petitioners’ challenge to the introduction of the vaccine but found no reason to stop its administration at this stage. It directed the Centre, the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) and the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) to file separate replies within four weeks.

“The justification to introduce the vaccine is one thing, and we will consider.. So far as your prayer for instantly stopping the administration of the HPV vaccine is concerned, we are not going to stay that for two reasons. The data which is now being given to us suggests that there is no instant harm. There may not be long-term benefit, but there is no instant harm at the moment. Secondly, the apprehension that it is going to be part of the universal immunisation programme, that is not there. So let them file their reply,” the court said.

“As of today, we don’t see any reason why the administration of this vaccine should be stopped,” it added.

The Centre also told the court that the HPV vaccination programme, launched across States and Union Territories on February 28 for 14-year-old girls, is voluntary and that no vaccine is administered without prior informed consent from parents.

The petition, filed by Dr. Sujata Mittal and Jitendra Chouksey, claimed that internationally, “significant safety concerns” have been raised against the ‘Gardasil’ HPV vaccine, and incidents raising questions over the vaccine’s safety have been reported in India as well.

According to the PIL, a 14-year-old girl from Tamil Nadu was administered the HPV vaccine at a Government Hospital in Kanai on March 30, 2026. It was alleged that within three to four days, she developed severe and progressively worsening symptoms, including loss of voice, paralysis-like weakness on one side of her body, inability to walk, and blurred and diminished vision.

The matter is scheduled for the next hearing on October 29.

World.title: Man convicted in terrorism trial over 2022 stabbing of author Salman Rushdie
World.content:
A man was convicted Wednesday (July 29, 2026) of federal terrorism charges in the 2022 stabbing of Salman Rushdie, the author who has faced a decades-old death threat over his novel “The Satanic Verses”.

A jury found Hadi Matar guilty of all the charges against him, including engaging in an act of transnational terrorism.

Matar, 28, is already serving a 25-year New York state prison sentence on an attempted murder conviction in the August 2022 attack on an amphitheatre stage. The federal conviction carries a potential life sentence.

Rushdie, who was about to speak on writers' safety, was slashed 15 times in front of a stunned audience. He was gravely wounded and lost the sight in his right eye.

World.title: OMR residents want foot overbridges to be repaired
World.content:
It took a whole month for Kalaivani to be able to walk after she hurt her leg, while climbing down the stairs on the foot overbridge (FOB) near PTC Quarters on Rajiv Gandhi Salai. "I thought there was a step there, but there was none. That portion of the step had worn out due to constant use," she said.

She is not alone in missing a step or walking on dangerous steps. Many residents of the IT Corridor are complaining that the nearly dozen FOBs are damaged and rusted. R. Ramaswamy, a resident of Sholinganallur said that earlier not many people used the facility to cross the road. “But after the CMRL work began, they have no other go but to utilise it. We have taken up the matter with our MLA," he said.

The steel structure has rusted in many places and the paint is slippery when it rains. "The FOBs do not have any roofing and are open to the sky. The handles therefore are hot to touch in the summer. There is no ramp even at locations where people climb on the steps," said S. Suresh, a resident of Thoraipakkam.

FOMRRA co-founder Harsha Koda said that when the OMR was designed there were some 13-14 FOBs placed all along the road. They were placed at locations where there were zebra crossings also available. "But not many people used them. Over time these FOBs became a place for retail drug sales and homeless accomodation. The only real use was the revenue TNRDC, which manages the road, got from selling signage space," he said.

When Chennai Metrorail started construction, a few FOBs were removed. "We were told that they would integrate the FOBs with the stations and ensure they were well maintained. This remains to be seen. Hopefully they will be installed at high density locations like near schools, colleges and offices," he added.

World.title: Doctors’ associations oppose proposal to appoint IAS officer to head Directorate of Medical Education
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu Government Doctors Association (TNGDA) and Service Doctors and Post Graduates Association (SDPGA) have opposed a proposal to appoint an IAS officer to head the Directorate of Medical Education. Till date, the directorate is headed by a government doctor as per seniority.

In a letter to the Health Secretary, TNGDA’s president A. Srinivasan and general secretary T. Kanagarajan, urged the State government to withdraw the proposal.

The TNGDA said it had learned of a proposal to post an IAS officer as the Commissioner of the Directorate of Medical Education. Expressing shock over the move, the association questioned the need for such a proposal when the Health department had functioned effectively under the existing system for the past four decades.

Such a move, it said, would be counterproductive, as it would seek to compel the cadre to work rather than motivate and encourage them. The association also pointed out that despite shortages and inadequacies in manpower, infrastructure and budget, the cadre continued to work all these years for the welfare of the public. It warned that if the proposal is not dropped, it would be forced to launch direct agitations against the move. TNGDA said it would join hands with all associations to oppose the proposal.

SDPGA pointed out that until 2000, the Health department had only one IAS officer, who served as the Health Secretary. Subsequently, IAS officers were appointed to key administrative positions, including project director of Tamil Nadu State AIDS Control Society. Over the years, they have also come to head the Tamil Nadu Health Systems Project as project director, the National Health Mission, Tamil Nadu as mission director, Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation as managing director and Medical Services Recruitment Board as chairperson. The department has now proposed appointing an administrative cadre officer for the post of Director of Medical Education.

“We strongly condemn this move,” P. Saminathan, president of SDPGA, said. There are already six administrative posts manned by IAS officers, the association said and urged the government to increase the number of posts of doctors in line with the patient load, in accordance with the Indian Public Health Standards recommendations, which will strengthen the Health department.

There has been no proportionate increase in the number of government doctors over the years. In 2000, there were 8,000-odd doctors working in government health facilities, including 13 government medical colleges, government hospitals and primary health centres (PHC). More than two decades later, the number of doctors has increased to about 20,000. During the same period, however, the public healthcare network has expanded significantly to include 36 government medical colleges, nearly 270 government hospitals and more than 2,000 PHCs, Dr. Saminathan said.

World.title: Kerala Tourism to push for driver facilities in star-rating norms for hotels and resorts
World.content:
Kerala Tourism (KT) will take up with the Centre the need to include amenities such as well-maintained washrooms and dormitories in the checklist used by the Union Tourism Ministry to issue star ratings to hotels and resorts, a senior KT official said.

This comes in the wake of a protest by drivers on Friday at a luxury hotel here, seeking properly maintained washrooms for their use.

“At present, dedicated amenities for drivers are not mandatory for hotels and resorts to obtain classification from the Central agency. Rather, the focus is on fulfilling all the mandatory criteria with regard to hosting guests who visit them for accommodation or for food. Despite this, KT and Kerala Travel Mart [KTM] Society attempted to create such infrastructure at hotels and resorts a few years ago. But much more needs to be done,” the official said.

In the absence of such amenities yet to be made part of the classification process, there are two options. One is to construct them in properties where land is available, while the other is for them to tie up with lodges or with budget hotels nearby, where drivers can stay at affordable rates, he added.

Sources in the Union Tourism Ministry confirmed that they are focussed exclusively on the infrastructure available to maximise the ‘guest experience’ at hotels and resorts. “However, local bodies have the power to insist on restrooms and other infrastructure for drivers since they issue the no-objection certificate [NOC] for such units to commence operations.”

Back in September 2024, the Kerala government had issued an order making it mandatory for tourist accommodation units to provide clean and adequate restroom facilities for tourist taxi drivers, considering the vital role they played in the tourism industry. The order was issued after then Tourism Minister convened a stakeholder meeting to discuss issues faced by drivers of tourist vehicles.

Citing the need to enforce the order, Jackson Varghese, who led a hunger strike in 2019 demanding the rights of online taxi drivers, and who served as State president of the Kerala Online Drivers’ Union, said the Government Order was binding on all four- and five-star accommodation units in Kerala. They ought to provide clean dormitory accommodation and basic infrastructure for drivers who brought or picked up guests. “With many such units not implementing the order, drivers are often forced to use washrooms in nearby shopping malls or eateries. They also have no other option but to sleep inside their cars.”

Over the past 10 years, several drivers have died after sleeping inside their cars with the air conditioning running, he said, citing cases where fuel ran out and drivers were exposed to carbon monoxide and other exhaust fumes. The situation is grave in Alappuzha, where drivers sleep beneath trees or by the roadside, after dropping off their guests who stay in houseboats, he said.

World.title: Workshop to draft action plans for welfare of SHGs begins in Kochi
World.content:
A southern-level workshop as part of the National Supportive Supervision Framework (NSSF) under the Ministry of Rural Development to nurture cluster-level federations began here on Wednesday.

The event was part of drafting new action plans to ensure the social and financial welfare of self-help groups and members of neighbourhood groups. Jui Bhattacharya, national mission manager for the National Mission Management Unit, inaugurated the workshop. The aim is to make each cluster-level federation financially self-sustaining by 2047, she was quoted as saying in a release issued here.

Representatives from Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Puducherry, and Lakshadweep shared their suggestions and participated in group discussions on the occasion.

An action plan to suit the requirements of each State will be prepared after taking into consideration various factors like human resources, financial sustainability, and benefits for the members, according to the release.

World.title: CJP protest | Fresh reports of detentions, takedown of social media posts emerge
World.content:
The fallout from last week’s nationwide protests demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan continues, amid multiple reports of people, including minors, being detained or arrested by the police, and social media users being asked to take down posts related to the demonstrations.

A 21-year-old man, who was detained by the police in Uttar Pradesh’s Prayagraj after being identified from a photograph taken while he was participating in a protest on July 26, was released on Wednesday (July 29, 2026).

The victim, who did not wish to be identified, said that he was beaten up in police custody and the police wrongly accused him of vandalising a private vehicle, which belonged to a Bharatiya Janata Party member.

“They first called my father to the police station and then my mother. It was then that I went and surrendered myself to the police. I was merely there to protest, I was not involved in any vandalism, yet I was kept in detention for more than a day,” the victim said.

The Prayagraj Police had registered three First Information Reports (FIRs) at the Civil Lines police station on July 26 and July 27 in connection with the alleged vandalism of vehicles. The complainant in two cases are from he BJP, while in the third case, the son of a former BJP MP.

When contacted, a police official who answered the phone of Manish Kumar Shandilya, Deputy Commissioner of Police, Prayagraj City, said: “Nobody has been detained. People had been called for questioning based on CCTV footage, but they were released.”

Ten others were arrested in the case.

Rishav Ranjan of Congress party’s legal cell said that a 17-year-old boy from Bhagalpur in Bihar, who participated in a protest on July 25 was detained by the police from his home around 3.45 a.m. on July 26. The juvenile was among 40 others who were detained or arrested by the Bhagalpur Police after the protests turned violent.

Atulesh Jha, Superintendent of Police, Bhagalpur City said the juvenile was produced before the juvenile justice board and the family was aware of his whereabouts. “As per the assurance given by the Bihar government, the case pertaining to the violence during the (students) protest is being withdrawn and all the people who were arrested are being released. We have written to the JJ Board informing them about the withdrawal of the case and he will be released,” Mr. Jha.

The officer added that the police were also withdrawing photographs of 155 people, including boys and girls, that had been released on the basis of CCTV footage and showed individuals allegedly involved in violence during the protest.

Several Instagram users claimed that the videos related to the July 20 protests were being taken down. Akshay Chandra Madhav, an Instagram user said that several videos related to the “violence and brutality” posted by him were deleted by the platform.

On July 25, the Cockroach Janta Party called off its 36-day stir after the Centre agreed to its three main demands — ouster of Dharmendra Pradhan as the Union Education Minister, compensation for the families of those who ended their lives after the cancellation of NEET on May 3, and withdrawal of FIRs against the protesters and an assurance that no future action would be taken against them. The CJP had said that the agitation will resume if the “harassment of students at the hands of the police” continued.

World.title: Bangladeshi national arrested in Kozhikode over illegal stay
World.content:
​The Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) arrested a Bangladeshi national, identified as Muhammad Hassan, from Mavoor here on Wednesday.

Police sources said Hassan was apprehended during an inspection at a rented house following a tip-off.

​During the search, the ATS team recovered his Bangladeshi identity documents and currency. Hassan and his friend had moved into the house just a day earlier. On seeing the ATS team, the person accompanying him reportedly fled the scene. ​The police have intensified search for him.

The ATS also received information that another friend of Hassan was staying in the same house, and efforts are on to trace him as well.

Meanwhile, Hassan was shifted to the Mavoor police station, and a case will be registered against him under the Immigration and Foreigners Act.

World.title: ‘Bhadohi to be renamed Sant Ravidas Nagar again’: Yogi Adityanath at Varanasi event
World.content:
Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and others pay tributes at the statue of Sant Ravidas at Seer Govardhan village in Varanasi on Wednesday. PTI

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday announced to rename Bhadohi district as Sant Ravidas Nagar on the occasion of the 650th birth anniversary of Sant Ravidas.

The district was renamed as Sant Ravidas Nagar by the then CM Mayawati during her 2007-2012 tenure while her successor Akhilesh Yadav reverted the decision by retaining the old name Bhadohi during the Samajwadi government’s term.

Addressing an event organised by BJP at Seer Govardhan in Varanasi, the birthplace of Ravidas, the Chief Minister said the park where the programme was held will also be dedicated to Ravidas. In accordance with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision, the airport in Jalandhar has been named after the saint, he added.

World.title: Ram Temple Trust seized cash from donation ‘theft’ accused before police filed FIR, reveals Champat Rai’s letter
World.content:
The recovery of cash allegedly stolen from the Ram Temple’s donation boxes was made by the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust from the accused even before the FIR in the matter was registered by Ayodhya police, sources said, citing a letter by the then Trust general secretary Champat Rai.



In the letter, Rai claimed seizure of cash before the matter came into public domain, distancing himself from the Trust’s responsibilities pending an inquiry after the controversy over the alleged theft of donations erupted, they added.

According to the Ayodhya police, cash to the tune of nearly Rs 80 lakh has been recovered from the accused.

World.title: Amid Opposition protest, Rajya Sabha passes Bill criminalising insult to Vande Mataram
World.content:
The Rajya Sabha on Wednesday passed a Bill that criminalises intentional disruption or prevention of the singing of the national song, Vande Mataram, thereby according it legal sanctity at par with the national anthem, Jana Gana Mana.

The Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, seeks to amend a 1971 law by the same name, which makes insults towards the national anthem, national flag and the Constitution a criminal offence.

The Bill was passed through a voice vote following a walkout by nearly all opposition members. When the upper House proceedings resumed at 2pm, Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman Harivansh invited members to begin a discussion on the Bill.

However, opposition members protested and raised slogans, demanding Home Minister Amit Shah’s statement on the recent Delhi Police action against students and youngsters who were protesting against paper leaks at Jantar Mantar.

The Bill states that intentionally preventing the singing of the national song or causing disturbance to any assembly engaged in its singing will be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or fine, or both. Minister of State for Home Affairs Nityanand Rai had introduced the Bill for consideration in the upper House on July 24.

Replying to a discussion on the Bill, Nityanand Rai said he could not understand why some members, and especially the Congress party, have a problem with the Bill. “This is not just an amendment but our commitment towards national awareness, cultural heritage and the values of our freedom struggle,” he said.

The Union minister said that when Bankim Chandra Chatterjee composed the national song in 1875, he had said that one day it will be on every Indian’s lips “as a mantra”. Rai claimed that as Congress President, Jawaharlal Nehru limited the national song to only two stanzas in 1937. He went on to add that in 1938, Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, as the Congress president, had urged Timir Baran Bhattacharya to compose the full version of the song.



“On 24th January, 1950, Dr Rajendra Prasad said in the Constituent Assembly that Vande Mataram should be honoured on par with Jana Gana Mana,” Rai said. “Opposing this (Bill) only means that the Congress wants to adopt appeasement and wants to insult our national pride… the country’s youth, workers, and women will not support this,” Rai added.

Earlier, when the Bill was taken up for discussion, there was uproar in the House. Congress’ Ranjit Ranjan was slated to begin the discussion, but as the MP joined her colleagues in protests seeking the Home Minister’s presence, Deputy Chairman Harivansh said the member was not interested in speaking (on the Bill).

BJP’s Radha Mohan Das Agrawal, who was given the next opportunity to speak, said that the national song has been insulted for the last 123 years, and added that not just today’s Congress party but even the one during the freedom struggle repeatedly insulted the song.

Among opposition members, Deputy Leader of the Opposition Pramod Tiwari, Sagarika Ghose and Tiruchi Siva sought to demand Amit Shah’s presence, but the Deputy Chairman did not allow them to speak on any issue other than the Bill.



Manoj Kumar Jha of Rashtriya Janata Dal said, “I am witnessing for the first time that our national song and national anthem are being pitted against each other. Reverence cannot be legislated.” Biju Janata Dal’s Sulata Deo said none of the members of the House can sing the national song correctly and urged that it should be played in all state assemblies as well as in Parliament.

Aam Aadmi Party’s Sanjay Singh said that while his party supports the Bill, there should also be a Bill against those who insult the National Anthem and the Tricolour.

World.title: Delhi Confidential: Kiren Rijiju guest Appearance
World.content:
An unexpected guest dropped in on Wednesday at Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi’s office in Parliament – Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Kiren Rijiju. Sources in Rahul’s office said Rijiju stayed for around five minutes, taking Rahul and his staff by surprise. While sources refused to reveal anything related to the discussion between Rahul and Rijiju, the meeting came amid a logjam between the government and the Opposition. Rahul could not complete his speech in the Lok Sabha as the treasury benches demanded an apology from him for remarks against Union Home Minister Amit Shah over July 20 police action on students protesting at Jantar Mantar.



Chair Debut

Former senior Trinamool Congress leader Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar on Wednesday made her debut as Chairperson of the Lok Sabha for the first time since she and 19 other MPs of Mamata Banerjee-led TMC merged with the NCPI. Dastidar, among 10 members empanelled to run House proceedings when neither the Speaker nor the Deputy Speaker are available, occupied the Chair following the resumption of proceedings at 2 pm during debate on the anti-paper leak Bill. However, just a few seconds on the Chair, she announced another adjournment, this time for an hour. The Bill was eventually passed by voice vote a little after 3 pm when Speaker Om Birla was present..

Idea Exchange

Newly appointed Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar has asked all unit heads to identify at least one meaningful improvement each month under the “Idea of the month” initiative. At the monthly crime review meeting, the officers will have to exchange with each other the steps taken under the initiative.

World.title: Karnataka HC slams Civil Judge involved in road rage incident, halts probe against 2
World.content:
The bench in its order also directed the Registrar to place the interim order passed before the Chief Justice of the High Court for further action against Gayatri.

The Karnataka High Court on Wednesday came down heavily on a Principal Civil Judge who indulged in a squabble with two persons riding a two-wheeler and got the police to take criminal action against them. The High Court also stayed further investigation in the case.

Justice M Nagaprasanna saw the CCTV camera footage, showing Principal Civil Judge and JMFC, Gayatri, getting into a verbal spat with petitioners Vinya K M and V Kavita. “The video would clearly indicate that the judicial officer has behaved in a manner totally unbecoming of the office that she holds,” the court said.

The bench said: “Judicial office is a continuation of public trust, it is not only inside the courtroom, but it is behaviour outside the courtroom that would erode the confidence of the public or sustain the confidence. Every act of a judicial officer is discharge of official duties and is not confined to the four walls of the court hall but travels beyond the court hall when the interaction happens with the public.”

World.title: Rajasthan youth’s death in ‘accident’:  Why was UPSC aspirant found walking naked on road before his death, asks Gujarat HC, seeks report from govt
World.content:
THE GUJARAT High Court (HC) has directed the state government to file a further investigation report into the circumstances under which a 23-year-old UPSC aspirant had been seen walking naked on a road shortly before his death, observing that the issue requires closer scrutiny before it proceeds with hearing his family’s plea for a CBI investigation.

Hearing a petition filed by the man’s father, Justice M R Mengdey of the Gujarat HC on Tuesday accepted the state’s request to grant time to the investigating officer to submit an additional report specifically addressing the circumstances in which the man had been found roaming naked on a road on March 3, 2025. His dead body was recovered on March 9 on an overbridge on the Rajkot-Ahmedabad highway and an FIR registered at the local police station on an accidental death.

Justice Mengdey orally asked the Public Prosecutor to explain if there was any animosity between the deceased and the accused, why the deceased and his father had visited the house of the suspects and what transpired during the visit as well as a detailed investigation into the circumstances that led to CCTV footage that showed the man naked on the streets.



In an oral order, the court said, “At the request of learned Public Prosecutor to enable the Investigating Officer to submit further report on the aspect of the circumstances under which the man got naked and was roaming on the road …, (stand over) 25.08.2026.”

The Gujarat HC is hearing a petition filed by the man’s seeking to transfer investigation in the FIR lodged on March 9, 2025 under Sections of Bharatiya Nyay Sanhita for 106(1) (causing death by negligence), 125 (endangering life or personal safety of others), 281 (rash driving or riding on a public way) as well as the Motor Vehicle Act. As per the petition before the HC, the father of the deceased has “raised doubt that his son was murdered” as he was missing since March 2. The petitioner had approached the police giving details of the incident on March 5.



The petition alleges that a former MLA and his son were involved in the matter and accuses the local police of protecting them. The family has sought transfer of the investigation to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).

According to the petitioner, the UPSC aspirant went missing on March 2, 2025, after allegedly being assaulted at the residence of one of the accused. He had left home wearing a grey T-shirt and blue trousers. The family contends that CCTV footage later showed him walking naked on the Rajkot-Ahmedabad highway. Later, in another CCTV clip, he was seen wearing different clothes, while the clothes he had originally worn were never recovered.

The petition also questions how he could have travelled nearly 52 km overnight without carrying his mobile phone, alleges that several vehicles were seen following him while he was naked and claims the injuries recorded during the post-mortem examination are “inconsistent with a road accident”.



The state has previously informed the HC in December 2025 that an investigation had been conducted on the technical aspects of the case, including a Call Detail Record (CDR) and narco analysis as well as statements of witnesses in the three cases – a missing complaint filed by the man’s family, a complaint submitted to the police station regarding the suspicion against 11 persons, including the former MLA’s son, as well as a complaint of culpable homicide not amounting to murder against the driver of the luxury bus by which the man is alleged to have been run over.

The state also informed the court that a narco test was conducted on the former MLA’s son on December 11 last year, following permission received from the Rajkot court, with a set of 31 questions and the result of the narco test “was not in favour of the prosecution”.

World.title: Para Athletics: Dilip Gavit, Basil ensure top two podium finish for India
World.content:
Dilip Mahadu Gavit and Mohammed Basil finished at the top two positions in the men’s 100m T47 category to win gold and silver medals for India at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

It was a stunning run from Gavit in the Lane 7 as he accelerated massively in the last 30m to clock 10.71s while his counterpart Basil clocked 10.83s to finish in the second spot.



This is the second time India has done a podium double in Para Athletics after the gold and bronze medal of Sharmila Dhanker and Shilpa in the women’s shot put F57.

Gavit, the 23-year-old from Nashik, Maharashtra, is an Asian Para Games medallist from the 2022 edition where he won a gold medal in the men’s 400m T47.

World.title: AAP attacks BJP over Laxmi Yojana, says govt wants to exclude most women in Capital
World.content:
The AAP on Wednesday attacked the BJP-led Delhi government’s monthly financial assistance scheme for women, alleging that the eligibility criteria have been laid out in a way that would exclude most women in the Capital.

Hitting out at the government which announced that women with three children are not eligible, AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal said it was confusing for the Hindus as RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat has asked them to have many children.

“Mohan Bhagwat is saying that every Hindu should have as many children as possible and Rekha Gupta is saying that if you have more than three children, you will not get the benefit under the Delhi Lakshmi Yojna,” read a post by Kejriwal on X.

World.title: Pakistan welcomes Kuwait's recent ratification of 2023 pact to expand defence cooperation
World.content:
Pakistan has welcomed Kuwait’s ratification of a 2023 defence cooperation agreement between the two countries, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Wednesday.

In a statement responding to media queries, FO spokesperson Dr Tahir Andrabi said the agreement marked “another important milestone in the longstanding defence partnership between the two brotherly countries, dating back to the early 1980s”.

“It also reflects the shared resolve of both sides to further strengthen bilateral defence cooperation and elevate their security partnership,” Andrabi was quoted as saying.

The statement added that the pact provides a comprehensive institutional framework to broaden defence cooperation, encompassing military training, joint exercises, exchanges of expertise and “other mutually agreed areas of collaboration”.

“It will further enhance institutional linkages between the armed forces of both countries and consolidate the longstanding defence ties between Pakistan and Kuwait,” the statement read.

The FO added that Pakistan and Kuwait would continue to work closely to implement the pact in accordance with its provisions, thereby “expanding bilateral defence collaboration, strengthening their enduring defence partnership underpinned by mutual trust, shared interests, and close institutional cooperation and contributing to regional peace, security and stability”.

The statement came as Kuwait’s Foreign Minister Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah concluded his visit to Pakistan.

During his visit, the Kuwaiti FM held separate meetings with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Deputy Prime Minister and FM Ishaq Dar.

In a statement on Dar’s meeting with the Al-Sabah, the FO said the deputy premier noted the defence cooperation agreement between their countries would further strengthen institutional links between both nations’ militaries.

The pact was signed on June 11, 2023 at Kuwait’s Ministry of Defence by then-ambassador Malik Muhammad Farooq on behalf of Pakistan, and Brigadier General Fawaz Khudair Muhammad Al-Harbi, the ministry’s joint planning director, from the Kuwaiti side, according to the FO.

World.title: Govt increases diesel price by Rs2.24, decreases petrol's by 75 paisas
World.content:
The government on Wednesday increased the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.24 per litre, while reducing that of petrol by a meagre 75 paisas.

Following the revision, HSD will retail at Rs390.62 per litre, while petrol will cost Rs335.06 per litre. The Petroleum Division’s notification said the new prices would be applicable for July 30 (Thursday).

The diesel price has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan this week.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: CDF Munir, Kuwait FM discuss regional security and steps to boost bilateral cooperation
World.content:
Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and the visiting foreign minister of Kuwait discussed regional security and steps to boost bilateral cooperation on Wednesday, the military’s media wing said.

Kuwait’s Foreign Minister Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah, who landed in Pakistan last night on an official visit, called on the field marshal at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi, according to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR).

“During the meeting, matters of mutual interest, regional security and steps to further strengthen bilateral cooperation were discussed,” the statement issued by the ISPR on social media said.

It added that CDF Munir reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to Kuwait, emphasising that both countries shared a “common vision for regional peace and prosperity”.

Meanwhile, Al-Sabah appreciated Pakistan’s “steadfast support”, its constructive contribution toward regional peace and stability, and the deep fraternal ties between the two nations, the statement said.

Earlier in the day, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met with the visiting FM and expressed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening cooperation with Kuwait in diverse sectors, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said.

According to a statement issued by the PMO, the visiting minister was warmly welcomed by the premier.

The meeting was also attended by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, along with the federal ministers for defence, commerce, national food security and research, communications, maritime affairs, and petroleum. The adviser to the prime minister and senior government officials were also present.

“The prime minister expressed satisfaction over the positive trajectory of ties and reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening cooperation with Kuwait in diverse fields, including trade, investment, energy, agriculture, information technology, maritime affairs, and human resource development,” the statement said.

The two leaders exchanged views on the regional situation, with PM Shehbaz reaffirming Pakistan’s solidarity with the leadership and people of Kuwait. He strongly condemned the attacks on Kuwait and other Gulf countries during the ongoing Middle East conflict, the PMO added.

He stated that Pakistan was playing its part as an “honest and sincere mediator and facilitator” in the regional peace efforts, thanking the Kuwaiti leadership for its support.

Al-Sabah in turn reaffirmed Kuwait’s commitment to further enhancing bilateral cooperation across areas of mutual benefit, the statement said.

He appreciated the “valuable contributions” of Pakistan — particularly by PM Shehbaz, DPM Dar, and CDF Munir — in “advancing dialogue and diplomacy to resolve the current crisis and restore peace to the region”, it added.

According to the PMO, the two sides stressed the importance of “continued consultation and coordination” on issues of mutual interest and agreed to exchange delegations in the near future to carry these discussions forward.

“In this regard, the prime minister reiterated his invitation to His Highness the Crown Prince of Kuwait to undertake an official visit to Pakistan at a mutually convenient time,” it added.

Regional situation discussed in meeting with Dar

DPM Dar also held a separate meeting with Kuwait’s foreign minister, with the situation in the Middle East coming under discussion.

According to the Foreign Office (FO), the two held a “warm and productive” tête-à-tête at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

“The two leaders reviewed the full spectrum of Pakistan–Kuwait bilateral relations and reaffirmed their shared commitment to further strengthening the longstanding brotherly partnership,” it said.

“They also held in-depth discussions on regional and international developments, with particular focus on the evolving situation in the Middle East,” it added.

Later, the two leaders co-chaired delegation-level talks, the FO posted on X, adding that both sides reviewed the entire spectrum of Pakistan-Kuwait bilateral relations and discussed ways to further strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, energy, labour, agriculture, information technology, health, mining and minerals, defence and the broader economic partnership.

“They agreed to further institutionalise bilateral cooperation through enhanced institutional linkages and regular high-level exchanges,” the FO said.

It added that the two sides also “reaffirmed their commitment to close coordination and cooperation at multilateral forums on issues of mutual interest”.

According to the FO, the Kuwaiti FM thanked the government and people of Pakistan for the “warm welcome and gracious hospitality extended to him and his delegation”.

“He also expressed appreciation for Pakistan’s support to Kuwait during the Covid-19 pandemic,” during which Pakistan had signed an agreement to send hundreds of medical workers to the Gulf country at its request.

The FO further said that DPM Dar reaffirmed “Pakistan’s deep commitment to its longstanding brotherly relations with Kuwait and underscored Pakistan’s desire to further expand the mutually beneficial partnership across all areas of cooperation”.

“The two sides also exchanged views on regional and international developments of mutual interest, including the situation in the Middle East and Palestine. The Kuwaiti foreign minister also appreciated Pakistan’s constructive role in promoting regional peace and stability,” it said.

The visiting dignitary departed Islamabad following the successful conclusion of his official visit to Pakistan. He was seen off at Islamabad International Airport by Additional Secretary (Middle East) Zahid Hussain, according to the FO.

He had arrived in Islamabad on Tuesday at the invitation of Deputy PM Dar. The FO said that upon arrival at the Islamabad International Airport, he was received by Zahid Hussain, additional secretary at the foreign ministry.

It added that the minister’s visit to Pakistan reflected the longstanding brotherly relations between the two countries, “anchored in shared history, mutual trust and close cooperation”.

Announcing the visit on Monday, the FO said Kuwait’s top diplomat was expected to pay a courtesy call on the leadership of Pakistan.

Pakistan has been negotiating an expanded defence pact with Kuwait in exchange for energy cooperation and investment, the Reuters news agency reported earlier this month, citing five sources with knowledge of the talks.

World.title: 22 villages in Punjab's Multan district partially submerged under floodwaters
World.content:
LAHORE: At least 22 mouzas (villages) in Multan district have been submerged under three to four feet of floodwater from the River Chenab, forcing thousands of residents to move to safer places, while standing crops over large tracts have also been damaged, according to the district administration’s latest flood situation report.

The report compiled by the assistant commissioners, available with Dawn, said the district has 545 mouzas, of which 138 are flood-prone.

It said 22 mouzas have been partially inundated with up to 3-4 feet of water, including four in Multan Saddar, seven in Shujaabad and 11 in Jalalpur Pirwala tehsils.

Residents said the advancing floodwater drove thousands of people to relocate with their cattle to safer areas, while cotton, fodder and other standing crops were submerged, causing substantial agricultural losses.

The district administration said no mouza had been categorised as severely affected and no formal evacuation order had been issued. It added that water levels were receding and the situation was being monitored closely across all four tehsils.

In Multan Saddar, the affected mouzas are Abu Hatta, Vellan, Dhello and Zaman Pur. In Shujaabad, floodwaters have inundated Soman, Pounta, Tahir Pur, Marha, Agar Khawani, Dhundoon and Wanis.

The largest number of affected villages is in Jalalpur Pirwala, where Ripri, Manik Wali, Jung Wala, Narol, Wacha Sandila, Shahpur Lamma, Bait Kaitch Janubi, Shehni Shumali, Shehni Janubi and Bait Qaiser, among others, have been affected.

Civil society activist Majid Zahoor told Dawn that two union councils (UCs) of Tehsil Jalalpur, including Bait Kaitch and UC Sheeni of Jalalpur Pirwala, were submerged.

He said that all zamindara bunds constructed by locals on their own to stop the water from entering their crops and houses were washed away by the water.

Meanwhile, Multan Deputy Commissioner Dr Faisal Saleem said the flood wave in the River Chenab had receded to around 110,000 cusecs, but the district administration would remain on high alert until the river fully returned to normal.

He added that only minor inundation had occurred in a few riverine settlements, while residents living along the Chenab belt had been advised to remain vigilant and follow official instructions.

The DC also urged citizens to rely only on authentic government sources for updates on the flood situation and avoid rumours.

Separately, the Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA) said a low-level flood continued at Kalabagh and Taunsa on Indus River, while water flows in all other major rivers remained within normal limits.

According to the PDMA’s latest river situation report, Indus River recorded an inflow of 262,219 cusecs and an outflow of 253,979 cusecs at Kalabagh, and an inflow of 310,407 cusecs and an outflow of 290,407 cusecs at Taunsa, both remaining at low flood level.

At Tarbela, inflow stood at 246,000 cusecs and outflow at 242,100 cusecs, while Chashma recorded an inflow of 245,382 cusecs and an outflow of 236,582 cusecs, both at normal levels.

Similarly, Chenab River continued to flow within normal limits, with 92,901 cusecs recorded at Marala, 98,403 cusecs at Khanki, 89,017 cusecs at Qadirabad, 110,677 cusecs at Trimmu and 134,622 cusecs at Panjnad.

Jhelum River also remained normal, with 80,000 cusecs recorded at Mangla and 7,491 cusecs at Rasul.

On Ravi River, flows remained normal at Jassar, Shahdara, Balloki and Sidhnai, while Sutlej was also flowing within normal limits at Ganda Singh Wala, Sulemanki and Islam Head.

The PDMA warned that forecast rainfall in the upper catchment areas could increase flows in the eastern rivers and adjoining nullahs, raising the risk of flash floods.

It also cautioned about possible urban flooding in Lahore, Rawalpindi, Gujranwala, Gujrat, Sialkot, Faisalabad and Multan, and landslides in Murree, Galiyat and other hilly areas.

The authority urged people living in riverbeds to move to safer locations and advised the public to avoid unnecessary visits to rivers, canals and rain-fed streams. Flood relief camps were established in vulnerable areas where essential facilities and medicines were being provided.

Showers in Islamabad, parts of Punjab

Parts of Punjab and Islamabad received rain on Wednesday morning, marking the onset of a fresh monsoon spell in the country just as a previous one that caused flooding in several areas of Punjab and over 100 deaths ended.

An update by the Water and Sanitation Agency (Wasa) at 11:30am said the highest amount of rainfall in the city by then was recorded in Tajpura at 44.8 millimetres.

It was followed by 44.4mm of rain in Mughalpura, 32.8 in Shadipura, 31.4 at Pani Wala Talab, 29mm at Chowk Nakhuda, 26.8mm in Johar Town, 26mm in Mannawan, 22.4mm at Lakshmi Chowk, 16.4mm in Farrukhabad, 7.6mm in Saggian, 6.2mm in Nishtar Town and 5.8mm at Upper Mall.

Gulshan-i-Ravi received 1mm of rain while 0.8mm of rainfall was recorded at Jail Road and 0.2mm in Iqbal Town. Trace amounts of rainfall were also recorded at Kahna, Hdyara Defence Road, Samanabad, Airport and the Wasa head office in Gulberg.

Separately, the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) said that several areas of Sialkot, as well Jhelum, Rawalpindi, Islamabad, Narowal, Mangla and Murree also received showers between 2am and 5am.

According to a report by the Met Office, 54mm of rain was recorded in the Sialkot city during this period while Jhelum, Rawalpindi, Islamabad, Narowal, and Murree also received showers.

World.title: HRCP, Amnesty call for 'prompt, independent' probe into Rawalakot unrest
World.content:
The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) and Amnesty International have expressed concern over reports of violence in the Rawalakot area of Azad Jammu and Kashmir’s (AJK) Poonch district, and called on the authorities to probe the incidents.

Clashes took place between protesters and law enforcement personnel in Rawalakot on Monday and Mirpur on Tuesday, which reportedly resulted in several casualties.

The now-proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now.

The government has accused militant elements “pu­r­­s­u­ing a foreign age­nda and backed by Indian funding” of fomenting the unrest. The tensions come as elections are being held across AJK in three division-wise phases .

In a statement published on Tuesday, the HRCP said it was “deeply alarmed” at reports of deaths and injuries in clashes between protesters and law enforcement personnel in AJK’s Rawalakot area on Monday.

“The reported deaths in Rawalakot are a stark reminder of the human cost of the tensions that have gripped AJK in recent weeks,” the HRCP said. “While the authorities have a duty to maintain public order, this must never come at the expense of the right to life or the freedoms of peaceful assembly and expression,” it added.

HRCP urged an end to the “cycle of violence” and called for a “prompt, impartial and independent investigation” into the reports of deaths and injuries. It also called for “anyone responsible for unlawful use of force to be held to account”.

“We also urge the authorities to exercise restraint in responding to protests. As the remaining phases of the elections approach, the focus must shift from confrontation to protecting lives and restoring public confidence,” the statement concluded.

Meanwhile, Amnesty International called on authorities to lift a communications blackout in the region.

The statement, quoting Amnesty International’s Acting Regional Director for South Asia Isabelle Lassee, sought a “prompt, independent, and transparent investigation” into the reported use of force against protesters.

“So long as an internet and mobile services blackout remains in place, it will severely impede the independent verification of the full extent of the situation on the ground. We urge the Pakistani authorities to restore all communications access and allow media and independent observers into the area,” she stated.

Internet services restored in parts of Muzaffarabad

On Wednesday, internet services were restored in parts of Muzaffarabad division after remaining suspended for 54 days, bringing relief to residents who had repeatedly demanded an end to the blanket shutdown imposed on the night of June 5.

It was not immediately clear whether the restoration covered the entire Muzaffarabad division or was limited to the state capital.

The unexpected restoration was greeted with relief by residents.

However, many users complained that cellular data remained painfully slow, similar to the situation in Mirpur, and hoped the authorities would improve the service without further delay.

Amid the suspension of mobile services in several parts of AJK, it has been difficult to obtain information from residents and officials in those areas. Secondary officials have also refrained from commenting on the situation.

The authorities had restored internet services in Mirpur division on July 23, four days before polling in the first phase of the elections.

Although the situation in Muzaffarabad and Mirpur divisions had largely returned to normal, the authorities had continued to withhold internet services in both divisions despite repeated appeals from residents, businesses, students and political leaders.

Over the past month, the regional administration and the JAAC have been at odds over various issues, most notably the committee’s demand to abolish the 12 seats in the region’s Legislative Assembly, which has resulted in protests across the region.

On June 5, following the announcement of the JAAC’s June 9 strike, the AJK government declared the committee a proscribed organisation and placed it under the First Schedule of the region’s anti-terrorism act (ATA).

The next day, AJK authorities launched a crackdown on the JAAC, arresting scores of its leaders and later placing 147 of its activists on the Fourth Schedule of the ATA.

On Tuesday, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said that JAAC were not peaceful but violent, alleging the involvement of militant elements pursuing a foreign agenda and backed by Indian funding.

“Peaceful and transparent elections were held in AJK, with all the mainstream political parties participating fully. The people of Kashmir responded to the call of the election,” he stated, referring to the first phase of elections held in Mirpur division on Monday.

However, he said, the banned outfit could not accept this political activity, nor the peaceful and transparent elections.

Additional input by Tariq Naqash

World.title: Senate panel restricts Islamic banks from compelling female employees to wear abayas
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue on Wednesday restricted Islamic banks from imposing abayas on their female staff, and called for following a modest national dress code for all irrespective of gender.

A meeting of the panel, presided over by Senator Saleem H. Mandviwalla, took up complaints regarding dress code instructions at certain banks, particularly those running Islamic operations.

Senator Dr Zarqa Suharwardy Taimur informed the committee that female employees were allegedly being compelled to wear abayas, although there was no such compulsion for male staff who were free to dress as they chose.

Senator Sherry Rehman argued that no employee should be forced to adopt any specific attire. She remarked that a shalwar kameez, as worn by ex-prime minister Benazir Bhutto, was also sufficient for other women, adding that the state had defined national dress for both genders.

State Bank Pakistan (SBP) Governor Jameel Ahmed said that the panel had also issued similar guidelines last year, which had already been conveyed to all banks.

The committee reiterated that it had only directed observance of a modest dress code and had never mandated any specific attire. It directed all banks to submit their dress code policies and instructed the SBP to circulate updated guidelines to ensure that no employee was subjected to unnecessary compulsion.

Meanwhile, Mandviwalla took exception to the non-implementation of the committee’s instructions for the payment of a budget honorarium to Senate staff. The committee was told that the matter was sub judice.

The payment of special honorariums, equivalent to five months’ salary, to various government and parliamentary employees on account of the annual budget has continued to be the subject of lobbying and political and bureaucratic influence.

Mandviwalla stressed that Parliament had passed a law and no court had the jurisdiction to interfere in such matters.

“Have we ever interfered in judicial matters? Have we ever asked why they are taking so much in salaries? How can they interfere in our domain?” he questioned, emphasising that he wanted payment of salaries to Senate employees.

He asked the finance ministry to return to the Supreme Court and inform it of the law, adding that a notice of privilege motion would be issued if the matter was not resolved within seven days.

Regarding the non-issuance of revised payslips to directors, staff and private secretaries of the Senate Secretariat by Accountant General Pakistan Revenues (AGPR), the committee chairman directed the authorities concerned to resolve the matter within seven days, warning that “failure to comply would result in referral to the Senate Privileges Committee”, a statement said.

Earlier this month, officials from the AGPR briefed the committee on the matter, seeking additional time for implementation. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb and the AGPR officials were non-committal about making the honorarium payments to Senate staff without first obtaining legal opinion.

The committee also reviewed complaints regarding difficulties faced by customers, particularly Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), in dealing with commercial banks.

MNA Muhammad Moin Amir Pirzada informed the committee that despite its earlier directions to designate dedicated officers in banks including the SBP, no uniform standard operating procedures (SOPs) had been developed in this regard.

He said his bank account had been closed in April this year and despite repeated correspondence with the concerned bank and the SBP, no response had been received. He stressed the need for a standardised annual data update mechanism to prevent such incidents.

The SBP governor acknowledged that while regulations governing PEP-related cases already exist, the lapse occurred at the branch level. He informed the committee that a backup officer had been designated and assured members that a dedicated focal person would also be appointed in this regard.

The committee emphasised the need for uniform SOPs across the banking sector, while the finance minister termed standardised procedures “essential” to ensure effective customer service and grievance redressal, according to a statement.

The committee also discussed investment protection policies. Senator Manzoor Ahmed proposed extending the incentives currently available for the Reko Diq project to other investment projects across Pakistan.

Officials of the finance ministry informed the committee that only one project currently qualified under the existing criteria, and that the government’s fiscal position did not permit extending similar concessions. However, the finance minister assured the committee that future proposals would be considered within the available fiscal space.

Discussing taxes collected through electricity bills, Senator Kamil Ali Agha expressed concern over the burden on consumers.

Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) Chairman Muhammad Rashid Langrial informed the committee that approximately Rs476 billion had been collected through electricity bills, including Rs351bn in sales tax and Rs124bn in adjustable withholding income tax. He explained that sales tax on electricity formed part of the country’s overall sales tax regime.

World.title: AJK police accuse JAAC of targeting LEAs, say 26 personnel martyred this year
World.content:
Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Police on Wednesday said that 26 personnel were martyred this year during incidents of unrest as they accused the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) of deliberately targeting law enforcement agencies (LEAs).

Addressing a press conference, AJK police spokesperson and Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Riaz Mughal said that members of the proscribed JAAC were “martyring and injuring rangers and police personnel” in AJK.

“In 2026 only, 26 of our personnel were martyred, while 157 were seriously injured, and 629 faced minor injuries,” he said, without mentioning the specific incidents in which the casualties occurred.

“After this figure, how can you say that they are peaceful protesters?” the SSP asked.

The police spokesperson further said, “Our institutions don’t target anyone. We only target those who target our personnel.”

The police official’s remarks come after clashes between protesters and law enforcement personnel in Rawalakot on Monday and Mirpur on Tuesday, which reportedly resulted in several casualties.

The JAAC, which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now.

“What is happening to police, rangers and other people? They (JAAC members) have held people captive and taken their IDs? Do people not see this?” the SSP said.

The police spokesperson suggested that one should go to AJK and impartially witness the situation and the kind of people who were staging sit-ins there.

“They have snipers. They target people who are from our institutions and police,” he said, stressing how the JAAC supporters could be called peaceful people who did nothing.

SSP Mughal also presented weaponry allegedly recovered from the protesters during different operations. “They use this weapon against law enforcement people.”

He recalled that on May 11, 2024, when the police confronted JAAC protesters who were heading towards Muzaffarabad, adding that the incident resulted in the martyrdom of a police officer and 60 personnel getting seriously injured, most of whom were still recovering. At least 174 policemen also sustained minor injuries, the SSP added.

SSP Mughal went on to note that in October 2025, three cops were martyred on the spot, 52 personnel were seriously injured, and 357 others were also hurt.

The spokesperson emphasised that these were “anti-state” individuals who were carrying out “terrorist activities” under a plan.

Moreover, he claimed that 70 per cent of the protesters were “criminals”, including drug dealers who had taken shelter under the JAAC’s banner.

SSP Mughal emphasised that these were “anti-state” people.

On Tuesday, the government accused militant elements “pursuing a foreign agenda and backed by Indian funding” of fomenting the unrest. On the other hand, the JAAC alleged that dozens of its supporters were killed in clashes with security personnel, but there was no official confirmation of the claim from any quarters.

The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) and Amnesty International have expressed concern over reports of violence in the Rawalakot area and called for an independent probe.

‘JAAC working under an agenda’

Earlier in the day, SSP Khawar Ali Shaukat from AJK Police accused the JAAC of working under an “agenda”, saying that sophisticated weapons had been seized from arrested suspects.

Senior Superintendent of Police Khawar Ali Shaukat addresses a press conference in Rawlakot on Wednesday. — DawnNewsTV

Addressing a press conference, SSP Shaukat alleged that the incidents in Rawalakot had demonstrated that the organisation’s narrative of peaceful protest was inconsistent with events on the ground.

“The violent incidents, acts of provocation and attacks on security forces have made the reality clear,” he said, adding that it was the legal and constitutional responsibility of LEAs to act whenever police or other security personnel came under attack.

The SSP alleged that armed groups had ambushed officials at different locations across the city over the past two days and opened fire on security personnel with sophisticated weapons.

He said one Rangers official was martyred while around 15 police officers and other law enforcement personnel were injured in the attacks.

“This demonstrates that the proscribed group is working under an agenda, the purpose of which is to disrupt peace in AJK, disturb the social fabric and damage the atmosphere of brotherhood,” he said.

“The events of yesterday and today, the way our forces have been attacked with heavy and sophisticated weapons, show that these groups … this is not an ordinary organisation,” he said.

He said law enforcement agencies had arrested several suspects allegedly involved in the violence and recovered a large cache of arms, including heavy weapons.

“An automatic American weapon was also recovered,” he said, adding that this indicated that the banned organisation was operating under a “different agenda”.

Rejecting what he described as a misleading narrative circulating on social media, Shaukat said the group was falsely portraying itself as peaceful while accusing security forces of targeting protesters.

“The facts on the ground are contrary to those claims,” he asserted.

He maintained that law enforcement agencies had exercised restraint throughout the situation and only responded when their personnel came under attack.

World.title: NCCIA summons journalist Asad Ali Toor over allegedly spreading 'false information'
World.content:
The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Wednesday issued a summons notice to journalist Asad Ali Toor for an inquiry into alleged dissemination of false information by him.

The notice, available with Dawn, named the state as the complainant against Toor for “alleged dissemination, transmission and/or public exhibition of false/fake information”. It was issued on a complaint filed under Section 26A (punishment for false and fake information) of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016 (Peca).

The journalist was directed to appear before the NCCIA Cybercrime Reporting Centre in Islamabad at 11am on July 31.

The NCCIA warned that failure to appear “without lawful excuse shall be deemed as your unwillingness to offer any defence, and the inquiry will proceed” in his absence.

It added that non-compliance with the notice would be punishable under Section 174 (non-attendance in obedience to an order from public servant) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC).

Toor, in a post on X, also shared the notice alongside poetry by revolutionary poet Faiz Ahmed Faiz.

“NCCIA has summoned me on this Friday, July 31, 2026 on the complaint of the state,” Toor wrote.

The National Press Club (NPC) in Islamabad condemned the NCCIA notice, expressing alarm at the state of press freedom.

Asserting that the right to freedom of expression was a constitutional right, NPC leadership said, “Subjecting journalists to legal pressure and retaliation for performing their professional duties or expressing critical opinions is not a good omen for any democratic society.”

NPC urged institutions to play their respective roles in accordance with law, constitution and fundamental human rights.

“Free, responsible and safe journalism is the foundation of a strong democratic system,” NPC said, demanding that notice be withdrawn and the “constitutional and legal rights” of journalists be respected.

It warned against steps curtailing freedom of the press and fostering “insecurity among the journalist community”.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.
